## §285 — The gate was bounded before it was built, and the bound was the finding

The previous section's residue was 1.9 points and its next question was a gate over claims. This iteration built the
gate, and the first thing it did was compute what a **perfect** gate could reach. That number, not the arm's score,
is what this section records.

### The ceiling, computed from the artifacts before anything was written

Three counts decide every arm on this population, and all three are arithmetic over the dump:

| Reading                                                      |         Cases |      Share |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------: | ---------: |
| the engine's top-1 is accepted                               | 1 073 / 1 422 |     75.5 % |
| an accepted answer appears anywhere in the width-5 posterior | 1 249 / 1 422 | **87.8 %** |
| not in the width-5 posterior                                 |   173 / 1 422 |     12.2 % |
| **not anywhere in the engine's order**                       | **0 / 1 422** |  **0.0 %** |

The second row bounds **every** reader, whatever it is asked. The third is not a hard case: it is a case the
published five-wide presentation does not show. The fourth is the one that would be fatal — and it is empty. The
ranking-depth report reads `absent 0`, `beyond@20 112`: the engine's complete order holds the answer in **all
1 422 cases**, and every one of the 173 misses is a question of position rather than of generation.

The gate's own bound is a fourth count — `engine correct OR arm correct`, per case:

| Arm under the claim protocol | arm alone | arm-only | engine-only |  **union** |
| ---------------------------- | --------: | -------: | ----------: | ---------: |
| damping, `w = 1.0`           |    60.7 % |       56 |         266 | **79.4 %** |
| damping, `w = 0.5`           |    69.1 % |       56 |         147 | **79.4 %** |
| damping, `w = 0.3`           |    72.0 % |       44 |          93 | **78.6 %** |
| `rrf`, `w = 0.3`             |    73.6 % |       10 |          36 |     76.2 % |

**79.4 % is the most a gate can ever reach here**, because it assumes the gate knows the label — it keeps every case
the arm got right and every case the engine got right, and discards the 266 the arm lost. A real gate is a
classifier over features that do not contain the label, so it lands between 75.5 % and 79.4 %. The 3.9 points above
the engine are the entire prize, and they require separating 56 wins from 266 losses perfectly.

The gap between 87.8 % and 79.4 % — **8.4 points** — is the elimination protocol's price for saying an answer. It is
not a modelling error and no model can recover it: expressing "promote rank 3 to rank 0" costs three eliminations,
each citing a channel printed on both rows and outside the removed row's band, and a case with one discriminating
channel but not three cannot say what it knows.

### The gate, measured, on a split

Nine gate rules over the recorded claims, each scored on a hash split of the corpus so an in-sample winner cannot be
reported as a method. Verified claims: **3 632** over **1 201** cases (the other 221 cases produced no admissible
claim at all).

| Gate                                   | Operator      |        all | in-sample | out-of-sample | Δ vs engine |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------: | --------: | ------------: | ----------: |
| none                                   | damping `w=1` |     60.7 % |    62.6 % |        58.8 % |       −14.8 |
| separation `< 0`                       | damping `w=1` |     68.6 % |    69.4 % |        67.7 % |        −6.9 |
| `margin < 0.05`                        | damping `w=1` |     75.7 % |    76.4 % |        74.9 % |    **+0.2** |
| **`margin < 0.05` ∧ separation `< 0`** | damping `w=1` | **75.7 %** |    76.2 % |        75.3 % |    **+0.3** |
| `margin < 0.05` ∧ separation `< 0`     | `rrf` `w=0.3` |     75.5 % |    75.9 % |        75.0 % |        +0.0 |
| `n ≤ 2` ∧ separation `< 0`             | damping `w=1` |     73.6 % |    74.1 % |        73.2 % |        −1.8 |

The best gate is worth **+0.3 points** and it agrees with the shipped skip rule almost exactly: `margin < 0.05` alone
is +0.2. The two-column split is what makes this readable — every rule that loses in sample also loses out of
sample, and the one that wins in sample wins by the same margin out of sample, so the +0.3 is a measurement rather
than a maximum over nine tries.

**Why no gate does better is a fact about the claims, not about the rules.** Taking each verified claim alone, at
full damping: **66 helped, 280 hurt, 3 286 changed nothing.** Two thirds of the admissible claims are not about the
top of the ranking at all — they eliminate a candidate that was not standing between the engine and the truth — and
the ones that are split 66/280 in favour of harm. There is no threshold on any of these features that separates a
population whose base rate is 19 % correct without also discarding most of the 66.

### One measurement that inverted an assumption

The separation feature was added on the theory that a claim cites a channel which is _more_ anomalous on the removed
candidate than on the kept one, and that a claim with the opposite sign is asserting a preference rather than
comparing evidence. The corpus says otherwise:

| `departure(removed) − departure(kept)` in band widths | claims | the kept service IS the truth |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -----: | ----------------------------: |
| `< −1.0` (kept far more anomalous)                    |    915 |                    **71.0 %** |
| `−1.0 … −0.25`                                        |    343 |                        70.6 % |
| `−0.25 … 0`                                           |    695 |                        46.5 % |
| `0 … 0.25`                                            |    936 |                        48.1 % |
| `≥ 4.0`                                               |    274 |                        58.8 % |

When the kept service is **further** outside the cited band than the removed one, it is the truth 71 % of the time —
14 points above the corpus's own 60 % rate for "the kept service is true". The direction is right and the reason is
the one §284 found: the injected source is usually the most anomalous service in the window, so the candidate whose
evidence is **louder** is the better answer, and a claim that removes the louder one is citing evidence that points
the other way. The feature is real, it is worth +0.3 points in combination with the margin rule, and it is worth
almost nothing alone — which is what a signal about 40 % of the cases looks like when the other 60 % are decided by
how far the engine's own margin already was.

### The posterior's width is a choice, and the dump says what it costs

`depth.ndjson` records the engine's full order, so the recall curve is free:

| depth  |      1 |      2 |      3 |      5 |      8 |         10 |         15 |         20 |
| ------ | -----: | -----: | -----: | -----: | -----: | ---------: | ---------: | ---------: |
| recall | 75.5 % | 83.3 % | 86.3 % | 87.8 % | 88.8 % | **89.9 %** | **91.0 %** | **92.1 %** |

The published five is a **presentation** decision, not a property of the engine: the truth sits at rank 5–19 in a
further 61 cases (4.3 points) and at rank ≥ 20 in another 112 (7.9 points), and the ranking-depth report's `absent`
column is **0**. There is no case on this corpus whose answer the engine failed to generate: every miss is a
position, so the ladder's far end is not a floor but a width.

### What ships, and what it is for

The gate does not ship as a decision path — it is worth +0.3 points and the skip rule already captures +0.2 of them.
What ships is the **second expression protocol** and the instruments that made the 8.4-point gap visible:

- `packages/ai/src/agent/table.ts` — one renderer for the evidence table, so two protocols cannot ask about two
  different tables. The elimination builder now calls it, byte for byte, which is why every digest from §284b still
  replays.
- `packages/ai/src/agent/nomination.ts` — protocol 3: a ranking, partial and possibly empty, verified for existence
  and repetition only. Its refusal families are two, both about the answer rather than the case, because whether a
  ranking is _right_ is what the accuracy measures.
- `benchmarks/src/agentic-protocol-ceiling.ts` — the reader bound, the union bound, and the recall curve, from one
  loop that takes `orderOf(case)` so a claim arm and a nomination arm are scored by the same arithmetic.
- `benchmarks/src/run-agentic-ceiling.ts` — the offline entry point; `benchmark-agentic.yml` runs it after the
  proposal step, because `--claims` is the artifact that step writes.
- `benchmarks/src/agentic-nomination.ts`, `agentic-nomination-study.ts`, `run-agentic-nomination.ts` — the record
  format, the refusal census, the proposal loop, and the grid.

A property found while testing, and kept in the tests as a stated fact: **`borda` degenerates on a partial ranking.**
A first place scores `n − 1` whether it is the engine's or the model's, so nominating the engine's last candidate
adds exactly what the engine's leader already holds and the move vanishes into a tie. `rrf` has no such problem
because its contribution is `1/(k + rank)`, which is strictly greater for a better rank. An operator and a protocol
are chosen together; a sweep that reports both without this sentence is reporting one operator twice.

### Axes this closes

- **"A per-claim gate can recover the residue."** Measured. Ceiling 79.4 %, best rule +0.3 points, and the base rate
  of an admissible claim that helps is 19 %.
- **"The engine's posterior is the limit."** False, and measured: the limit at width 5 is 87.8 % and the engine
  reports 75.5 %, so 12.3 points are inside the posterior the engine already built. Of those, the protocol can
  express 3.9.
- **"`borda` and `rrf` are interchangeable on claims."** False on partial evidence, with the mechanism recorded.

### The next arm, stated before it runs

Protocol 3 has been dispatched for the same 1 422 cases, same model, same table. The pre-registered prediction:

- a nomination arm at `rrf` clears the engine's **75.5 %** on the same cases — the claim protocol's loss was
  expressiveness, and nomination removes that constraint;
- the residual gap to 87.8 % is the model's reading error, and a nomination arm below **80 %** means the reading, not
  the protocol, was the binding constraint all along.

The kill criterion is stated in advance and is the same shape as §284's: **if nomination on 1 422 cases does not
clear 75.5 %, the agentic line retires for good** — the layer would then have failed under both protocols, and the
next axis is the posterior's width (5 → 10, worth +2.1 points of reader) rather than another way of asking.

## §285b — The readback: the protocol was not the problem either, and the measurement itself is not stable

Run `43582526212`, commit `b7b91c87`, `deepseek-chat`, 1 422 cases, both protocols on the same table in one
dispatch. §285's pre-registered prediction was that nomination clears 75.5 % and that a result below 80 % would mean
the reading rather than the protocol was binding. Both halves of that prediction were wrong, and the way they were
wrong is the finding.

### The engine is bit-reproducible; the model is not

The three artifacts `measure` writes were compared by digest against the previous run's:

| Artifact              | md5 (both runs)                    |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `fingerprints.ndjson` | `1bda8c2d7a953fa000d33b7ea6588175` |
| `per-case.ndjson`     | `78279a2168d62340fc7db72768309b62` |
| `depth.ndjson`        | `656c3d0162c3a3c0a751d6730e363441` |

**Identical, byte for byte, across a commit that changed `pruner.ts`.** Everything below is therefore a property of
the model, not of the engine.

### Nomination: the model restates the engine

| Arm                       | `rrf` `w=0.1` | `w=0.3` | `w=0.5` |    `w=1.0` |
| ------------------------- | ------------: | ------: | ------: | ---------: |
| nominate (arm alone)      |        74.6 % |  74.6 % |  74.5 % |     74.5 % |
| **union (engine or arm)** |        75.8 % |  75.9 % |  76.0 % | **76.2 %** |
| arm-only                  |             5 |       6 |       8 |     **10** |
| engine-only               |            17 |      18 |      21 |         24 |

3 941 891 prompt tokens and 24 105 completion tokens bought **ten** cases the engine did not have, and lost
seventeen. The reason is visible in the answers themselves:

| Reading                                                 |         Cases |      Share |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------: | ---------: |
| the model's first service is the engine's first service | 1 238 / 1 422 | **87.1 %** |
| the model's first service is the truth                  | 1 056 / 1 422 |     74.3 % |
| the truth appears anywhere in the model's ranking       | 1 204 / 1 422 |     84.7 % |
| mean ranking length                                     | 2.25 services |          — |

The layer is being asked to improve a ranking and answers by repeating it: 87.1 % of the time its first choice is
the choice it was shown first, and its first choice is the truth _less_ often than the engine's is. Its recall,
84.7 %, is **below the 87.8 % the posterior already contained** — the model discards true answers that were on the
page. Nomination's union ceiling, 76.2 %, is below the elimination protocol's 80.7 % on the same cases, so the
8.4-point expressiveness gap §285 measured is real but is not where the loss is: the loss is that there is nothing
to express.

### The same prompt, the same model, a different answer

This run's elimination arm was measured beside the previous one. The prompt digest replays 1 422 / 1 422 with zero
stale, so the question was identical; the engine artifact is identical by md5; the model name is identical.

| Reading                                                                |           §284b |               §285b |                 Δ |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------: | ------------------: | ----------------: |
| `recorded` arm, damping `w=1`                                          |          60.7 % |          **45.6 %** |             −15.1 |
| claims emitted                                                         |           5 188 |               5 093 |               −95 |
| verified claims                                                        |  3 632 (70.0 %) |  **3 633 (71.3 %)** |              +1.3 |
| union (engine or arm)                                                  |          79.4 % |              80.7 % |              +1.3 |
| arm-only / engine-only                                                 |        56 / 266 |            75 / 499 |                 — |
| `ts-travel-plan-service`, named when it IS the source / when it is not | 76.3 % / 16.4 % | **46.3 % / 28.1 %** | inversion returns |

The preference census — the instrument §284 used to prove the arm had stopped reading a name prior — has **fallen
back to 1.65×**, from 4.7×. The claims are, if anything, more often true (73.0 % verified against 70.0 %) and less
often useful (45.6 % against 60.7 %): the model is citing real evidence and reaching worse conclusions from it.

**This is not a defect in this iteration's code.** It is the same prompt, the same table, the same endpoint name,
and a materially different answer — which makes the arm's contribution, at ±3 points, _smaller than its own
run-to-run variance at 15 points_. A component whose signal is under its noise cannot be shipped in a decision path
and cannot be measured into one either: every ablation of it would be an ablation of the day it ran.

### The verdict the pre-registration requires

§285 stated: _"if nomination on 1 422 cases does not clear 75.5 %, the agentic line retires for good."_ It scored
74.5–74.6 % against 75.5 %, with a union ceiling of 76.2 % that no gate could exceed. **The line retires.** Not
because a protocol was badly chosen — three protocols were measured, two of them this month — but because on this
corpus, with this presentation, the model's reading carries no information the engine does not already have, and its
variance exceeds its value.

Retirement is specific and does not generalise to "models cannot do RCA". `arXiv:2608.21310v2` reports 90.0 % for
Sonnet + ThinkDepth.ai on the same benchmark, with **open-ended telemetry requerying** as the mechanism. What retires
here is the _read-one-page-and-answer_ shape — a single call over a pre-extracted feature table — which the same
paper measures at 45.8 % for OpsAgent, the framework it describes as issuing no telemetry queries of its own. Two
measurements, three orders of magnitude apart in cost, agreeing that the shape is the limit.

### What this redirects the effort to

The two obstacles that remain are both deterministic and both arithmetic:

1. **Position, not generation.** The depth report's `absent` column is **0 of 1 422**: the engine's complete order
   contains an accepted answer in every case. The 173 misses at width five are 61 at rank 5–19 and 112 at rank ≥ 20.
   There is no case whose answer was never generated, so the ceiling is a function of how deep a reader may look and
   nothing else.
2. **The presentation width.** `run-fse26.ts:270` calls `pruner.analyze(faultGraph, 5)`. The reader bound rises from
   87.8 % (width 5) to 89.9 % (10) to 92.1 % (20) at no cost in Acc@1, because top-1 is a prefix of the same total
   order. **No model is involved** — and since §285b retires the model, width does not help either: it raises what a
   reader _could_ reach, and the shipped engine already reads the whole order. What the ladder measures is therefore
   the engine's **ordering** error, which is where all 24.5 points of Top@1 headroom sit.

Against the published table (`arXiv:2608.21310v2`, Table 2), the shipped deterministic engine at **75.5 %** is above
six of the ten reported configurations — TaskWeaver 65.2, RCLAgent V2 53.4, GoS 48.2, OpenRCA 46.6, OpsAgent 45.8,
Qwen mABC 42.6 — and below AIQ 77.6, ThinkDepth.ai 79.2, ClaudeCode 79.6 and Sonnet+ThinkDepth.ai 90.0. A ranker with
zero model calls is inside the band only three LLM frameworks occupy.

### Axes this closes

- **"The expression protocol was the binding constraint."** False, measured: nomination removes the expressive cost
  entirely and scores 0.9 points _below_ the engine, with a union ceiling 4.5 points below the elimination protocol's.
- **"A stronger harness on the same table would clear the engine."** False for the read-one-page shape, at 1 422
  cases, with a pre-registered kill criterion that fired.
- **"An LLM arm's delta can be measured by one run."** False, and this is the iteration's most transferable result:
  the same prompt produced a 15.1-point swing. Every LLM ablation in this repository's history was a single run.
- **"The engine's contribution is reproducible."** True, and now proven by digest rather than asserted: three
  artifacts, identical md5 across a commit that edited the pruner.

### What ships

The instrumentation is kept, because the next iteration needs it: `agentic-protocol-ceiling.ts` prints the reader
bound, the union bound and the recall curve for any protocol, and `run-agentic-ceiling.ts` does it offline in under
a second. The nomination module stays as a measured negative — a second protocol that was built, dispatched, scored
and retired, with its ceiling recorded so nobody has to build it again. No decision path in the product reads either
of them: `AgentOptions` still has no model-facing switch, which is the correct state for a layer that lost to its own
control.

The agentic plan document is amended rather than deleted: `docs/agentic-layer-plan.md` §9 records the retirement, the
three ceilings that bound it, and the two deterministic obstacles that replace it.

## §286 — The caller wins 100 of the 111 one-step cases, and four terms that cannot move a rank

Iteration 285b left one sentence to test: _every remaining point is the engine's ordering error_. This iteration
asked the corpus where that error lives, and the answer is specific enough to name a mechanism — but the three
levers the engine already has for that mechanism are **inert on this corpus**, which is the finding that matters
more than the numbers.

### 1. The pairing adds three quantities the collector's dump does not carry

The raw parquet corpus carries client and server spans, so every RPC can be paired on `(trace_id, parent_span_id)`.
From that pairing, per service, over the abnormal window against the same service's normal window:

| quantity | definition                                               | what it separates                      |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `own`    | median server duration minus the slowest callee's median | time the service spent itself          |
| `tIn`    | median transport ratio on the edges that point at it     | link latency into the service          |
| `tOut`   | median transport ratio on the edges it originates        | link latency out of it                 |
| `egress` | `tOut / tIn`                                             | whether the delay is on its own egress |

All four are post/pre ratios of medians, computed for **1 248 of 1 422** cases (one case's parquet the reader
cannot open; the scope is exactly the cases whose truth is one of the five presented, baseline `1 072 = 85.90 %`).

### 2. Every fusion of them loses, and the loss is not marginal

Plain argmax over the five candidates, on the same scope:

| rule             | correct | %         |
| ---------------- | ------- | --------- |
| engine (shipped) | 1 072   | **85.90** |
| `srv` ratio      | 572     | 45.83     |
| `own`            | 573     | 45.91     |
| `tOut`           | 550     | 44.07     |
| `tIn`            | 456     | 36.54     |
| `egress`         | 306     | 24.52     |

Three fusion families were tried, all pre-registered before the numbers were read:

- **gated swap** — replace the engine's first choice only when a candidate's `own` beats it by more than `θ`:
  net **−65 to −73** at every `θ` from 0 to 3 (gain 25 / loss 98 at `θ = 0`). `tIn` is far worse (−137 to −230).
- **multiplicative** — `score × exp(α · log own)`: −51 at `α = 0.05`, −345 at `α = 1`.
- **rank fusion** — `rrf(engine, own)` and `rrf(engine, tIn)`: −188 to −307 at every `k`.

A bucket census by `max(own)` over the five explains why: `own`'s hit rate does **not** rise with its magnitude
(46.7 % below 1.0, 51.7 % above 20, 26.7 % in the 5–20 band). There is no threshold at which the quantity becomes
the better reader, so no gate can be built on it.

**This corrects the previous iteration's reading.** A three-case sample showed `own` ranking the truth first in two
of three; at n = 1 248 the same statistic is 45.9 %, thirty points _below_ the engine. The sample was the
instrument's noise floor, not a signal.

### 3. What the decomposition did find: the weakness is a fault family, not a rule

Top@1 by fault family on the full 1 422, with the rank of the first accepted answer:

| family                   | n   | Top@1     | rank-2 | rank-3 | outside 5 |
| ------------------------ | --- | --------- | ------ | ------ | --------- |
| JVMMemoryStress          | 171 | **100.0** | 0      | 0      | 0         |
| ContainerKill            | 89  | **100.0** | 0      | 0      | 0         |
| PodFailure / PodKill     | 34  | **100.0** | 0      | 0      | 0         |
| HTTPRequestReplacePath   | 39  | 97.4      | 1      | 0      | 0         |
| NetworkDelay             | 21  | 95.2      | 1      | 0      | 0         |
| HTTPResponseReplaceBody  | 51  | 88.2      | 4      | 2      | 0         |
| HTTPResponseReplaceCode  | 231 | 70.1      | 11     | 2      | 55        |
| HTTPRequestReplaceMethod | 190 | 65.8      | 18     | 4      | 38        |
| NetworkPartition         | 97  | 66.0      | 10     | 7      | 15        |
| HTTPRequestDelay         | 88  | 64.8      | 13     | 5      | 11        |
| HTTPResponseDelay        | 89  | 62.9      | 17     | 5      | 7         |
| NetworkLoss              | 48  | 60.4      | 8      | 3      | 7         |
| **NetworkBandwidth**     | 42  | **47.6**  | 3      | 9      | 6         |

The engine is exact on resource faults (208/208 on memory, container and pod kills) and weak on the two families
that carry no resource signal: **content substitution** (`ReplaceCode` / `ReplaceMethod`: 421 cases, 68.2 %) and
**link faults** (network family: 208 cases, 66.3 %). Any lever worth dispatching has to act on those 629 cases.

### 4. The 111 one-step cases are one mechanism, and it is inheritance

Of the 176 in-scope misses, **111 put the truth at rank 2** — one step, 7.8 points of the corpus. Pairing the
spans gives the relation between the rank-1 candidate and the truth for each of them:

| rank-1 candidate's relation to the truth | rank-2 cases | rank-3 cases (control) |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------------- |
| **caller** (the truth calls it)          | **100**      | 3                      |
| callee                                   | **0**        | 21                     |
| no direct edge                           | 11           | 19                     |

A caller's response time _contains_ its callees', so on any anomaly that propagates along the call graph the
caller's deviation is the larger of the two by construction. 90 % of the one-step misses are exactly that, and
the channel evidence says so directly: on those 100 cases the truth's
`http.server.request.duration` departure exceeds the winner's by a factor of 5 to 20 (e.g. 187.8 against
2 210.1), while the winner leads on `http.response.error_rate` (31 cases against 6) — the victim's signature.

### 5. The three terms that exist for this mechanism are inert on this corpus

Four arms on the shipped configuration (FSE'26, 1 422 cases, run ids in the table):

| knob                                     | value              | Top@1        | Δ         |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------ | --------- |
| shipped                                  | `selfTimeWeight=0` | **75.457 %** | —         |
| `self_time_weight`                       | 0.25               | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `self_time_weight`                       | 0.5                | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `self_time_weight`                       | 1.0                | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `self_time_weight`                       | 2.0                | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `topo_discount=0.25, gate=0`             | scope `external`   | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `topo_discount=0.5, gate=0`              | scope `external`   | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `topo_discount=1, gate=0`                | scope `external`   | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `topo_discount=1, gate=0.5`              | scope `external`   | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `topo_discount=1, gate=0`                | scope `caller`     | 75.457 %     | **0**     |
| `topo_discount=1, gate=0`                | scope `all`        | 72.570 %     | **−2.89** |
| `topo_discount=0.5, gate=0, closure=sum` | scope `all`        | 74.890 %     | −0.57     |
| `victim_weight`                          | 0.5                | 74.402 %     | −1.06     |
| `victim_weight`                          | 1.0                | 71.590 %     | −3.87     |
| `victim_weight`                          | 2.0                | 62.030 %     | −13.43    |

Byte-identical rankings at four different self-time weights and at a fully open topological gate are not a
measurement of "the term does not help". They are the signature of a term that **contributes zero to every
candidate**, and the code says which one:

- `computeSelfTimeScores` marks a candidate `undecided` — and drops it entirely — as soon as **any** of its
  callees lacks a latency level (`ranking-signals.ts:834-848`). On a 41-service graph that condition holds for
  nearly every candidate, so the map is empty and `presenceOf` reports `ABSENT` for all five. The guard is
  deliberate (reading an unmeasured callee as 0 would make the caller look self-created, i.e. vote for the exact
  wrong service), which means the term as written can only speak on a graph where every callee is measurable —
  not this one.
- The topological deduction is gated at `topoDiscountGate = 1`, which charges a node only where its callees
  account for **all** of its anomaly (`pruner.ts:1597-1616`). Opening the gate to 0 and 0.5 moved nothing, which
  says the deduction's extensive space is degenerate here — the same rank-normalisation the constant's docblock
  already records for TrainTicket.

`victimWeight` is the control that proves the wiring is fine: the same dispatch mechanism moved it by −1.06 and
−13.43 points. The difference is that its input map is dense.

### 6. The caliber of the 90.0 % the campaign is chasing

`arXiv:2608.21310v2` reports Sonnet + ThinkDepth.ai at 90.0 Acc@1 on **a 500-case simple random sample** of
RCABench's 1 430. This corpus is the same family at 1 422 cases. Resampling 500 cases from the shipped per-case
outcomes 20 000 times gives Top@1 **75.46 % mean, 95 % interval [72.40, 78.60]**, with `P(sample ≥ 90.0) = 0`.
The gap to the published leader is therefore not a sampling artefact and not a different corpus: it is 15 points
of ranking, and the family table in §3 says where.

### Axes this closes

- **"The client/server pairing carries a ranking signal the dumps lack."** False at n = 1 248, in three fusion
  families, with the small-sample reading that suggested otherwise recorded as an illusion.
- **"PRISM's internal/external symmetry mask helps."** False and monotone: −1.06 / −3.87 / −13.43 at weights
  0.5 / 1 / 2. The axiom's _direction_ is right (the winner is external-only in the rank-2 cases) but its
  _magnitude_ cannot be separated from self-anomaly without also discounting true external faults, which are 53 %
  of the corpus.
- **"Weights nobody swept are the remaining lever."** False for the three mechanism terms: two are inert by
  construction on this graph and the third degrades monotonically. A weight sweep is only a measurement where
  the term's input map is dense.

### What is dispatched next, and why it is not another weight

`--terms-dump` (workflow input `terms_dump`, artifact `fse26-terms.ndjson`) emits the engine's own per-term
`(weight, slope)` for every candidate, so **any** weight vector is `score + Σ (w' − w)·slope` — a local
computation over one run rather than one dispatch per arm. The dump is in flight; the next iteration reads it to
answer the two questions this one could only pose:

1. Which terms actually carry the ranking on the 421 content-substitution and 208 link cases, and what fraction of
   the score gap in the 100 caller-inheritance cases each one contributes?
2. Whether the self-time term can be repaired rather than swept — the dense observable already exists
   (`edgeLatency`, span-derived), and the choice between "repair the map" and "accept the term is silent" is a
   code decision this register can now state with numbers instead of a sweep.

## §286b — The term dump: five terms with no coverage at all, and one term carrying fourteen points

`--terms-dump` writes, per case, every candidate's 19 terms as `(name, weight, slope)`. One run over the
FSE'26 corpus (1 422 cases, 51 candidates each, 38 MB) turns every weight question into a local computation
instead of a dispatch — and it also answers a question no dispatch could: **which terms are populated at all**.

### Coverage: five of nineteen terms appear on no candidate

| term                                                                   | configured weight | cases where the term is present on at least one candidate |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------: | --------------------------------------------------------: |
| `selfAnomalyLog1p`                                                     |                 1 |                                                     1 422 |
| `prism`                                                                |                 0 |                                                     1 422 |
| `rise`, `pool`, `collision`, `temporal`, `source`, `topo`, `stability` | 0 / −0.0679 / 0 … |                                                     1 422 |
| `log`                                                                  |                 1 |                                                     1 000 |
| `dualFamily`                                                           |              0.25 |                                                     1 003 |
| `failedEdge`                                                           |                 3 |                                                     1 222 |
| `lat`                                                                  |          0.561495 |                                                       760 |
| `podState`                                                             |                 8 |                                                       294 |
| **`trace`**                                                            |             **1** |                                                     **0** |
| **`selfTime`**                                                         |             **0** |                                                     **0** |
| **`emission`**                                                         |                 0 |                                                     **0** |
| **`faultFree`**                                                        |                 0 |                                                     **0** |
| **`victim`**                                                           |             **0** |                                                     **0** |

`trace` is the one that matters: it is configured at weight **1** — the same as `selfAnomalyLog1p` — and it is
present on **zero of 1 422 cases**. A term at weight 1 that never fires is indistinguishable, in every published
score, from a term that does not exist. The sweep of `selfTimeWeight` in §286 is the same fact from the other
side: the map is empty, so four weights produce one ranking.

### No single term is a ranker; the engine is a combination

Sorted by each term alone over the same 51-candidate lists:

| term               | Top@1 as the only ranker | usable cases |
| ------------------ | -----------------------: | -----------: |
| `failedEdge`       |                  47.89 % |        1 222 |
| `prism`            |                  44.02 % |        1 422 |
| `log`              |                  43.67 % |        1 000 |
| `dualFamily`       |                  42.12 % |        1 003 |
| `lat`              |                  25.67 % |          760 |
| `selfAnomalyLog1p` |                  24.47 % |        1 422 |
| `podState`         |                  20.68 % |          294 |
| `rise`             |                  14.70 % |        1 422 |
| `pool`             |                  12.45 % |        1 422 |
| `collision`        |                   5.63 % |        1 422 |
| `temporal`         |                   4.22 % |        1 422 |
| `stability`        |                   2.53 % |        1 422 |
| `topo`             |                   0.70 % |        1 422 |
| engine (all 19)    |              **75.46 %** |        1 422 |

Every individual term is far below the combination, which is the honest statement of why the architecture is not
replaceable by any one signal — and why "which term is the lever" has no answer at the level of a single term.

### One term carries fourteen points, and it is not the anomaly

Zeroing one configured term at a time, reconstructed from the dump (`Δ` from 1 096, see the residual note below):

| term               |   weight |         Δ Top@1 |
| ------------------ | -------: | --------------: |
| **`podState`**     |    **8** |        **−205** |
| `failedEdge`       |        3 |             −65 |
| `dualFamily`       |     0.25 |             −25 |
| `lat`              | 0.561495 |             −22 |
| `pool`             |  −0.0679 |              −1 |
| `trace`            |        1 | 0 (no coverage) |
| `log`              |        1 |          **+9** |
| `selfAnomalyLog1p` |        1 |         **+14** |

The shipped ranker on this corpus is, by contribution, a **pod-state ranker with a failed-edge tie-breaker**;
the two terms that the architecture's documentation treats as the model — `selfAnomalyLog1p` and `log` — each
cost one to two tenths of a point when zeroed, i.e. the ranking is _better_ without them. That is consistent
with the family table in §286 (208/208 on resource faults, 66 % on link and content faults): `podState` is
exactly the term that solves resource faults, and it is doing the work.

### The residual, recorded rather than hidden

The reconstruction `score = Σ weight × slope` is **not exact**: the worst residual is `3.0`, and it is
`failedEdge` on a candidate that records `weight = 3, slope = 1` in a case whose recorded score does not
contain that 3. The dump carries no `presence` field, so an absent term (`None`) and a present term of value
zero are indistinguishable to a reader — which is the one thing this artifact cannot answer, and the reason
every number in the table above is stated as a reconstruction rather than as a re-run. The ablation's _ranking_
of terms is robust to it (a 3.0 residual on one candidate cannot move a 205-case effect); the third decimal is
not.

### Dispatched on the strength of this table

`prism` is present on all 1 422 cases, ranks 44.02 % alone, and is configured at weight **0** — the only
populated term with no weight. Three arms (`prism_weight` 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5) are in flight; the axis was refused
once on RCAEval's nine cells as an additive term, and this corpus is the one where its shape (`min(Sⁱ, Sᵉ)`) is
already enrolled at 0.25 through `dualFamilyWeight`. What the sweep asks is whether the _score_ form is refused
there too, on a population whose two weak families are exactly the ones PRISM's axiom describes.

## §286c — The readback: podState saturates at four, and PRISM's score form is refused a third time

Six arms closed the two axes §286b opened.

### `prism_weight` on this corpus: refused, and monotonically

| weight      |        Top@1 |               Δ |
| ----------- | -----------: | --------------: |
| 0 (shipped) | **75.457 %** |               — |
| 0.1         |     75.530 % | +0.07 (+1 case) |
| 0.25        |     74.610 % |           −0.85 |
| 0.5         |     72.640 % |           −2.82 |

One case is not a signal, and the monotone decay on either side of it says the same thing the RCAEval nine
cells said in iteration 140: PRISM's `min(Sⁱ, Sᵉ)` works as a **shape indicator** (`dualFamilyWeight` 0.25,
enrolled) and not as a **score**. Third refusal, now on the population whose weak families it was designed for.

### `pod_state_weight`: a plateau at four, and what the plateau means

| weight             |        Top@1 |      Δ |
| ------------------ | -----------: | -----: |
| **8 (shipped)**    | **75.457 %** |      — |
| 4                  |     75.392 % |  −0.07 |
| 2                  |     71.800 % |  −3.66 |
| 1                  |     65.050 % | −10.41 |
| 0 (reconstruction) |      ≈62.6 % |  −12.9 |

The shipped value sits **on a plateau**: halving it costs one case. Below four the curve is steep. That is not a
tuning opportunity — it is the scale statement this register could not make before the dump existed.

### The scale imbalance, stated as arithmetic

Every prior in the sum is a share on `[0, 1]`. The weights are not on a common scale: `podState` 8,
`failedEdge` 3, `selfAnomalyLog1p` 1, `dualFamily` 0.25, `pool` 0.0679. At `podState` 8 a candidate whose pod
state share is 0.75 contributes **6.0**, while the base term — `log1p(anomaly)` at weight 1 — contributes
**0.34** on the same candidate. The extensive anomaly that the collision picture is built to rank is therefore
0.6 % of the score it is supposed to determine, and the sweep in §286 is the arithmetic consequence: no
self-time or topological weight can move a ranking whose first six points come from a term that is a pod
lifecycle indicator.

This is not a defect introduced by any single change; it is the accumulated result of eight knobs each
measured on the corpus that made it look good. What §286b's ablation establishes is that the corpus this
campaign must win is being ranked by the one term that is exact on resource faults (208/208) and silent on the
629 content and link cases — which is precisely the family table in §286.

### What this licenses for the next iteration

`pod_state_weight=4` is **free** (−0.07, one case). That is the only configuration change in this register
that costs nothing, and it is worth one arm only as the _floor_ of a scale experiment: 4 is where the balance
between the pod indicator and the anomaly can be redressed without paying for it. The experiment is
`pod_state_weight=4 × self_anomaly_weight ∈ {2, 4} × topo_discount` measured against the shipped ranking on the
629 weak cases, not on the corpus total — a lever that only buys resource-fault cases has no headroom left.

## §287 — The containment order: 41 wins, 0 losses, and the instrument that finally reconciles

Iteration 286 ended with a family table, a mechanism (inheritance) and a puzzle: three terms aimed at that
mechanism, four weight sweeps and seven gate settings, and a **byte-identical** ranking. This iteration answers the
puzzle three ways — by repairing the instrument that produced it, by closing the data path that would not have
helped, and by stating the mechanism as an **order constraint** instead of a weight, which is the only form it has.

### 1. Correction: the term dump reconstructs exactly, and §286b's residual was a reading error

§286b reconstructed `score = Σ weight × slope` with the CONFIG weights and recorded a residual of `3.0` on 1 114
cases, then qualified every number by it. The dump does not carry the config weight — it carries **the weight the
engine actually used per term per candidate**, and on this corpus `failedEdge` is recorded at `3` on 394 candidates,
at `0` on 3 522 (the gate refused it) and `None` elsewhere. Using the dump's own weight:

```
max |Σ w_dump·slope − recorded score| = 8.882e-16      over 1 422 cases
Top@1                                 = 1 073/1 422 = 75.4571 %
```

So the reconstruction is **exact**, the shipped number is reproduced, and every offline screen in this register is
a local computation over one run with no residual to qualify. §286b's ablation _ordering_ was right; its stated
error bar was not, and this supersedes it.

### 2. The `trace` data path is repairable and not worth repairing

§286b found `trace` at weight **1** with zero coverage on 1 422 cases and called it a data-path defect. It is one:
the bridge pre-aggregates spans into distinct caller→callee edges and drops the per-service counts the term reads.
The parquet has them, so the observable was measured before a line of loader code was written — 1 249 cases, span
counts per service over both windows, the engine's own rule applied to them (pre ≥ 500, growth ≥ 1.15, growth ≥ 2×
the fleet's median drift, **unique** riser):

| quantity                             |                  value |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------: |
| cases with a unique qualifying riser | **91 / 1 249 = 7.3 %** |
| of those, the riser is the truth     |        **51 = 56.0 %** |

Seven per cent coverage at 56 % precision against an engine that reads 85.9 % on the same scope. The axis is
**closed by measurement rather than by absence of data**: the data path could be built, and it would not pay.

### 3. Every populated-but-unweighted term was swept, and none of them pays

Six terms carry data on this corpus and a weight of zero — `collision` (31 190 candidates), `temporal` (64 237),
`source`, `topo`, `rise`, `prism`. Each was swept alone over
`w ∈ {±0.05, ±0.1, ±0.2, ±0.5, ±1, ±2}`, then a greedy forward pass combined the winners:

| term                  | best single weight |           Δ Top@1 | halves  |
| --------------------- | -----------------: | ----------------: | ------- |
| `temporal`            |              +0.05 |                +4 | −1 / +5 |
| `collision`           |              −0.05 |                +3 | +2 / +1 |
| `rise`                |               −0.2 |                +3 | −2 / +5 |
| `source`              |              −0.05 |                +2 | −1 / +3 |
| `prism`               |              +0.05 |                +2 | +1 / +1 |
| `topo`                |               +0.1 |                 0 | −2 / +2 |
| greedy stack of three |                    | **+6 = +0.42 pp** |         |

Four cases out of 1 422 is the noise floor, and the halves disagree in sign on three of the six. **`collision` —
the Deng Yu collision source — is populated on 45 % of candidates and worth nothing as an additive weight on this
corpus.** That is the third independent statement of the same fact (§286's weight sweeps, §286b's ablation, this
sweep), and it is the reason the next section changes the FORM rather than the coefficient.

### 4. The mechanism as an order constraint

A caller's response time contains its callee's, so the pair is inverted by construction. The statement that repairs
it is relational, and no additive term can express a relational statement. `pruning/containment-order.ts` applies
it directly:

```
band(v, label) = [centre − σ·scale, centre + σ·scale]        (the corpus fault-free profile, σ = 3)
excursion(v)   = max over latency labels of (0 if post ∈ band else distance / band width)
invert rank(i), rank(i+1)  when  rank(i) calls rank(i+1)  and  excursion(rank(i+1)) > excursion(rank(i)) + margin
```

Measured on all 1 422 cases, one pass over the top five:

|                       |     cases |        Top@1 |
| --------------------- | --------: | -----------: |
| shipped               |     1 073 |     75.457 % |
| shipped + containment | **1 114** |  **78.34 %** |
| Δ                     |   **+41** | **+2.88 pp** |

Gains **41**, losses **0**, halves **+25 / +16**. The families that gain are the ones that PROPAGATE
(HTTPRequestDelay +8, HTTPResponseDelay +7, NetworkPartition +5, NetworkCorrupt +4, NetworkLoss +3,
NetworkBandwidth +3, HTTPRequestReplaceMethod +2); resource faults are unchanged at 12/12.

The rule without the band — a plain ratio comparison — reads 24 gains and 0 losses. **The band is worth 17 cases**,
which is why the pass reads the corpus profile and not a ratio: a service whose latency is naturally wide is not a
service that moved.

Three fusion forms were measured first and all failed, which is why the shipped form is an order constraint:

- `tOut(callee) > tOut(caller)` (the transport reading): 61 gains, **5 losses**;
- `own` gated swap (§286): 25 gains, 98 losses;
- `rrf(engine, own)`: −188 to −307.

### 5. Prior art, and the precise size of the claim

**TD-RCA** (IWQoS 2026, `10.1109/IWQoS70441.2026.11661074`) names this mechanism _Cascade Confusion_ — "synchronous
blocking RPC can amplify upstream anomaly signals and cause victim services to exhibit stronger symptoms than the
true root cause" — and decouples it with a Dual-Perspective module inside a VAE-GNN, reporting HR@1 93.9 % on
TrainTicket and 94.3 % on SocialNetwork. The mechanism is therefore established prior art and is not claimed here.
What is claimed is narrower: a deterministic band test needs no training, costs **zero** losses on this corpus (a
learned module cannot state that about itself), and reads one number per arm instead of one model per corpus.

TD-RCA's dual perspective is the transport reading measured above at 61 gains and 5 losses, so the two are the
same family with a different observable — and this corpus prefers the band.

### 6. Shipped off, and the exact reason

`DEFAULT_CONTAINMENT_ORDER = false`. The pass needs `faultFreeProfile`, and **no benchmark dispatch supplies one**:
`--fault-free-profile` sits on the dispatch-surface census' unreachable list, because "a dispatch that could name a
path could name one fitted on another corpus". That rule is right — and it makes a `true` default a switch whose
input is empty in every production run, which is the defect §286b recorded for `traceWeight = 1` over zero
coverage. The arm is stated on `.github/workflows/benchmark-agentic.yml` (input `containment_order`), the only
workflow that builds the profile it ranks against.

Promotion is three steps, all named in `docs/containment-order.md` §7: derive the profile inside the benchmark
workflow (a derived path, never a dispatch input), revise the census entry so the check matches its rationale, and
flip the default to `true` with all four cells re-read.

### Axes this closes

- **"The term weights are the remaining lever."** False for the sixth time: every populated-but-unweighted term is
  worth ≤ 4 cases with halves that disagree in sign, and the greedy stack of three is +6.
- **"`trace` is a data-path bug worth fixing."** False by measurement: the data exists, would cover 7.3 % of cases,
  and would be right 56 % of the time.
- **"Inheritance is a weighting problem."** False, and this is the finding that matters: the same mechanism worth
  **+2.88 pp** as an order constraint is worth **0.000 pp** as any coefficient of the fusion, because a
  candidate-local sum cannot express a relation between two candidates.

## §287b — The readback: 47 wins, 5 losses, and a second lever worth more than the first

§287 registered the containment order at **41 gains / 0 losses** from a screening formula over the presented five.
Two dispatches of `.github/workflows/benchmark-agentic.yml` — identical but for `containment_order` — replace that
number, and the replacement is worse in one direction and larger in the other.

|                       | cases |        Top@1 |  gains | losses |     net |
| --------------------- | ----: | -----------: | -----: | -----: | ------: |
| `containment_order=0` | 1 422 |     75.457 % |      — |      — |       — |
| `containment_order=1` | 1 422 | **78.411 %** | **47** |  **5** | **+42** |

Per case, read from each run's own `per-case.ndjson`: 47 gains, 5 losses, and the five are
`HTTPResponseReplaceCode`×2, `HTTPResponseAbort`, `HTTPResponseDelay`, `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` — i.e. the
response-rewrite mechanism, where the injected service's _callees_ look worse on duration and the pass promotes one
of them past it.

**Why the screen said zero and the engine says five.** The screen's `maxdep` was the largest normalised departure
over **every** channel a candidate carries; the shipped `latencyExcursions` restricts the quantity to the latency
family, because a claim about inherited _response time_ should be made on the channel that carries response time. A
counter channel departs its band under a source fault far more sharply than any duration channel does, so the
all-channel form inverts on the wrong instrument and, on this corpus, happens never to invert a correct pair. The
41/0 figure is therefore a true statement about a quantity that does not ship; §287's own table is left standing as
the record of the screen and is marked as such.

**Second falsification, of §287's own margin claim.** §287 read the margin sweep as "a flat plateau in the only
direction that matters (losses stay at zero)". Re-measured in the engine on the 711-case half (`waveB2`, profile
built from that half), the sweep is monotone in the wrong direction: margin 0 gives 518 Top@1 (+34/0), 0.1 gives
517, 0.25 gives 509, 0.5 gives 504. Zero is the maximum, and **no margin on this axis can be the discriminator for
the five** — all five lie outside that half. The local harness reproduces both CI arms per case, 711 of 711, with
zero disagreements on either verdict, which is what licenses reading it as a measurement of the shipped path.

**The lever this iteration found, which is larger than the one §287 registered.** The failed-edge term — the only
directional signal in the engine — is gated by `admitsFailedEdgeTerm`, which conditions the term on the _current
rank-1's_ dominant metric being duration-shaped. Four arms over the same 711 cases, one graph per case, only the
gate mode changed:

| gate mode                |             Top@1 |  gains | losses |     net |
| ------------------------ | ----------------: | -----: | -----: | ------: |
| `absolute` (shipped)     |     484 (68.07 %) |      — |      — |       — |
| `evidence`               |     476 (66.95 %) |      2 |     10 |      −8 |
| **`margin` (share 0.5)** | **518 (72.86 %)** | **61** | **27** | **+34** |
| `fleet`                  |     458 (64.42 %) |      3 |     29 |     −26 |

`margin` asks the only question that matters for a ranking — _can this term overturn the leader at all_ — and gains
concentrate exactly where the shipped gate is blind: **36 of the 61 are `HTTPResponseReplaceCode`**, the family that
owns 46 of the 112 cases whose truth is outside the presented five. Its 27 losses are the delay families, so the
discriminator is the same one the containment pass needs, which is the useful part: **`margin` and the containment
pass fail on one family and gain on another, and both are gated by the same question — is the failing interface the
SOURCE or a VICTIM.**

A share sweep — 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05 — reads 61/27, 61/25, 61/25, 58/23, 45/15: the losses fall by two and then
ride the gains down, so the bar buys a better ratio only by refusing the term altogether. Neither lever is
shippable under the zero-regression rule as it stands.

**A trap this iteration found in the plumbing, recorded because it silently mislabelled a measurement.** `margin`
reads `failedEdgeGateShare`, and the FSE'26 CLI always populates that field with the _gate_ default (0.5). So
`--failed-edge-gate-mode margin` with no share runs the **fleet-share number**, not
`DEFAULT_FAILED_EDGE_MARGIN_SHARE` (0.3): the two maxima share one option, which is the defect the pruner's own
comment at `failedEdgeGate` warns about. The four-arm table above is measured at 0.5 for that reason, and says so.

### Axes this closes

- **"The screening formula's zero is the module's zero."** False, and it cost the iteration a claimed result: a
  screen that re-derives a quantity is not a measurement of the module that ships it.
- **"A threshold on the containment margin removes its losses."** False. The margin is monotone in gains and the
  losses are not in its reach.
- **"The passed five is the same population as the full order."** True but not sufficient — the five-set is
  identical between the arms (1 422 of 1 422), so the difference between a screen and the engine is the quantity,
  not the window.

### Prior art, checked 2026-11-15, for the discriminator §287b names

The source-versus-victim question is **not** unclaimed, and the register must say so before the next iteration
proposes a form for it:

- **TopoEvo** (2026, arXiv `2605.15611`) discretises node representations into VQ symptom tokens whose evidence
  signature includes "trace-derived interaction patterns indicating **incoming (victim-like) versus outgoing
  (source-like)** anomaly directionality", then reasons over them with a hypothesis/evidence/judge multi-agent
  loop. That is the same discrimination as a learned token inside an LLM framework.
- **Beyond Fault Localization** (arXiv `2608.21310`) shows the failure this register keeps measuring from the
  evaluation side: agents "rank services by error count → **affected service ranks first**", with answer
  correctness and diagnostic quality coming apart, and `Acc@1 43.5 % → 52.5 %` from a grounding/verification
  stage.
- **TD-RCA** (IWQoS 2026) remains the named precedent for the containment mechanism itself (§8 of
  `docs/containment-order.md`).

What is left to claim here is therefore narrow and unchanged in kind from §287: a **deterministic, zero-training**
discriminator whose refusals are enumerable — not the question itself. Any future draft that presents
"source vs victim" as the contribution is contradicted by the first bullet.

## §288 — Two phase-coupling defects, found by the same question asked twice

§287b ended with one discriminator named and two levers that both carried regressions. This iteration asked a
narrower question — _which phase does each option belong to_ — and the answer produced two defects and one
measurement that is better than either lever alone.

### 288a. The margin bar read the fleet constant, and no predicate test could see it

`failedEdgeGateShare` is filled at construction from `DEFAULT_FAILED_EDGE_GATE_SHARE` (0.5), so the margin branch's

```ts
share: gateMode === 'margin' ? (this.options.failedEdgeGateShare ?? DEFAULT_FAILED_EDGE_MARGIN_SHARE) : …
```

had an **unreachable right operand**: `?? 0.3` can never run when the field is always populated. A run that
selected `margin` and named no share therefore compared against **0.5** while the default's own docblock, the
predicate's docblock and five predicate-level tests all said **0.3**.

It survived because of where the tests were pointed. At the `admitsFailedEdgeTerm` layer the CALLER passes the
share, so no assertion there can observe which field the engine read it from. The defect was found by two harnesses
disagreeing on **two cases out of 711** (518 against 520) and then by a three-way probe — omit the key, spell it
`undefined`, name 0.3 — in which _omitting_ the key behaved differently from _spelling it undefined_, which is only
possible if something fills it in between.

**Fix:** a field per maximum. `failedEdgeMarginShare` (default 0.3) is what the margin bar reads;
`failedEdgeGateShare` (0.5) serves `fleet` and `evidence`. The engine-level fence is
`failed-edge-gate.test.ts`'s "reads the margin default from the MARGIN constant": a case whose reach is **0.3375**,
i.e. inside the gate constant and outside the margin one, so the two readings disagree on a live term versus
`WEIGHT_ZERO`.

**The dispatch surface was built, then withdrawn, and the withdrawal is the finding.** `--failed-edge-margin-share`
was threaded through the CLI, the engine options, the rendered configuration line and all **seven** `anomaly_knobs`
copies of `.github/workflows/benchmark-rcaeval.yml`. It made three golden-anchor tests fail in the way that
mechanism exists to fail: a configuration line is the digest the committed cell baseline is held to, so naming one
more field obliges the iteration to re-anchor `benchmarks/baselines/rcaeval-nine-cells.json` against **a fresh
735-case battery of the shipped configuration**.

That is the correct price for a shippable option and the wrong price for this one. The margin bar carries 25
regressions (§288c) and cannot ship; spending a re-anchored battery on an arm that is already refused would move a
published number to record a measurement that changed nothing. The field therefore lives in the ENGINE with no
dispatch surface — the same status `containmentOrder` had before its own workflow input existed — and the pipe is
built the day a discriminator makes the bar shippable. The census keeps the distinction it exists to keep: the
margin share is _absent from_ the dispatch surface, not _unreachable from_ it.

**Independent verification, not a re-run of the same harness.** The seven-arm factorial reports `mar3` = **520** and
`mar5` = **518**, the two historical readings, from the fixed engine. The numbers did not move because the fix
restores what the documents always claimed; what moved is that the two are now _different arms_ instead of the same
arm under two names.

### 288b. `containmentOrder` lived in the build phase, and `analyze` takes a graph from anywhere

`containmentExcursions` was built only when the pass was switched ON, which made two facts one: _the graph carries
the measurement_ and _this run applies it_. `analyze(graph)` is public and its graph argument can come from any
pruner, so a graph built by a pass-off pruner carried no map and **every** pruner reading it ran without the pass.

The factorial hit this on its first run: `cont` reported **484**, exactly the shipped count, on a corpus with
**13 violating adjacent pairs** (5 of them at rank-1/2). The tell was not the number but its exactness.

**Fix, in two halves.** The map is now built whenever a profile is supplied — a measurement belongs to the case —
and `contained()` reads `this.options.containmentOrder` itself instead of inferring the switch from the map's
existence, because whether it acts belongs to the run. `failedEdgeGateMode` already lives in `analyze`; the two
options are the same kind of choice and now live in the same phase. The fence is
`containment-order.test.ts`'s "lets one pruner analyze a graph another pruner built, under its OWN setting": the
builder has the pass OFF and the reader ON, and both verdicts are asserted on the same graph.

### 288c. The factorial, on the shipped vector, one graph per case, 711 cases

| arm                                |   Top@1 |          % |  gains | losses |     net |
| ---------------------------------- | ------: | ---------: | -----: | -----: | ------: |
| `off` (direction term at weight 0) |     476 |     66.948 |      — |      — |       — |
| **`shipped`**                      | **484** | **68.073** |      — |      — |       — |
| `mar3` (margin bar, share 0.3)     |     520 |     73.136 |     61 | **25** |     +36 |
| `mar5`                             |     518 |     72.855 |     61 |     27 |     +34 |
| **`cont`** (containment order)     | **518** | **72.855** | **34** |  **0** | **+34** |
| `mar3+cont`                        | **550** | **77.356** |     90 |     24 |     +66 |
| `mar5+cont`                        |     548 |     77.075 |     90 |     26 |     +64 |

Three readings worth keeping:

- **Containment is still zero-loss.** 34 gains, 0 losses, on a fixed engine and under the shipped signal vector.
  The families it repairs are the propagating ones (`HTTPResponseDelay` 11, `HTTPRequestDelay` 10,
  `NetworkPartition` 7), which is §287's own mechanism claim surviving a second, differently-built measurement.
- **The two levers are nearly additive on gains and not on losses.** 36 + 34 = 70 against a measured 66, and the
  losses barely move (25 → 24): containment repairs **one** of the margin bar's 25. They are not substitutes.
- **The margin bar's losses are the delay families** (12 `HTTPRequestDelay`, 8 `HTTPResponseDelay` = 20 of 25), so
  §287b's channel hypothesis was right about where they live and wrong about what to do: gains in the same families
  are only 7, and refusing the whole channel would trade 20 losses for those 7 gains — a bar, not a discriminator.

`mar3+cont` at **77.356 %** is the upper bound this iteration can state, and it is **not shippable**: it carries 24
regressions. `cont` alone is the one arm here that satisfies the register's rule.

### Axes this closes

- **"A default that two tests agree on is a default the engine uses."** False when the agreement is at a layer the
  engine's own field choice cannot reach. The margin default had five passing assertions and was not in force.
- **"An option placed in `buildFaultGraph` is placed."** False — `analyze` accepts a foreign graph, so a build-phase
  option is a per-graph option wearing a per-run name.
- **"Containment and the margin bar are two parts of one answer."** False in the useful direction: they overlap on
  one case out of 25, and their gains add.

## §289 — The containment pass had a ceiling, and the ceiling was a channel

§288 ended with `containmentOrder` at +34/−0 on this half and a full-corpus arm at +47/−5 that could not ship. This
iteration asked what the pass cannot do rather than how to tune it — _which of the one-step misses does it not
repair, and why_ — and the answer turned out to be a second instrument, of the same shape, that needs no profile
at all.

### 289a. The census: 34 of 82, and the 41 that no delay can reach

Every one of the 82 cases that publish the truth second behind its own caller, on the 711-case half:

| why the pair is not repaired        |  cases |
| ----------------------------------- | -----: |
| the containment signature fires     | **34** |
| BOTH candidates inside their bands  | **41** |
| no direct edge                      |      5 |
| callee not further outside its band |      2 |

The 34 are the pass's gains exactly. The 41 are its ceiling: a replaced status code, an aborted request or a
rewritten path moves no latency percentile, so the excursion is `0` at both ends, and `0` is a measurement of no
excursion. No margin, weight or profile can turn that `0` into evidence.

### 289b. The second instrument is the failed-call channel read relationally

The channel was already a term, charging every failing edge to its callee. A term scores one candidate at a time;
the relation is a flow: `unexplained(v) = max(0, incoming(v) − outgoing(v))`, where incoming is what v's interface
reported and outgoing what v's own calls reported. A source's inbound rise is its own; a victim's is produced by
the calls it makes and cancels. The pass inverts an adjacent pair on a failing direct edge when
`unexplained(lower) > unexplained(upper)` — the same quantity on both candidates, strictly, with no margin.

| arm                      |   Top@1 |  gains | losses |
| ------------------------ | ------: | -----: | -----: |
| shipped                  |     484 |      — |      — |
| `containmentOrder`       |     518 |     34 |      0 |
| **`failureContainment`** | **538** | **54** |  **0** |
| both                     | **560** | **76** |  **0** |

Halves, by case index: flow **31/0** and **23/0**, union **41/0** and **35/0**. The overlap is 12 cases, which is
what the census predicts — the two channels are silent in almost disjoint places.

**The full corpus disagrees with the half, and the disagreement is the finding.** Two dispatched runs on
`765b399c`, 1 422 cases each: control **75.457 %**, `failure_containment=1` **80.028 %**, i.e. **+4.57 pp** and
**67 gains against 2 losses**. Both losses are `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod`: a fault that corrupts the caller's
outgoing request makes the callee reject it, so the failing edge belongs to the caller while every count says the
callee's interface failed. It is §10.4's degenerate relay generalised to a family, and it is invisible to counts
because the counts are correct — what is missing is the status the callee returned.

### 289c. The one regression, and the degeneracy test that refuses it

Unguarded the arm reads **555 (72/1)**. The loss is a relay whose every hop carries the same 203 failures, so the
leaf's residual is the whole count and the middle's is zero: the three accounts are ONE account and the asymmetry
is an artefact of where the chain stops. The refusal is an equality at three sites — the callee saw that count on
this edge, the caller reported it on this edge, and the caller's inbound count is the same number — and it costs
**18 of the 72** gains. It is not a threshold: nothing is compared against a chosen number.

Two sound guards were measured and refused for cost, and recorded so the next iteration does not rediscover them:
self-anomaly corroboration keeps **22/0**, a second failing caller keeps **12/0**.

### 289d. The temporal instrument, measured and refused

`postInjectOnsetDelays` is the collision-source-at-`t₀` model in its plainest form, and it is right about the loss
case (`food-service` +2 338 ms, `travel-service` +25 768 ms). It is still refused as a rule: **45/18** alone, and
every arbiter that consults it inherits the eighteen. The dominant metric an onset is measured on is often not the
metric the fault drives, so the ordering is noisy in both directions. Being right about the case it was consulted
for is not evidence about a rule.

### Axes this closes

- **"Tuning the containment margin is the way to repair the rest."** False — the remaining 48 have no delay
  signature at all, so the axis has no purchase on them (§5's sweep already said this from the other side).
- **"A second instrument must be a third threshold."** False — the flow rule compares one quantity on two
  candidates, exactly as the excursion rule does, and its only parameter-free refinement is an equality.
- **"A channel that is right about the case in front of you is an instrument."** False for onset: 45 gains against
  18 losses, on the same pairs where the flow channel costs one.

## §290 — The failure-flow pass lost two cases because a count cannot name its own author

§289 closed with the second relational pass at **+67/−2** on the full corpus and a promotion path whose first task
was a data-pipeline change: split the failed calls by HTTP status, 4xx for a caller's malformed request and 5xx for
a failing callee. This iteration opened the datapack and found the split does not encode that distinction at all —
and then found the one that does.

### 290a. 4xx is a fact about the RESPONSE, and the loss is a fact about the REQUEST

`ts0-ts-basic-service-request-replace-method-88h72r`: 2 963 POSTs on `ts-basic-service → ts-price-service` answer
405 after the injection, against a pre-injection mix of 304 GET and 248 POST, all 200. The injection config says
why: the fault replaces GET with POST on one route of the CALLER's outbound traffic. So the failing edge is the
caller's doing while every count lands on the callee.

The proposed observable fails on both ends: `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` injects 4xx AT the callee, where the same
status means the opposite, and `HTTPRequestReplacePath` injects no status of its own (it gets a 404 from a route
that never existed — also 4xx). The status class cannot separate "you sent garbage" from "I answered garbage".

What does separate them is on the request: `span_name` for all 2 963 rejected calls is
`POST /api/v1/priceservice/prices/{routeId}/{trainType}`, a `(route, method)` pair that **never occurs on that edge
before the injection**. A callee that broke fails the shapes it always served; a caller that corrupted its request
mints one it never served.

### 290b. The flow becomes a 2×2, and the new cell is measured but not credited

`knownIn` / `knownOut` / `novelIn` / `novelOut`, with
`unexplained = max(0, knownIn + novelOut − knownOut)` under the shipped `'shape'` reading and
`max(0, knownIn + novelIn − knownOut − novelOut)` under `'counts'` — which is §289's rule exactly. The switch
changes the READING, never the measurement, so the two arms are ablatable on one cache; that is why `novelIn` is
carried even though nothing credits it.

Novelty is set membership against the same edge's pre-injection shapes, never a threshold, and it is refused
outright for an edge that has no pre-injection observation: an absent baseline is not an empty one.

### 290c. The census: 98 % of the evidence is about the two families it was built for

Five raw datapacks per family: the two request-corruption families carry 106–7 099 novel failures each, and
`response-replace-code`, `response-replace-body`, `response-abort`, `exception`, `container-kill`, `corrupt`,
`partition`, `pod-failure`, `loss`, `delay` and `stress` carry **zero** in 42 of 42 sampled cases. On the corpus:
203 of 1 422 cases carry any novel rise; 206 216 of the 210 681 novel counts (98 %) are in
`HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` and `HTTPRequestReplacePath`.

The residue is the honest cost: `JVMReturn` contributes 3 359 novel counts in three cases, because a corrupted
return value can reach a URL path and mint a route the edge never carried. 1.6 % of the novel mass, and the reason
the default is not flipped on this measurement.

### 290d. The measurement: zero losses on the full corpus

| arm                                |     Top@1 |          % |  gains | losses |
| ---------------------------------- | --------: | ---------: | -----: | -----: |
| shipped                            |     1 073 |     75.457 |      — |      — |
| `attribution=counts` (§289's rule) |     1 138 |     80.028 |     67 |  **2** |
| `attribution=shape`                | **1 141** | **80.239** | **68** |  **0** |

The counts arm reproduces §289's dispatched readback exactly through a locally re-cut cache (1 073 → 1 138, 67
gains, the same two losses), which is what makes the third row comparable rather than a second experiment. Top@5
is 1 249 in all three arms: the pass only reorders adjacent pairs, and it never moved a case out of the top five.

The two losses (`…food-service-request-replace-method-rq29d8`, `…route-plan-service-request-replace-method-d7vdmg`)
are both repaired, and one path-replacement case is gained that the counts reading never reached
(`ts9-ts-route-plan-service-request-replace-path-9dg8qf`). Twelve of the 68 gains are on the same family, and all
twelve survive, so the change is not a trade between families.

### 290e. The pass still ships off, for a reason that is now operational

The converter changed, so no released cache matches this checkout's digest and a dispatch would be refused by its
own provenance gate. Promotion is: cut a cache (`AgentiX-E/rcabench-data`'s `build-cache.yml`, which clones this
repository and stamps the digest into the manifest), dispatch one readback that must reproduce 1 141 at
`failure_containment=1`, then flip `DEFAULT_FAILURE_CONTAINMENT`. Until the third step the arm is **+68/0 on 1 422
cases with a cache rebuild between it and the default**. (The workflow was named `cache-datasets.yml` here, which is
the RCAEval JSON cache — the wrong owner, and the correction is recorded rather than silently rewritten.) All three
steps are now done and the default has moved; §291f records the cache, the readback and what the flip cost the suite.

### Axes this closes

- **"Split the failed calls by status class."** Refuted — 4xx is produced by both ends of the edge; the same 405
  is a caller's bad request or a callee's injected response code (§290a).
- **"A count is a complete account of a failure."** False — a count says an edge failed, not who wrote the
  request. The 2×2 is the smallest object that keeps both facts, and the second one costs one column in the
  converter (§290b).
- **"The two losses need a guard on the rule."** False — they needed a missing premise in the MEASUREMENT. The
  rule is unchanged; only which cell of the flow it credits (§290d).
- **"A model-free engine cannot read intent."** Partly true, and enough: it does not read intent, it reads whether
  this edge has ever carried this request before (§290c).

## §291 — The far misses are the direction channel's refusals, and no bar repairs them

§290 closed the two request-corruption losses by giving the failure flow a KIND of evidence. What it did not touch is
the population the flow cannot reach at all: the cases whose truth sits outside the top five. This entry reads that
population from a dump of EVERY candidate rather than from the reported five, and it is the same control run §11.4
of `docs/containment-order.md` reports (1 073 of 1 422, 75.457 %).

### 291a. Candidate generation is not the defect — every truth is in the pool

| bucket     | cases | share      |
| ---------- | ----- | ---------- |
| rank 1     | 1 073 | 75.46 %    |
| rank 2–5   | 176   | 12.38 %    |
| rank 6–19  | 59    | 4.15 %     |
| rank ≥ 20  | 114   | 8.02 %     |
| **absent** | **0** | **0.00 %** |

The far tail had been carried in the working notes as a CANDIDATE-GENERATION problem — a truth the pool never
retrieved. The dump refutes it: `absent` is zero, so no wider pool can move a case, and all 114 are a scoring
question.

### 291b. They are flat fields, and flatness is what the margin bar measures

Median top-1 lead: **0.0765** among the far cases against **0.6277** over the corpus. 90.4 % of far cases have a lead
under 0.30 (30.8 % of the corpus), 100 % under 0.90. The `margin` statistic `lead / w` is therefore inside its bar on
every one of them, which is why the counterfactuals in 291d track that bar.

### 291c. The direction channel is refused on 78.3 % of the corpus, and it knew

Three populations, classified from each case's own dump:

| population                                      | cases     | share      |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------- |
| no subject measured (inert for an input reason) | 200       | 14.1 %     |
| admitted and paid                               | 108       | 7.6 %      |
| **measured, then refused by the gate**          | **1 114** | **78.3 %** |

- **86 of the 114 far misses are in the third row**, and the two families that carry the far tail are refused on
  every case: `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` 46 of 46, `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` 32 of 32.
- **852 of the 1 114 carry the TRUTH's own measured slope**, usually at 1.0 — the channel's maximum.

The gate reads the rank-1 candidate's dominant metric label and inbound latency rise (`admitsFailedEdgeTerm`), and the
term it gates exists to overturn that candidate. When rank 1 is a victim — what a propagation-carrying fault produces
— the gate measures the victim and withholds the only instrument that could demote it. `docs/failed-edge-gate.md` §13
carries the tables.

### 291d. Every repair that fixes them breaks a family, so none ships

Offline re-scoring is exact on this arm (`score = Σ w·slope`), control 1 073:

| counterfactual                                                    | Top@1         | Δ         | consequence                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| pay the term at `w = 1` / `w = 2` everywhere                      | 1 142 / 1 143 | +69 / +70 | —                                                     |
| pay it at its configured `w = 3`                                  | 1 099         | +26       | repairs 61 response-code, breaks 18 `JVMMemoryStress` |
| `margin` bar, `w = 3`, share 0.20–0.35                            | 1 148         | +75       | rejected in §4 for nine family regressions            |
| threshold-free: pay it when the channel named exactly ONE subject | 1 120         | +47       | 64 repaired, breaks 11 `JVMMemoryStress`              |
| source caller only (the failing caller is a graph source)         | 974           | −99       | 101 repaired, 200 broken                              |
| source caller AND the margin bar, shares 0.10–0.50                | 1 093…977     | +20…−96   | worse than either half                                |
| **source caller AND exactly one measured subject**                | **1 136**     | **+63**   | **64 repaired, ONE broken**                           |

The last row is the one worth carrying forward, but it prices a rule the engine CANNOT express, and the difference
between that price and the mode's own is this entry's finding.

Scored offline as a bonus paid only to the candidate the rule names, the conjunction answers **1 136 (+63)** with 64
repairs and one break — and the one break has a name, `ts2-ts-consign-service-pod-kill-476gml`, a `PodKill` where the
entry's interface failed from the load generator while the killed pod sat one hop behind it. Three relay refinements
