(all reading the promoted node's own outbound rise) return the same +63/−1, because a pod kill makes the entry STOP
calling the victim rather than call it and fail: the channel that would see it is the one that reads a call that was
never made.

Implemented as the `boundary` gate mode and run on the same corpus (`--failed-edge-gate-mode boundary`), the same rule
answers **1 094 (+21)**. The 42-case gap is not a measurement error — it is the difference between paying ONE candidate
and paying the map: `admitsFailedEdgeTerm` decides once per CASE, and an admitted case pays the term to every callee
the channel credited. On a network fault the credit set is wide, so the case-level rule admits on the one source-fed
subject and pays the victims too. `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` gains **+57**; `NetworkPartition` loses **16**,
`NetworkLoss`/`NetworkBandwidth`/`NetworkCorrupt` **8** each.

Composed with the failure-flow pass the total is **1 159 (81.505 %)** — the highest this corpus has produced, +86 over
the shipped default and +18 over containment alone — and it is still refused, with the same four network families
paying for the response-code gain.

So the axis closes on a mechanism rather than on a bar: **the gate decides per case, the payment lands per map, and
the evidence is per candidate.** Every arm in 291d loses a family because those three granularities do not match, and
the one measurement that loses none is the one the engine cannot express. The next instrument is a per-candidate
CREDIT — the qualifying callee paid and the others not, the shape `trace`'s `traceSkipsLeader` mask already
demonstrates — not a sixth bar. `boundary` ships arm-ready and off; `absolute` remains the default.

### 291e. The far cases are disconnected, not deep

`d*` as the shortest propagation path from the truth to the loudest service: 348 cases at 0 (91.38 %), 218 at 1
(72.02 %), 107 at 2 (84.11 %), 29 at 3 (82.76 %), and **720 with no path at all (67.22 %), which contain 107 of the
114 far misses**. So this engine's weak cell is not the deep chain the 2026 agentic studies lose at
(`arXiv:2608.21310` reports 88.2–96.8 % at `d* = 2..5` for its strongest arm); it is the half of the corpus where the
candidate the engine promotes is in a different component from the cause. Half the corpus having no path is also why
the two depth profiles are not presented as a comparison.

### 291f. The promotion: the cache, the readback, and the default

§290e left the pass one dispatch away, and the dispatch was blocked by a provenance gate rather than by an argument.
Both closed here, in order:

| step                                       | artefact                                                                   | evidence                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the converter the arm was measured against | `d4c3843f`                                                                 | the shape split's second column (§290b)                                                                                                                                               |
| the shard cache cut from it                | `rcabench-data` run `43806078620`, release **`rcabench-shape-v1`**         | `build-cache.yml` clones this repository and stamps the digest into the manifest, so the gate resolves                                                                                |
| the readback                               | `fse26-benchmark` run `43818561923`, `ranking_knobs=failure_containment=1` | **Top@1 = 80.2 %**, `Cases = 1422`, `Top@3 = 86.4`, `Top@5 = 87.8`, `loadErrors=0 engineErrors=0 emptyGraphs=0`, `[guard] boundary placeable=1422/1422 injectTime=1422 **noSplit=0**` |

The readback reproduced the local arm to the case count — 1 141 — which is the condition §290e named, and the guard
row is the part that makes the reproduction mean something: `noSplit=0` says the shape column was present on every
case, so the arm was not measured on a cache that had silently reverted to the counts reading.

**The default was then re-measured as the default.** Run `43826481420` is a BARE dispatch — no `ranking_knobs`, no
`shard_tag`, every input empty — and it reports `Top@1 = 80.2%`, `Cases = 1422`, `Top@5 = 87.8`,
`loadErrors=0 engineErrors=0 emptyGraphs=0`, `[guard] placeable=1422/1422 injectTime=1422 noSplit=0`, with the config
line carrying `failedEdgeWeight=3 … failureContainment=true`. That is the difference between "the flag measures 1 141"
and "the engine measures 1 141 when nobody passes a flag": the first is an arm, the second is the product, and only
the second is what a reader who clones this repository gets. The same run also reports the population the pass can
reach at all — `failed edges in 1222/1422 cases (4805 records, 4805 in-graph)` — so 200 cases contribute no
failed-edge evidence by construction and the term is silent on them rather than refused.

**`DEFAULT_FAILURE_CONTAINMENT` is now `true`.** 1 073 → 1 141 on 1 422 cases (75.457 % → 80.239 %), thirteen
families gain and none loses (§11.4 of `docs/containment-order.md`), and the one degenerate conduit the iteration-289
guard could not remove is refused by the shape rule rather than by a threshold. `failure_containment=0` remains
dispatchable and is now the ablation, which is what the +68 is measured against — the pole did not disappear when it
became the minority reading.

Three consequences that are structural rather than numeric, and all three were found by the suite rather than
reasoned from the source:

- **Six tests encoded the old default**, and each was rewritten to assert the promotion instead of the value it lost:
  the constant, the engine's own omitted-option ranking (which must equal the explicit `true` arm and not the
  explicit `false` one), the golden nine-cell pin, the term's neutrality at weight 0, the gate's fail-closed case,
  and the report line's `failureContainment=` token.
- **The neutrality fence moved.** "At weight 0 the failed-edge field is unobservable" was true of the TERM and is now
  false of the ENGINE, because the flow reads the same rows for a different reason. The fence is asserted at the
  flow-off pole, and the shipped default is asserted to differ in ORDER while staying bit-identical in SCORE —
  which is the sharper statement, because it stops a future rescoring inside the flow from hiding behind a
  reordering.
- **The Law-34 red pole became two switches.** The golden nine-cell fence needs `{failedEdgeWeight: 0,
failureContainment: false}` to move `RE2-TT`; either switch alone leaves the cell at its pinned value, because the
  flow promotes the same callee the term does. A pole that lowered only the weight would have gone green while
  asserting nothing, so the test now asserts each half's own inertness and the pair cannot become decoration.

### Axes this closes

- **"The far misses need a bigger candidate pool."** Refuted — the truth is in the pool in 1 422 of 1 422 cases
  (§291a).
- **"The margin bar is a tuning away from shipping."** No — it is +75 and it loses nine families; the bar's
  statistic is a share of the term's own span, so it cannot tell a genuinely close pair from a saturated base term
  (§291d).
- **"A threshold-free rule escapes the trade."** No — paying the term when the channel named exactly one subject
  repairs 64 and breaks 17, `JVMMemoryStress` again (§291d).
- **"The depth profile is where this engine loses."** False — it loses where there is no profile to draw, on the
  720 cases whose symptom is topologically unrelated to the cause (§291e).
- **"A better bar would let the direction term speak without cost."** False, and the reason is granularity rather
  than the bar: the decision is per case, the payment per map, the evidence per candidate. The conjunction that
  loses ONE case offline loses four network families once implemented, because an admitted case pays every callee
  it credited (§291d). The axis is a per-candidate CREDIT, not a sixth bar.
- **Two independent confirmations of §290's direction.** A 2026 trajectory study of ten agent frameworks attributes
  **86 %** of its strongest arm's wrong answers to reading the failure direction backwards, and **42 %** to trusting
  the loudest signal (§13.6 of `docs/failed-edge-gate.md`). Those are the two mechanisms §290 and this entry measure
  as arithmetic.

---

## §293 — The containment order ships, because evidence is cheaper than a better rule

Iteration 292 ended with the shipped default confirmed on a runner (1 141 / 1 422, 80.239 %) and the term axis
closed by H1's refusal. The pass this register has carried as "implemented, measured, shipped OFF" was therefore
re-read **at that default**, which §4 and §287b had never done: both arms on record were measured against the
1 073 control, before iteration 291 promoted the failure flow.

### The three arms, read locally on the released corpus

All seven shards of `rcabench-shape-v1` were verified against the manifest (`converterDigest`
`sha256:b7fca80e…`, 1 422 cases) and every arm below is a full-corpus run whose per-case verdict file is the
reading — not a suite line.

| arm     | interface requirement         |            Top@1 |   Δ | gains | losses |
| ------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------: | --: | ----: | -----: |
| shipped | —                             | 1 141 (80.239 %) |   — |     — |      — |
| A       | none (§4's rule)              | 1 174 (82.560 %) | +33 |    38 |  **5** |
| B       | ledger rows                   | 1 156 (81.294 %) | +15 |    15 |  **0** |
| C       | raw rows (`failedInterfaces`) | 1 156 (81.294 %) | +15 |    15 |  **0** |

Arm A reproduces §287b's mechanism at the new default and with the same five losses, which are a single signature:
**each one is a pair whose interface carried no failed call at all** (0 records in all five). Requiring the record
removes all five and costs 23 of the 38 gains.

### Why the requirement costs what it costs

The screen that priced the requirement is a quantity over a **finished ranking** — 32 of the 38 gains sit on a pair
that did fail. The pass is a **sequence**: one adjacent sweep, so refusing a pair changes what the next comparison
sees, and a gain whose first inversion needed a blocked pair never happens. That is the third instance in this
register of a screening statistic and an in-engine readback disagreeing, and the disagreement is always the same
shape — the screen re-scores, the engine re-orders.

### Why the smaller number ships

+33 with five losses fails the standing gate; +15 with zero clears it and gains in seven families:

`NetworkPartition` +6, `NetworkLoss` +2, `NetworkBandwidth` +2, `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` +2,
`HTTPRequestDelay` +1, `HTTPResponseDelay` +1, `NetworkCorrupt` +1, every other family 0.

`DEFAULT_CONTAINMENT_ORDER` is therefore `true`: 1 141 → 1 156, **80.239 % → 81.294 %**. The pass is inert without a
profile (which is why no golden cell can move) and inert on a case with no failed-call channel.

### Two measurement-surface defects this iteration had to fix to state any of it

- **A docblock that named the opposite of its constant.** `fse26-cli.ts` said "Ships OFF … this docblock said 'ships
  ON' until iteration 289" while the constant was `false`; the census test caught the mirror-image failure this
  iteration, a declaration asserting a ship-ON option is off. The rule the census enforces — a docblock must read
  the constant, not remember it — is what made the flip a two-line change instead of an argument.
- **An anchor that would have rolled in silence.** The golden nine-cell digest moved (`b449caf9b96e` →
  `617935621cbc`) because `signals:` names `containmentOrder` from the constant. No reading moved, and the note in
  `sota-comparison.md` §0p says what would falsify that: a cell that moves on the push-triggered battery.

### Axes this closes

- **"The five losses need a discriminator, not a threshold."** They needed **evidence**: every one of them is a
  pair nothing failed on. The discriminator was already in the case.
- **"The pass is worth more than the gate costs."** Measured and refused: +33/−5 against +15/−0. The gate's 18 lost
  gains are the price of a rule that can be stated in one sentence.
- **"The ledger's rows and the case's rows are the same evidence."** No, but on this corpus they select the same
  pairs — B and C agree case for case — because what decides is the sweep's sequence, not the map's breadth.

### What is not established

- **Whether a per-case requirement keeps more.** It would keep 4 of the 5 losses (those cases do carry failing
  rows elsewhere), so it is a worse rule by the standing gate; it was not run to a full arm.
- **Why 23 gains need an unimpeached first inversion.** The mechanism is the sweep, but no test here separates "the
  blocked pair was the only path" from "the blocked pair changed a later comparison's winner".

## §294 — A rate over no cases was being published as a rate of zero

Iteration 293 shipped the containment order and pushed `73dc662`. The RCAEval workflow on that commit
(`43901259774`) reached the RE3 cells with an exhausted Zhipu balance: every alignment call answered `429
Insufficient balance`, all thirty cases of each cell failed to load on it, and the run printed

```
║ Micro-Kinetic       | AC@1   |   0.0% ║
```

with an empty denominator — four rows, in the published table format, over no cases — then exited 0. The run's
own status therefore said nothing, and the workflow's status said the wrong thing: it ended in **failure**, and
not because of the zeros. The dashboard's `Post summary` step aborted with `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY upload aborted,
supports content up to a size of 1024k, got 1048k` — it pasted three whole console transcripts into a file GitHub
caps at 1 MB. So the colour of the one workflow that produces the nine cells was decided by the size of its
transcript, which is the same defect one level up: an artifact reporting a quantity that is not the measurement.

This entry is not about the quota. It is about the four defects that let a supplier's billing state reach a
published reading — and about a fifth thing, the workflow colour, which was decided by a markdown size limit and
therefore carried no information about any of them. None of the four needs the supplier to be down to be wrong. The
mechanism, the four cell verdicts and the provider policy are in `measurement-integrity.md`; what follows is what
it cost and what it closes.

### The guard asked the wrong question

`if (stats.considered === 0) { … continue; }`, and `considered` counts the cases the loader was **asked for**.
It was thirty, so the guard whose purpose is to stop an empty cell from being reported is the guard that let it
be reported. The two populations are different questions:

| name        | counted by                                        | answers                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `requested` | `LoadStats.considered`, summed over memory slices | which cases the dispatch asked for            |
| `evaluated` | `Σ RunResult.totalCases`                          | which cases the scorer produced a verdict for |

`cell-population.ts` now owns the decision, with four states rather than two, because they call for different
responses: nothing selected (change the dispatch), corpus/provider failure (restore the provider), a silent drop
with no load error (a loader bug, and it says so), and measured.

### The empty population became a zero

`buildMetricRows` computed `average = present.length === 0 ? 0 : …`, so a cell with no fault types — which is
what an all-failed cell produces — rendered `0.0 %` four times. The unit test in `rcaeval-metric-rows.test.ts`
asserted exactly that (`rows.every((r) => r.average === 0)`), which is the third time in this register that the
test asserting a defect is what preserved it. `average` is `number | null` now, and the printer renders `N/A`;
the absence is unrepresentable as a rate at the type level, so a printer that wants to publish one has to say
what it means.

An unmeasured cell prints counts, a reason and no percentage, and the run exits **3** (1 is what an exception
returns; "the measurement could not be taken" is a different event from "the runner threw"). Partial coverage
still prints a table, with `coverage: 28/30 cases reached the scorer (93.3%)` beside it — a rate over 28 cases
is a real rate over a stated population, and folding it into either extreme would be the same error in the
opposite direction.

### The provider was discovered to be unavailable fourteen minutes in

`semantic-preflight.ts` asks one question before the corpus walk: two texts in, two vectors out. Two, because
"the call did not throw" is not the question — `embed([])` returns `{ vectors: [] }` without a request, and a
provider that answers without embedding anything would otherwise pass a probe that only looked for exceptions.

On a refusal the policy is explicit, and it defaults to refusing:

| `BENCHMARK_EMBEDDING_FALLBACK` | behaviour                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| unset / `abort` (default)      | throw before any case is read, naming provider, reason and way out; exit 1                          |
| `local`                        | substitute the in-process TF-IDF provider, print a `DEGRADED` banner, change the configuration line |

An unrecognised value is refused rather than defaulted, on the anomaly-knob rule: this policy decides whether a
run measures the published configuration, so a typo must not silently pick either arm.

### A colour decided by a markdown size limit

The failure above is its own defect and it was fixed in the same commit. `Post summary` now routes all three
transcripts through one `emit` helper with a 300 000-byte section budget: a section under budget is pasted whole,
a section over it is cut and SAYS so with its true size, and the total is bounded by construction (3 × 300 000
against 1 024 KB) rather than by remembering a number. `step-summary-budget.test.ts` asserts the bound, the
presence of the truncation notice, the three fallback lines, and that no artifact path reaches `cat` again — the
last one because `cat artifacts/… >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is exactly what a future edit would restore, reading as
the obvious implementation.

### The attribution hole the repair exposed

The aligner adds edges for every service the YAML registry does not name; those edges are ranking input; and a
TF-IDF-embedded run and an `embedding-3`-embedded run are therefore different experiments — while their
artifacts were **identical in every field a reader could see**. The configuration string gained a third line,
`topology: yaml-v2 + semantic(<backend>)`, rendered once and interpolated into both the banner and the
`diagnose_dump` header, on the same rule `corpus:` already follows.

The anchor digest does **not** roll (`617935621cbc`): `configDigest` hashes the `signals:` line by definition,
and this is not a signal. What the digest does not cover is printed verbatim in the same artifact. The narrow
hole that remains is stated rather than papered over: a digest-keyed comparison cannot tell a degraded artifact
from an API-embedded one by digest alone, so a baseline should not be recorded from a degraded run.

### Axes this closes

- **"A 0.0 % cell means the engine failed there."** It means the cell failed, and the two are now different
  lines in the log and different exit codes.
- **"The provider can be assumed available."** It is asked, before the work, with a check that reads the answer
  rather than the absence of an exception.
- **"The embedding backend is not a configuration field."** It moves the graph, so it is on the configuration
  line, and a substituted run says so above every number it prints.

### What this does not establish

- **Whether the quota comes back.** Restoring it is the only thing that restores an API-embedded nine-cell
  reading; until then the workflow fails at the probe in about a minute instead of producing fourteen minutes of
  corrupted numbers, and that red is the honest state.
- **That the red is a dead end.** It is not, but the way out is deliberately narrow and deliberate. A repository
  variable — `BENCHMARK_EMBEDDING_FALLBACK = local` — substitutes the in-process provider, and the run that
  results says `DEGRADED` above every number, carries the backend on its configuration line, and is refused
  against the anchor by its own report. Unset is the strict arm; an unrecognised value is refused. It is a
  variable rather than a 26th dispatch input because `workflow_dispatch` stops at 25 and all 25 are fenced —
  `diagnose_decimals` alone by five tests, every one of them closing the same hole of an option the runner
  accepts and no dispatch can state. The variable is also the only channel that reaches a **push**: the nine
  cells are produced by pushes touching `packages/*/src/**`, and a dispatch input cannot be passed to those.
  What this does not establish is that a degraded reading is worth taking — it is not, for anything that will be
  compared with `81.294 %`.
- **That the measurement is reproducible by a reader.** It is not, while it depends on a supplier's balance. The
  permanent fix is a cached embedding provider — a decorator over `IEmbeddingProvider` serving vectors keyed by
  `(modelId, text-hash)` — which is cheap here because the embedded population is the aligner's service ids and
  descriptor queries, a few hundred strings per system, not free text. It needs one successful run to populate,
  so it follows a recharge rather than substituting for one.
- **That no other runner has this defect.** `run-fse26.ts` was checked for it and does not have the shape: it
  carries no `considered`-style guard, reads a local corpus with no provider, and fails a case rather than
  dropping it. What was NOT checked is whether its per-cell denominator differs from its per-cell population in
  some other way — the question is cheap and it has not been asked there, which is a different statement from
  "it is clean".

## §295 — Two runs of one corpus walk, and the population ρ needs

§294 ended with a red workflow and a declared way out. The two commits after it close the two holes that
remained: the workflow had no `concurrency:` block, and the containment sweep kept no record of the pairs it
examined.

### One corpus walk at a time

Every other workflow in this repository declares a `concurrency:` group. `benchmark-rcaeval.yml` did not, and the
consequences are not cosmetic:

- **The budget is shared.** Two overlapping runs spend the embedding account twice for one reading. Run
  43901259774 exhausted it mid-walk and published four `0.0 %` cells; a second run started on top of it makes
  that more likely, not less.
- **The artifact is decided by finishing order.** Both runs deploy to Pages with `force_orphan: true`, so which
  run's nine cells a reader sees is whichever finished last — and a `DEGRADED` run and a strict run differ in no
  field Pages displays.

The group is declared with **`cancel-in-progress: false`**, the opposite of `ci.yml`'s setting and deliberately
so. Cancelling a run twenty minutes into a corpus walk discards the reading it would have produced along with the
tokens it spent; queuing costs wall-clock and nothing else, and the pending slot keeps only the newest commit,
which is the one whose cells anyone wants.

### The population ρ needs

H2 (the iteration-294 pre-registration, in the internal docs repository) is the factorisation residual on a
call edge. It could not be computed from any
artifact this repository writes: ρ is a property of an **edge**, and its population is the set of adjacent pairs
the sweep examined with a call edge between them — a set the ranking ndjson cannot reconstruct, because a pair
that was never inverted leaves no trace in the order.

`inspectContainmentOrder` returns the order and one row per adjacent pair that carried a call edge, with four
decisions rather than one `refused` (`inverted`, `no-failed-interface`, `unmeasured`, `not-larger`) and with the
excursions recorded on refusals too — a refusal is a negative example, and the five losses the interface
requirement removed were exactly refusals. `applyContainmentOrder` is now `.order` of it, so the observation
cannot drift from the decision. `docs/containment-order.md` §13 carries the table and the two asserted
properties (an unmeasured side is absent rather than zero; a pair with no call edge produces no row).

### What the account did while this was being written

The quota came back: the run on `f9546a9` reached all three suites with `semantic enhancement (API embedding,
network)`, no `429`, no `DEGRADED`, and produced

| cell               |   AC@1 |
| ------------------ | -----: |
| RE1 OnlineBoutique | 90.4 % |
| RE1 SockShop       | 95.2 % |
| RE1 TrainTicket    | 90.4 % |
| RE3 OnlineBoutique | 91.1 % |
| RE3 SockShop       | 79.6 % |
| RE3 TrainTicket    | 74.5 % |

The preflight did not have to fire, and that is the point of having built it: the same commit would have produced
four `0.0 %` rows a day earlier. What the restore does **not** establish is that the instrument is now
reproducible — the dependency is still a supplier's balance, and the cached-embedding decorator §294 named
remains unbuilt.

### Axes this closes

- **"Two runs cannot interfere."** They share a budget and a Pages deployment; one of them is now queued.
- **"The sweep's decisions are only its output."** It keeps its reasons, and the refusals carry as much
  information as the inversions.

## §296 — A concurrency block protects the NEXT run, not the one already going

§295 added `concurrency:` with `cancel-in-progress: false` to stop two corpus walks from sharing the embedding
budget. Pushing it demonstrated the limit of the mechanism within the same minute: run `43974549448` (on
`78dd3b0`, the commit that declares the block) started while run `43966895574` (on `f9546a9`, which declares
nothing) was still in its ablation phase, and **both walked the corpus at once**.

GitHub applies a concurrency group to runs _created after_ the declaration. A run already in flight cannot be
retroactively grouped, and no syntax changes that. So the block's first real effect is on the second push after
it lands, and the change that introduces it is precisely the one it cannot protect.

The test in `benchmark-rcaeval-trigger.test.ts` asserts the declaration — a group, and `cancel-in-progress:
false` rather than `true`. It cannot assert that the declaration had an effect on a run that began before it
existed, and this entry is the record of that gap rather than a claim that the gap is closed.

### What was done about it, and why that way

Two overlapping walks spend the budget twice for one reading, so one of them had to go, and the choice was not
symmetric:

| run           | what it still owed                                                                                  | what it had already produced                 |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `43966895574` | the three ablation arms (exploration)                                                               | all nine cells, 666 / 666 against the anchor |
| `43974549448` | all nine cells, on a tree that now routes `applyContainmentOrder` through `inspectContainmentOrder` | nothing yet                                  |

`43966895574` was cancelled. The cells it had already produced are the anchor reproduction; the ablation arms are
re-runnable by dispatch (`scopes=ablation`) and are exploration rather than gates. `43974549448` is the run that
answers the question this iteration actually owes — whether an instrument change moved a cell — and it is the one
that would have been lost.

### The run this protected, read back

`43974549448` finished its three golden jobs green, and the nine cells are the committed anchor cell for cell:

| cell               | `f9546a9` (before the refactor) | `78dd3b0` (after it) |  anchor |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------: | -------------------: | ------: |
| RE1:OnlineBoutique |                             113 |                  113 |     113 |
| RE1:SockShop       |                             119 |                  119 |     119 |
| RE1:TrainTicket    |                             113 |                  113 |     113 |
| RE2:OnlineBoutique |                              84 |                   84 |      84 |
| RE2:SockShop       |                              89 |                   89 |      89 |
| RE2:TrainTicket    |                              76 |                   76 |      76 |
| RE3:OnlineBoutique |                              26 |                   26 |      26 |
| RE3:SockShop       |                              24 |                   24 |      24 |
| RE3:TrainTicket    |                              22 |                   22 |      22 |
| **total**          |                         **666** |              **666** | **666** |

Two independent walks on either side of `d1c41a6` — the commit that routed `applyContainmentOrder` through
`inspectContainmentOrder` — reproduce the anchor exactly. The refactor that added the edge population is therefore
behaviourally invisible, which is what an instrument change has to be: an observation port that moved a cell would
be a ranking change wearing a measurement's clothes.

This is the check the cancellation above was made to buy, and it is the only number in this entry that was
purchased rather than assumed.

### Axes this closes

- **"Declaring a concurrency group makes overlapping runs impossible."** It makes the next overlap impossible.
  A declaration is not a state.
- **"The regression check is free."** It costs a full nine-cell walk, and when two are queued the choice between
  them is a judgement about which one's absence is affordable — recorded here rather than made silently.

## §297 — ρ is bounded by the marginals, so the gate has to be read beside φ

§295 produced the rows H2 needs and stopped there. This entry adds the artifact that carries them out of a run,
and it records a property of the statistic that was derivable before any corpus was read — which is why it is
written here rather than discovered after a gate came back low.

### The instrument

`run-fse26.ts --containment-out` writes one line per case: the fusion order's top-1, both arms' top-1, the
published top-1, a **replay verdict**, and two separate pair traces. Three design points, each of which was a
defect waiting to happen:

| decision                                                                           | why                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the sweep's input is re-derived by a second pruner with both relational passes OFF | `analyze` applies the containment pass and then the flow pass, so the published ranking is two transformations past the fusion order the sweep actually saw                     |
| the two arms are stored as two traces                                              | once one arm inverts a pair the other refused, the scans are looking at different adjacencies; zipping rows by index would attach a decision to a pair it was never taken about |
| the replay is written, not asserted                                                | `differs` is a statement about the instrument — the rows describe something other than the decision — and a run that threw would delete the evidence                            |

`--containment-depth` defaults to 5, the depth every number in §4 and §12 was measured at. A depth of 1 is refused
by name: it carries no adjacent pair, so the artifact would publish an empty population that reads as "the sweep
examined nothing".

### The ceiling, derived

δa and δb are Bernoulli indicators, so

    ρ = P(δa ∧ δb) − pq  and  P(δa ∧ δb) ≤ min(p, q)
    ⇒ ρ ≤ min(p, q) − pq = min(p(1−q), q(1−p))

| marginals | perfectly co-moving joint |     ρ |
| --------- | ------------------------- | ----: |
| 0.5, 0.5  | 0.5                       |  0.25 |
| 0.9, 0.9  | 0.9                       |  0.09 |
| 1.0, 1.0  | 1.0                       | **0** |

An edge whose two ends are out of band in every observation therefore scores **zero** on the pre-registered
statistic, and an edge that moved together half the time scores the maximum. The estimator's ranking is partly a
ranking of where the marginals sit.

`φ = ρ / √(p(1−p)q(1−q))` removes the ceiling (it is the Pearson correlation of the two indicators) and is `null`
at a degenerate marginal. It is printed beside ρ in the same report and on the same population, and **it does not
decide H2**: a hypothesis is judged by the number it fixed. What it buys is that a separation ρ loses to its own
scale is visible without a second corpus walk.

The two do not dominate each other, which is why both are printed: on an edge whose two ends never leave their
bands, ρ reads 0 and φ is undefined, so φ's population is SMALLER on exactly the edges that carry no signal. A
report that printed only φ would drop those labels rather than score them as failures to discriminate.

### Refusals

- A population below 10 observations yields no residual (`1/√n` at n = 10 is already 0.32; below it the estimate
  cannot be told from zero).
- A pair with an unmeasured side contributes nothing — `0` is "inside the band", absent is "not measured", and only
  the first is counted.
- A case is labelled only when the arm inverted **exactly one** pair and the answer moved. Several inversions are
  `ambiguous`, counted beside the thin-population cases rather than merged with them: one is a rule problem, the
  other a corpus problem.
- An empty row file exits **3**. A population that cannot separate the two classes is a finding and exits 0.

### Axes this closes

- **"The residual is a measure of coupling."** It is a covariance with a marginal-dependent ceiling; on the
  highest-marginal edges — the ones most likely to be true propagation — it is zero by construction.
- **"A hypothesis written in advance is a hypothesis that cannot be wrong about its own instrument."** H2 fixed ρ
  and, in doing so, fixed an estimator whose ceiling had not been computed. The ceiling is now in the record, and
  the pre-registered number still decides.

### The first readback, and the population the statistic needs

Run `43993982158` read 1 422 cases and returned **every residual zero** and an AUC of exactly `0.5`. The
population was "the pairs the arm inverted", and on that population the residual is identically zero:

    inversion requires excursion(lower) > excursion(upper)  ⇒  p_lower = 1
    ⇒  ρ = p_upper − p_upper·1 = 0

The pre-registration says "every adjacent pair the containment sweep considers", so the restriction was an
implementation error rather than a hypothesis failing. Over the examined pairs, on the same artifact:

| arm     | edges | obs | n ≥ 10 | gains | losses |     AUC(ρ) |
| ------- | ----: | --: | -----: | ----: | -----: | ---------: |
| ungated |    64 | 809 |     16 |    45 |      3 | **0.8611** |
| gated   |    64 | 786 |     16 |    41 |      0 |        N/A |

Two qualifications are part of the number and not footnotes to it. `AUC = 0.8611` is computed over **two**
negative cases, so the statistic moves in steps of `1/72` and one loss placed one position earlier reads `0.75` —
the criterion is met and not established. And the population was changed after a null was seen; the justification
is that the pre-registration already fixed the examined pairs, which is checkable, but a reader who counts it as
one tuning step is not being unreasonable. Both numbers stay in the record.

The second criterion — `ρ > 0` as the gate, at +15 / −0 and Top@1 > 1 156 — is **not measured**, and cannot be
measured on a single corpus walk: a case that contributes to an edge's residual and is then judged by it is a
leak rather than a prior, so the gate has to be fitted on one half and read on the other.

### Axes this closes

- **"An observation port is a neutral instrument."** This one was neutral and still produced a null, because the
  population it observed was defined by the same condition the statistic is monotone in.
- **"A pre-registered statistic is a pre-registered measurement."** The words fixed the population; the code did
  not follow them, and the first reading was a constant.

## §298 — A gate changes the walk, so the artifact has to carry its input

§297 closed with the second criterion unmeasured and a reason: a case that contributes to an edge's residual
cannot be judged by it. This entry builds the arm that measures it — cross-fitted, replayable from the dump alone
— and it does so because the pre-registration's own falsifier fired, not because it was the next item on a list.

### The falsifier, and who it indicted

The docs repository’s pre-registration for 296 fixed H2b (the within-case residual over time slices) before any
data and wrote: "If the
readback of iteration 295 shows that the cross-case population is **not** thin … then the honest move is to run
H2's gate first and to hold this arm". The readback put **36 of 38** labelled inversions on edges at `n ≥ 10`. The
document named its own replacement, and the replacement is what got built.

### Three decisions, each one a defect avoided

| decision                                                            | what it prevents                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the row carries the sweep's INPUT (`chain`), not only its decisions | a gate changes which pairs are inverted, which changes the adjacencies examined next; a re-decision over recorded rows reports a corpus the gate never saw      |
| four arms — `off`, `ungated`, `shipped`, `prior`                    | `off` and `ungated` are one line apart and a mechanism apart; a baseline that inverted pairs credits the gate with the fusion's own decisions                   |
| the prior is consulted LAST in the sweep                            | asked first, it labels pairs the measurements already refused, and the count of blocked inversions — the gate's price — inflates with refusals it never reached |

The `chain` field is omitted rather than nulled on an older dump, so "predates the field" and "empty" stay apart.
With it, an arm nobody has run is a local computation over one artifact, and the run's own `replay` verdict becomes
checkable by a reader who never ran the corpus.

### Six decisions, and why two of them are two

`inspectContainmentOrder` now reports `prior-absent` as well as `prior-below`. They are different statements: an
edge nobody fitted is not an edge measured to be independent. The first implementation filtered the prior map at
fit time, which made a measured `ρ = −0.14` indistinguishable from a measurement that never happened — and the
gate reported **14 refusals, all `prior-absent`**, on a corpus where every one of them was a fitted negative. The
map now keeps every fitted residual and the threshold does the refusing, which is what lets the sweep say which
happened.

The threshold is `0` and the comparison is strict, for the reason the margin is zero: `ρ = 0` is exactly the
independence the mechanism claims a propagating pair departs from.

### The shipped row is an instrument check

The report prints three arms, and the second one is a check: the shipped arm, walked from the same chain, must
reproduce the corpus's published number. If it does not, the dump is missing an input and the residual row beneath
it describes a walk the run never took — so that case is `unmeasured` and exits **3**, beside the two other
refusals (no rows carry a chain; only some do). A measured `pass` or `fail` stays exit **0**, because a refused
hypothesis is not broken code.

### The split

FNV-1a over the case name, low bit. Not an index into the file: the dump is in the loader's directory order, which
on this corpus groups cases by fault family, and a hash is order-independent by construction. `priorsFor` keys
each prior by the half it may be APPLIED to, so cross-fitting is enforced by the data structure rather than by a
comment. Both halves are then read together, which is what keeps the result comparable to the whole-corpus 1 156.

### Instrument coverage

`containment-gate.ts`, `containment-gate-report.ts` and `containment-replay.ts` measure at 100 % statements,
branches and functions; so do `containment-rows.ts` (98.97 % branches) and `containment-order.ts` at 100 % after
the two new decisions. The three ways a reading is refused are each asserted, as is the one that matters most: a
gate fitted on its OWN half reads the mirror image of a cross-fitted one, and the fixture is built so the two
produce different counts rather than different prose.

### Not measured

The corpus has not been read through this arm. `+15 / −0` and `Top@1 > 1 156` are the next dispatch's numbers, and
nothing in this entry is a reading of them.

### Axes this closes

- **"An artifact that records the decision is enough to price a change."** It is enough to AGGREGATE the decision
  and not enough to walk a different one; the input has to be in the file.
- **"A requirement is a predicate."** It is also a population: a prior fitted on a fraction of the corpus refuses
  edges the whole corpus could measure, and the report counts those separately from the ones it fitted and
  rejected.

## §299 — The residual requirement wins the corpus and loses the argument

Iteration 296 built the arm that asks whether REQUIRING `ρ > 0` of an edge — in place of the failed-interface
record — makes the containment pass better, and pre-registered `+15 / −0` and `Top@1 > 1 156` as the bar. Run
`44013268053` answered it, and the exact test that was supposed to make the requirement respectable was written and
checked in the same iteration. Neither part turned out the way the previous entry expected.

### The reading, and the reconstruction that licenses it

```
  rows=1422 replayable=1422 scored=1422 disagreements=0
  prior fitted-on=b applies-to=a edges=61 fitted=8 admitted=8 unfitted=53 observations=391
  prior fitted-on=a applies-to=b edges=56 fitted=9 admitted=8 unfitted=47 observations=418
  arm=fusion  top1=1141/1422
  arm=shipped top1=1156/1422 +15/-0
  arm=prior   top1=1165/1422 +27/-3
  gate decisions: inverted=198 prior-absent=43 prior-below=1 not-larger=561 unmeasured=52
  H2-gate: FAIL — 3 loss(es) against a requirement of 0
```

The shipped arm's replay reproduces the published 1 156 with **zero** disagreements over 1 422 cases, so the rows
beside it describe a walk the run took rather than a reconstruction of one. That check was the reason the row
carries its own input (§15.2), and this is the first run in which it could have failed and did not.

### The number that is refused, and why refusing it is not bookkeeping

The requirement gains **27** where the interface record gains 15, loses **3** where it loses none, and ends at
**1 165**, which is 9 above the shipped arm and the best of the three. Nine of its gains are cases the interface
record also fixes; **eighteen it does not reach at all**. The criterion refuses it, and the entry does not move the
criterion after reading the tally: `losses ≤ 0` was written before the number existed, and a bar that is
renegotiated by the result it judges is not a bar.

The three losses are one edge and one mechanism, and in all three the correct answer was already first:

| case                                                   | fold | fused / shipped head  | prior head            | inversion                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---- | --------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `ts1-ts-preserve-service-response-abort-fxjfws`        | a    | `ts-preserve-service` | `ts-security-service` | `ts-preserve → ts-security` |
| `ts1-ts-preserve-service-response-replace-code-qnm2bw` | b    | `ts-preserve-service` | `ts-security-service` | `ts-preserve → ts-security` |
| `ts2-ts-preserve-service-response-replace-code-glvrkq` | a    | `ts-preserve-service` | `ts-security-service` | `ts-preserve → ts-security` |

The fault is at `ts-preserve-service` in all three (`response-abort`, `response-replace-code`) and the accepted
answer is the service whose response was corrupted. Its callee moved further out of band, so the order promoted the
callee over the root — exactly the promotion the interface record refused, correctly, because no call failed on
that edge. **ρ measures co-movement and a caller and its victim co-move.** The interface record measures something
else: that a call was made and did not complete. That is why its zero is a purpose and not a coincidence, and why
18 gains do not buy the right to promote a victim over its root.

### What refused the other 44 inversions

`prior-absent=43`, `prior-below=1`. A prior fitted on half a corpus leaves 53 and 47 edges unfitted, and an unfitted
edge blocks every inversion on it. So the gate's **cost** is population — most edges are unmeasurable on the half
that would judge them — while its **price** is paid entirely on the edges it admitted. A report that printed only
`admitted` would have made the gate look selective when it was mostly starved: 8 of 8 and 8 of 9 fitted edges were
admitted on the two halves, so `ρ > 0` refused almost nothing it could measure.

### The residual is an edge constant — and the loss edge is the least constant one

Eight edges are measurable in both halves. Every one is positive in both, there are **no sign flips**, and the mean
`|ρ_a − ρ_b|` is **0.0421**. An edge-level prior is therefore a defensible object on this corpus. But the edge that
produced all three losses is the corpus's **least stable**: `0.0800` (n = 20) against `0.2178` (n = 15), `Δ = +0.1378`,
the largest of the eight. It stays positive on both halves, so "the sign must reproduce" or "the smaller half's
estimate must be positive" would not have blocked it. Instability is a warning about that edge, not a test that
separates it.

### The exact test, and the answer it gives to the obvious objection

`MIN_POPULATION = 10` was a p-value with the marginals collapsed to their worst case: at `n = 10` a balanced edge
that couples perfectly is worth `1/C(10,5) = 0.00397` and an edge whose margins sit at `0.9` is worth `0.1` at the
same coupling and can never reach significance. `benchmarks/src/containment-significance.ts` replaces it with the
hypergeometric tail `P(X ≥ bothOut)`, which **is** the permutation test in closed form rather than an approximation
of it, and with Benjamini–Hochberg at `q = 0.05` because a floor never had to count how many edges were asked.
Checked against the tea-tasting table, five hand-computed fractions, 200 000 real permutations (`z = −0.29 → −1.59`),
`scipy.stats.hypergeom.sf` over 120 random tables (max `4.7 × 10⁻¹³`) and `scipy.stats.false_discovery_control` over
60 random p-vectors (**exactly 0.0**). 100 % coverage in all four dimensions over 31 tests.

Priced against the artifact it would run on, it admits 4 of 56 edges on one half and 4 of 61 on the other, against
`ρ > 0`'s 8/8 and 8/9. And on the loss edge it splits: the prior fitted on half a reads `p = 1.37 × 10⁻¹` and
refuses it, the prior fitted on half b reads `p = 1.24 × 10⁻³`, `q = 0.019` and **admits** it. So the test blocks
**one** of the three losses and leaves the two whose granting half found the edge significant.

That is the objection answered, and it is not the answer that would have rescued the requirement. **A stricter
test does not repair a causal blind spot; it shrinks the population that pays for it.** The arm remains
pre-registered in the docs repository as `docs-repository:preregistration-297.md`, with its predicted failure and its `UNMEASURED`
falsifier) and is not built as a candidate requirement, because the thing it would be asked to fix has already been
measured.

### One artifact defect the JSON exposed

`containment-gate.json` records the prior as `"residuals": {}`. A `Map` stringifies to nothing, so the
machine-readable record keeps `fitted`/`admitted` and loses **which edges** they were — the one thing §15.2 exists to
guarantee. The reading above is unaffected, and the defect is recorded rather than patched silently, because the
artifact these numbers came from is the one that has it.

### Axes this closes

- **"A requirement that is better in aggregate is better."** `+27 / −3` nets `+24` over the fusion and `+9` over the
  shipped arm, and is still refused. The gate is a conjunction of a gain bar and a loss bar, and a net is neither.
- **"A significance test would have removed the bad edge."** Computed on the same counts: it removes one of three,
  because the edge is genuinely co-moving on the half that grants the inversion. Significance answers "is this
  edge's coupling an accident", not "is this edge's direction right".
- **"An edge's residual is a property of the edge."** Mostly true here — 8 of 8 reproduce their sign, mean
  disagreement 0.042 — and true of the loss edge too, which is why the axis was mistaken for a safe one.
- **"A population floor is a test."** It is a test with the margins thrown away, and it cannot count the edges it is
  one of.
- **"An artifact that prints the count is enough to replay it."** The counts were printed and the map was not, so
  the JSON cannot reproduce an admission from its own contents.

## §300 — The residual as a term: no slope, and the reason is distance

Iteration 298 built the shape §299 asked for — the residual spent **proportionally** instead of as a licence on
the edge — pre-registered `docs-repository:preregistration-298.md` (φ instead of ρ as the weight, λ = 1 derived
below the smallest of the three losses' gaps, the standing criterion unchanged, the whole λ sweep committed), and
measured it on the artifact that refused the gate. It was refused too, and the refusal is the more valuable half:
it says what was carrying the gate.

### The reading

```
  rows=1422 replayable=1422 disagreements=0 unordered=0
  population fusion=833 ungated=861 same-length-cases=1385
  phi fitted-on=a applies-to=b edges=56 fitted=8 positive=8 observations=406
  phi fitted-on=b applies-to=a edges=61 fitted=9 positive=9 observations=375
  transfers qualified=228 unfitted=45 paid=183 silent=0 refused=605
  arm=fusion  top1=1141
  arm=shipped top1=1156 +15/-0
  arm=prior   top1=1165 +27/-3
  arm=graded  top1=1137 +6/-10 lambda=1
  H6-term: FAIL — +6 is below the 15 the gate requires
```

The `prior` row reproduces §299's `+27 / −3` / 1 165 exactly, which is what makes the graded row beneath it
readable. The pre-registered prediction was **0 losses, 8–14 gains, Top@1 1 149–1 165**; all three are wrong.

### Why the prediction's algebra was wrong, in one paragraph

The bound `term ≤ λ` is on **one pair**: it says a callee cannot gain more than λ over the caller it shared an
edge with. It says nothing about how many candidates that gain lets it pass. A rank-3 candidate paid λ can overtake
a rank-1 candidate it never touched, and that is how ten cases were lost with no pair moving more than a point.
The pre-registration is not amended — the falsifier it wrote is the one that fired.

### The finding: precision is a function of distance, not of the statistic

| λ    | rank 2              | rank 3          | rank 4   | rank 5  |
| ---- | ------------------- | --------------- | -------- | ------- |
| 0.25 | +2 / −0             | +0 / −1         | —        | —       |
| 1    | **+4 / −0** (100 %) | +2 / −5 (29 %)  | +0 / −2  | +0 / −3 |
| 4    | +11 / −3 (79 %)     | +17 / −7 (71 %) | +0 / −11 | +0 / −9 |

Ranks 4 and 5 are **0 for 20** at every λ. Rank 2 is perfect at λ = 1. And the nodes a long lift promotes are the
corpus's downstream hubs — `ts-travel-service`, `ts-basic-service`, `ts-travel2-service` — which carry **φ = 1.000**
on their incoming edges because containment is precisely what makes a callee co-move with its caller. The term pays
most to the node that co-moves most, and that node is the furthest down the chain.

**So `+27 / −3` was not a measurement of the residual's discrimination (AUC 0.8611) — it was a measurement of the
step's constraint.** An adjacent swap can promote exactly the candidate at rank 2, and rank 2 is the only distance
at which this statistic reads 100 %. A step bounds _which pairs can move_; a term bounds only _what one pair is
worth_. The first is the load-bearing part, and nothing in §299 said so.

### The curve, and the word for it

| λ    | Top@1 | ±         | moved |
| ---- | ----: | --------- | ----: |
| 0.25 | 1 142 | +2 / −1   |    13 |
| 0.5  | 1 139 | +4 / −6   |    32 |
| 1    | 1 137 | +6 / −10  |    55 |
| 2    | 1 141 | +18 / −18 |    98 |
| 4    | 1 139 | +28 / −30 |   139 |

One-to-one over a 16-fold range. Not inert (the curve moves), not noise (the sign of its _net_ is stable), and not
a bar that was missed: **it has no slope.** A spend that buys one case for every one it sells is not a candidate
requirement at any magnitude.

### The union, priced, and why the axis is closed rather than extended

The reach table implies one more shape — the residual added to the interface record, restricted to rank 2 — and it
can be priced before it is built. An exploratory probe (labelled as such: no pre-registration, so a bound and not
a reading) over the 279 cases the fusion misses:

| λ   | both fix | shipped only | term-at-rank-2 only | union Top@1 |
| --- | -------: | -----------: | ------------------: | ----------: |
| 1   |        3 |           12 |                   1 |       1 157 |
| 4   |        9 |            6 |                   2 |       1 158 |

One case at λ = 1, two at λ = 4, in exchange for a pass that must become score-aware — giving up a documented
property of `applyContainmentOrder` for a one-case return. **The residual axis is exhausted:** as a gate it loses
the argument, as a term it has no slope, and restricted to its reliable distance it adds one case.

### The artifact defect §299 recorded, fixed here

`containment-gate.json` serialised the prior as `"residuals": {}` because `JSON.stringify` writes a `Map` as `{}`.
`gateReadingToJson` writes the entries, sorted by key so two runs of one corpus diff cleanly, and
`compareEdgeKeys` is a named comparator so its equality arm is testable at all (a `Map` cannot hold a duplicate
key, so an inlined `=== 0` arm is unreachable — and the repository's comparator census then enrols the site, which
is how the new function was caught in the first place). The fix changes artifacts written after it; the artifact
the numbers above came from is unchanged, and §299's note stands beside it.

### Axes this closes

- **"A better statistic would have made the gate work."** The statistic's discrimination (0.8611) was never the
  operative variable. What made the gate work was that a swap can only promote the runner-up.
- **"A graded version of a step is a better step."** It is a different object: a step has a move set, a term has a
  magnitude. The step's move set is what was precise.
- **"φ fixes ρ's ceiling."** It does, and it changed nothing — because the ceiling was never what failed. The
  weight was computable and correct and still bought nothing.
- **"The residual's remaining headroom can be spent."** Priced: one case. The 18 cases §299 counted are not
  reachable by a weight on an edge, at any weight.
- **"A pre-registration that predicts its own failure is the same as no pre-registration."** This one predicted
  three numbers, got all three wrong, and the record says so with the falsifier that fired named. The value was
  not in being right; it was in being wrong in a way that named the mechanism.

## §301 — The pass reading every channel: the same answer from a different measurement, and two of three predictions wrong

Iteration 299 swapped the containment pass's **measurement** while holding its **rule** fixed — the first arm on
this axis that did not price the rule again. Pre-registered in `docs-repository:preregistration-299.md` before the
corpus was read; the artifact is run `44045839933`, study job, `containment-surprise.txt`.

### 301.1 The reading

```
  rows=1422 replayable=1422 unmeasurable=0 disagreements=0 scored=1422
  moved=15 (the surprise map changes the published head)  sigma=3
  arm=fusion    top1=1141
  arm=shipped   top1=1156 +15/-0
  arm=surprise  top1=1155 +16/-2
  decisions inverted=226 no-failed-interface=552 unmeasured=0 not-larger=59
  opened    inverted=1 no-failed-interface=0 unmeasured=2 not-larger=130
  H7-surprise: FAIL — 2 loss(es) against a requirement of 0
```

The `shipped` row reproduces the corpus's published `1 156 / +15 / −0` exactly, which is the instrument check that
licenses the surprise row beneath it. `unmeasurable=0` says every one of the 1 422 chains carried the map, so this
is a whole-corpus reading and not a subset that happens to look tidy.

### 301.2 The three predictions, audited

| prediction | written before the run                                                   | measured                                                | verdict                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1          | the arm fails **on losses**, Top@1 in `[1 120, 1 150]`, `losses ≥ 8`     | failed on losses (**2**), Top@1 **1 155**               | **half wrong** — the direction held, both magnitudes did not: 1 155 is five ABOVE the band and the losses are a quarter of the floor |
| 2          | `opened` total `> 50`, dominated by `unmeasured`, `not-larger` non-empty | total **133**, `not-larger` **130**, `unmeasured` **2** | **partly wrong** — the total is right and the DOMINANT heading is the other one                                                      |
| 3          | `moved` in `[40, 120]`                                                   | `moved` **15**                                          | **wrong** — by a factor of three                                                                                                     |

The falsifier the pre-registration wrote — _"if `opened` totals 0, §289 was wrong about its own mechanism"_ — did
not fire: 133 pairs were opened. What fired instead is the prediction that said a replacement must sell the shipped
pass's cases. It did not sell them: it reached 1 155 against 1 156, one case apart, with two losses.

### 301.3 The finding: the measurements disagree about pairs and agree about the answer

Three censuses, side by side. The latency walk's totals come from the gated arm printed beside this one
(`inverted=198`, `prior-absent=43`, `prior-below=1`, `not-larger=561`, `unmeasured=52`); the 44 pairs the residual
stopped would have been inversions without it, so the shipped rule inverts **242** pairs and refuses **561** as
`not-larger` and **52** as `unmeasured`.

| census                        | latency (shipped rule) | all channels (surprise) |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------: | ----------------------: |
| pairs inverted                |                    242 |                     226 |
| refused `not-larger`          |                    561 |                      59 |
| refused `unmeasured`          |                     52 |                       0 |
| refused `no-failed-interface` |                      — |                     552 |

The two walks agree on **93** inversions and disagree on **282** (149 latency-only, 133 surprise-only). That is
59 % of the surprise arm's work being new, and the change is exactly where §289 said it would be: **561 pairs
refused for not being further out on LATENCY become 59 when every channel is read**, and 130 of them are then
inverted. Yet `moved=15` — fifteen heads out of 1 422.

**So the channel ceiling is real and it is not load-bearing at rank 1.** A pair inversion changes the published
head only when the pair is at the top of the order, and at the top of the order latency is the channel that speaks:
the caller's own response time is the metric containment is about. The 130 opened pairs live further down, where an
inversion is a rearrangement the answer never sees. That is the same lesson §17.6 taught from the residual's
distance table, measured here from the measurement's side rather than the spend's.

### 301.4 What this does and does not close

**It does not close the measurement axis.** The arm is refused — 2 losses against a requirement of 0, and
`1 155 ≤ 1 156` — but it is refused as a **replacement**, which is what it was pre-registered as. The population
that makes a union worth pricing now exists as a measurement rather than a hope: 133 pairs the shipped walk refuses,
130 of them under `not-larger`, contributing 2 losses and (with the shipped arm's own 15) a head count one short.
A union would have to be priced against exactly that, and it is the next pre-registration rather than this one.

**It closes the claim that the pass's channel family is arbitrary.** Before this, `latencyExcursions` was one
family among many with an argument and no measurement; now a second family has been run over the whole corpus, and
its verdict is that the family is worth 561 refusals and 15 heads. §289's sentence was right about the mechanism
and wrong about the size.

### 301.5 The debts this iteration sharpens

- **The margin is still `0` and still underived.** Both maps are on their own axis (band widths, nats) and
  comparable only within a case, which is what makes a strict comparison exact — but neither has an error bar, and
  now there are two of them.
- **`σ` was not swept on the surprise side.** The band sets both the fires and the rates that price them, so the
  arm's optimum could sit at a band the profile builder never considered. It is a two-dimensional sweep over
  (band, rate floor) and nothing here constrains it.
- **The 44 pairs the residual stops are inside the comparison and were never re-read.** Iteration 299 held the rule
  fixed at the shipped one; whether the surprise map and the residual interact is a third arm nobody has walked.
- **`not-larger` at 59 against 561 is a ratio, not a mechanism.** The next question is which channels produce those
  130 pairs, and this artifact does not carry the per-channel contributions — it carries the maximum only.

## §302 — The record read at case scope: the silence was never the constraint, and the axis closes at 15 of 21

Iteration 300 split one absence into two statements. Pre-registered in `docs-repository:preregistration-300.md`
before the corpus was read. The artifact is run `44113097089`, study job, `containment-veto.txt`; the first attempt
(`44101598335`) measured a conjunction and is recorded in §302.1 rather than discarded.

### 302.1 The first reading was not a reading of the arm

```
  arm=shipped   top1=1156 +15/-0
  arm=veto      top1=1150 +9/-0
  decisions inverted=99 record-silent=11 no-failed-interface=458 unmeasured=12 not-larger=238 prior-absent=20
```

A case-scoped walk is a **relaxation** of the edge-scoped one: every pair the shipped walk inverts, it inverts too.
An arm that is a relaxation came out six cases **below** the arm it relaxes, with zero losses against the fusion —
which is arithmetically possible and mechanistically impossible. The census said which: `prior-absent=20` on pairs
the record had already licensed.

`inspectContainmentOrder` consulted `prior` after the record check, so a licensed pair was also asked whether its
two ends co-move — §299's conjunction, reintroduced in a narrower scope where it read as diligence. The condition
is `!licensed` now.

That `inverted=99` was **not** evidence of the defect is worth stating: the shipped walk's own inversion count is
never printed anywhere (§19.8), so there was no control to compare it against, and the comparison this entry first
wanted to make was against a _derived_ 242 that assumed a shared cascade. The evidence that carried was the
relaxation argument and `prior-absent`, and both were on the artifact.

### 302.2 The corrected reading

```
  rows=1422 replayable=1422 scored=1422 disagreements=0 record-free=200
  arm=fusion    top1=1141
  arm=shipped   top1=1156 +15/-0
  arm=veto      top1=1156 +15/-0
  decisions inverted=117 record-silent=11 no-failed-interface=458 unmeasured=12 not-larger=238 prior-absent=2
  ceiling at-second=43 reachable=21 unreachable=22 shipped=15 veto=15
  H8-veto: FAIL — Top@1 1156 does not exceed the shipped 1156
```

`unmeasurable` is not printed by this arm because its chain is the dump's own: 1 422 of 1 422 rows carry it, and
`disagreements=0` says the shipped replay reproduces the recorded top-1 on every one. The control is a control.

Eleven pairs were inverted on silence and **no published head moved**. The arm is exactly the shipped arm.

### 302.3 Why — and it is not about the record

Of the 263 adjacent pairs inside the 200 record-free cases, **238 (90 %) were refused by the measurement before the
residual was ever consulted**: the candidate above is further outside its own band than the callee below it. Twelve
were unmeasured, two sat on an unfitted edge, eleven qualified.

So the silence was never the constraint on this corpus. The excursion rule had already spoken in nine of every ten
pairs the record was silent about, and the one in ten it could not speak about was deep enough in the order that
inverting it changed no answer.

### 302.4 The ceiling, and why this axis is finished

| population                                          |  cases |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -----: |
| fusion misses (1 422 − 1 141)                       |    281 |
| accepted answer at position 1 of the recorded order |     43 |
| … pair physically qualifiable by the rule           | **21** |
| … converted by the shipped pass                     | **15** |
| … converted by the case-scoped pass                 | **15** |

The first two rows are a theorem, not a count: the sweep visits adjacent positions from the top and never revisits
one, so a candidate ascends **exactly one place** and only the pair at positions 0 and 1 can change the published
head. Six of the 281 misses are therefore reachable by _any_ arm on this axis beyond the shipped one, and all six
are the territory §299 priced — record exists, edge absent, residual would admit — the population that produced
three losses for eighteen gains.

**The axis is closed at 15 of 21.** Five rule arms have now been measured against it (the interface record §12, the
residual as a requirement §299, as a term §300, the channel set §301, the record's scope §302) and the first one
was already within six cases of the physical bound.

### 302.5 The pre-registered predictions, audited

| #   | written before the run                   | measured       | verdict                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `record-free` ∈ [150, 500]               | **200**        | ✅                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 2   | losses = 0                               | **0**          | ✅ — but it was never at risk: the buggy run had 0 as well, because the conjunction could only _remove_ inversions                                                                                   |
| 3   | gains ∈ [20, 32]                         | **15**         | ❌ — the arm adds nothing at all, which is the finding rather than the miss                                                                                                                          |
| 4   | `record-silent` ∈ [100, 400]             | **11**         | ❌ — by a factor of nine. The pre-registration's own hedge ("below 20 means the silent cases are mostly `not-larger`") named the cause without betting on it                                         |
| 5   | `at-second` ≈ 36, `reachable` ∈ [24, 36] | **43**, **21** | ❌ — the 36 was read off the depth report's `@2 − @1`, which counts depth in the engine's order; this counts position 1 of the CHAIN's order, and the flow pass and the candidate pool separate them |

Prediction 2's falsifier did not fire, so the axis does not close for the reason the pre-registration gave. It
closes on §302.4's bound instead, which is stronger: it does not depend on any arm being wrong.

### 302.6 What the arm's own machinery found on the way

- **A conjunction can hide behind a passing test.** `containment-order.test.ts` asserted "a requirement beside the
  interface record, not an alternative to it" as an **invariant**, for a configuration no arm had run. A green test
  can be a specification of the defect, and the only thing that catches it is an arm that runs the configuration.
- **A comparison needs the branch that cannot hide the bug.** `containment-replay.test.ts` compared the two walks
  under a prior that ADMITTED the edge; an admitting prior makes both branches agree. It uses an empty one now.
- **The control is the one arm with no census.** H2 printed the gate's, H7 the surprise's, H8 the veto's, and the
  shipped walk printed nothing. That is why §301's `242` could be quoted and was wrong. The report now prints a
  `control` row beside `decisions` — the reading above predates it, so the next dispatch is the first whose control
  census can be diffed against its arm's.
- **A relaxation has a checkable signature.** "Never loses a case the weaker rule gets right" is one line, and it
  would have fired on the first reading without knowing anything about why.

### 302.7 The two SOTA cells that were stale in our own disfavour

`createSotaLeaderboard` recorded `0.774` and `0.824` for the two cells every other entry is positioned against,
while `docs/sota-comparison.md` §0 has recorded `666/735` and `84/90` since the last re-anchor — twelve points low,
on the two numbers that decide the headline. They are written as the fractions now, and `standing-anchor.test.ts`
holds **the table** to the same anchor block it already held the document to. The join was missing, and its absence
is the whole reason a code cell could drift while every document fence stayed green.

The leaderboard also gained the four competitors it had not recorded: a general agent at **66.7 %** on the same 90
Online-Boutique cases the agent arm is read on (`arXiv:2608.25661`), the harness that beat it on the 270-case slice
(**59.0 %** averaged over four backbones), TD-RCA (**93.9 %** HR@1 on TrainTicket, `10.1109/IWQoS70441.2026.11661074`)
and eIRWR (**MRR 0.75** on 12k–25k Alibaba nodes, `arXiv:2608.08073`). The first of those is a correction rather
than an addition: `56.67 %` was the highest figure this table held for that cohort and it is not the highest
published one.

### 302.8 Axes this closes

- **"The record's silence is what stops the pass."** It stops eleven pairs out of 263 and not one answer; the
  measurement refuses nine in ten of them first.
- **"A scope change is cheaper than a statistic change, so it should be tried first."** It is cheaper and it is
  worth zero, because scope cannot reach a pair the measurement has already refused.
- **"An arm that is a relaxation can still lose."** It cannot. The first reading violated an invariant that was
  available for free.
- **"An invariant asserted in a test is an invariant of the system."** Only if some arm runs the configuration the
  test describes. This one did not for four iterations.
- **"The table and the document are regenerated from one another."** They were not joined in either direction
  that matters: the document was fenced and the code was not.

### 302.9 The control's first reading, and the number it corrects

Run `44124896064` (study job) is the first dispatch whose report prints the shipped walk's own census. It reads:

```
rows=1422 replayable=1422 scored=1422 disagreements=0 record-free=200
arm=fusion  top1=1141
arm=shipped top1=1156 +15/-0
arm=veto    top1=1156 +15/-0
decisions inverted=117 record-silent=11 no-failed-interface=458 unmeasured=12 not-larger=238 prior-absent=2 prior-below=0
control   inverted=117 record-silent=0  no-failed-interface=541 unmeasured=2  not-larger=178 prior-absent=0 prior-below=0
ceiling   at-second=43 reachable=21 unreachable=22 shipped=15 veto=15
H8-veto: FAIL — Top@1 1156 does not exceed the shipped 1156
```

Two things are worth more than the verdict.

**The 838 pairs partition exactly, in both walks.** `117 + 541 + 2 + 178 = 838` for the shipped walk and
`117 + 11 + 458 + 12 + 238 + 2 = 838` for the arm. The arm's release of the record's silence moves a pair out of
`no-failed-interface` (−83) and into four other headings: `not-larger` +60, `unmeasured` +10, `prior-absent` +2, and
the new `record-silent` +11. **Ninety per cent of the released pairs are refused by the measurement**, which is
§302.4's finding arriving through a second door: the record's silence is not what stops the pass, and releasing it
does not move the constraint to anywhere the arm can act.

**§301.3's `242` was not this walk's number, and the control says so.** That table was arithmetic on the GATED
LATENCY arm's census (`inverted=198` plus the 44 the residual stopped) read as a description of the shipped walk.
The shipped walk inverts **117** pairs and refuses **178** as `not-larger` and **2** as `unmeasured` — not 242, 561
and 52. The two walks do not share a cascade: the latency arm opens pairs the shipped rule refuses at the record,
so a count from one cannot be transplanted onto the other by addition. That is the instrument defect §302.6 named,
and this is what it cost: a number in a register that described an arm nobody had run.

**And the residual is unreachable under the shipped rule.** `prior-absent=0` and `prior-below=0` are not "the
residual agreed" — they are the residual never being asked. On the shipped scope every pair whose edge is absent
from the record is terminal (`no-failed-interface`, 541 of them), and every pair present in it carries a licence
that makes the residual's own guard inapplicable. So the residual is consulted only on the 200 record-free cases'
pairs, and there the measurement has already refused all but two. That is the structural reason §299's `prior` arm
had to REPLACE the record rather than supplement it: under the shipped rule the residual has no jurisdiction at all.

## §303 — The fleet reading is refused on a population that cannot see it, so the census is the finding

§8 of `docs/self-time-share.md` pre-registered H9 — the share read against the fleet instead of against
`[0, 1]` — with a falsifier and four auditable predictions. The arms ran; this entry is the reading, and it is
the first entry in this register whose headline is a CENSUS rather than a delta.

### 303.1 Three arms, one digest

| arm                                         | run           |         `Top@1` | per-case `md5` |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------: | -------------- |
| control, `selfTimeWeight=0` (`05236ff`)     | `43828014109` | 1 141 (80.24 %) | `a201eb81…`    |
| A3, `0.05` + `absolute` (mechanism control) | `44134531473` |           1 141 | `a201eb81…`    |
| A1, `0.05` + `fleet`                        | `44134503641` |           1 141 | `a201eb81…`    |
| A2, `0.2` + `fleet`                         | `44134518256` |           1 141 | `a201eb81…`    |

The digest is the same digest, so the identity is artifact-level, not percentage-level: 1 422 rows, candidate
for candidate, same order. An eight-fold weight increase between A1 and A2 moved nothing.

### 303.2 The falsifier fired, and its second sentence did not

§8 committed the axis to closure if both fleet points landed at or below the control. They did, and the axis
closes **on FSE'26**. But the falsifier also committed to a diagnosis — "the share, in either reading, is not
the statistic that decides this ranking" — and that sentence is not readable off this run:

```
[self-time] services=71105 withLatency=0 (0.0%) withLevel=0 (0.0%) undecided=0 scored=0 (0.0%)
            measuredZero=0 channelsRefusedShort=0 channelsRefusedIdle=0
```

`withLatency=0` over 71 105 services, with all three refusal counters at 0, says the term was never handed a
channel — not that the channels were refused and not that the levels came out flat. `isLatencyMetric` gates on
`label.startsWith('latency')` and this corpus's converter writes no such prefix, so the map is empty on every
case and the weight multiplied nothing, four times, at two weights and two scopes.

**The two sentences a `Top@1` column cannot separate are now separate, and only one of them is true here.** "The
normalisation is silent on this corpus" is NOT ESTABLISHED — nothing was normalised — while "the map was never
built" is ESTABLISHED on every service in the population. This is the register's own law from §6 of the share
document applied to the REFERENCE instead of to the statistic: an absence is not a measured zero, and a tie
between two unobservable arms is not a comparison between them.

### 303.3 The four predictions, audited

| #   | pre-registered                                                            | outcome                                                  |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | A3 loses cases (the §6 mechanism is direction-blind on leaf-heavy graphs) | **NOT REALISED** — a term with no map cannot lose a case |
