| 2   | A2 moves strictly more than A1, both directions                           | **NOT REALISED** — both move zero                        |
| 3   | Residual ABSENT for most candidates on the 14- and ~10-service graphs     | **NOT TESTED** — there is no residual                    |
| 4   | Gains are win-the-CALLER cases; losses are leaf-among-moved-leaves        | **NOT TESTED**                                           |

Two failed and two were never reached, and the failure is informative in one direction only: it is evidence
about the arm's **reach**, not about its theory. The pre-registration is left as written. Rewriting it into a
retrodiction would have cost the one thing the ladder bought — the knowledge that a single point at `0.05`
would have produced "0.05 is not enough", a sentence about a weight measured on nothing.

### 303.4 What the corpus actually contains, and what it does not

The census was added because of this arm and it earns its place on the first reading. On FSE'26 the self-time
term has **no population**: the corpus supplies metric channels without the `latency` prefix, so the
`levels.size === 0` return is the term's entire life on all 1 422 cases. Every future arm on this statistic has
to run where the channel exists — RCAEval's nine cells — and a dispatch here will keep returning one digest
however many weights it is given.

That is the closing fact, and it is narrower than §8's falsifier anticipated. The share is not refused because
it failed to price transport; it is refused, on this population, because the population cannot see it. §6's
refusal on the golden nine cells stands as the only measured judgement of the statistic, and it stands
unchanged.

## §304 — The stability statistic's resolution was destroyed one stage upstream, not by the rank

Iteration 301 measured 163 misses whose truth outscores the winner on exactly one term — `stability` — and closed
with an arithmetic problem rather than an answer: one rank step on a 49-candidate case is `1/48 = 0.0208` while the
median winner-truth gap is `0.53`, so the rank needs a multiplier near **×350** to close it, and `×160` already
loses 65 cases. `docs/stability-dispersion.md` is the design record for the repair; this entry is what the repair
found on the way, because the finding changed the design before any arm ran.

### 304.1 The second defect, and it is not the rank

The pre-registration was written against `breakdown.cv`. That field is not a dispersion:

```
cvBonus = cv > 0.5 ? min(cv, 1.5) × anomalyCvWeight : 0        anomalyCvWeight ships at 0.05
```

Three transformations before the rank ever sees it — **hard-zeroed** below `cv = 0.5`, **saturated** above
`cv = 1.5`, and **scaled into a band `0.05` wide** in between. So the rank is ordering a quantity whose resolution
was destroyed one stage earlier, and a residual standardised _inside_ that band would have standardised the three
transformations rather than the node. The 163 cases would have stayed lost, and the arm would have reported "the
residual does not help" about a statistic that was never handed the raw quantity.

`AnomalyFeatures.dominantMetric.dispersionCv` now carries the raw `σ/μ` beside the bonus, and
`computeDispersionResiduals` reads it **or nothing** — no fallback to `breakdown.cv`, because a statistic that
silently mixed a compressed value with an uncompressed one would be two statistics under one name.

This is the third time in this register that a term's apparent failure was a SCALE question one level down: §6 of
`self-time-share.md` refused an absolute share against an unseen fleet, §303 found a term with no population at
all, and this one finds a statistic reading a pre-compressed input. The pattern is worth naming: **before
concluding that a statistic cannot separate, check what it was handed.**

### 304.2 The binning key, corrected by arithmetic rather than by taste

The pre-registration first said "peers = candidates whose dominant metric LABEL is the same". A case carries **50
services against 85–87 distinct labels**, so an exact-label bin averages **0.59 members** and almost every node
would be alone in its family — the term ABSENT **by construction**, which is the failure mode §6 of
`self-time-share.md` taught us to name before dispatching rather than after. The key is the metric **family**: the
label's first two dot-separated segments (`k8s.pod`, `jvm.memory`, `container.cpu`, `db.client`, `http.server`), or
the whole name below that. `k8s.pod.memory.rss` and `k8s.deployment.desired` must not share a reference even though
both begin with `k8s`, because their `cv` distributions do not live on one scale.

The correction is recorded **in the pre-registration**, not in a commit message: a key chosen after the reading is
a key chosen after the reading, and this one was chosen before it, from the corpus's own two numbers.

### 304.3 What ships, and what is measured

`stabilityScope: 'rank' | 'fleet' | 'fleet_unbinned'`, shipped at `'rank'` — the statistic every published number
was taken with. At `stabilityWeight = 0` every scope is bit-identical by construction; at the shipped `0.007352`
under `'rank'`, the new field is never read. `fleet_unbinned` is a member rather than a boolean because the
mechanism control has to be dispatchable: it prices the FAMILY KEY, which is the part of the design that costs
something (binning makes the term ABSENT far more often). If it matches `fleet`, the key is refuted while the
residual stands.

`DispersionCensus` counts what the pass could see from the same loop that writes the scores — `services`,
`measured`, `families`, `singletonFamilies`, `scored`, and `absent` decomposed into `peerShort` and `zeroMad` — so
"the reference was too thin" and "the reference had no spread" are different readings rather than one refusal.

The arms and the falsifier are in `docs-repository:preregistration-302.md`; their readings belong to §6 of
`docs/stability-dispersion.md`, which is empty until they exist.

## §305 — The dispersion residual loses 411 cases at the weight that was supposed to let it be felt

Four arms, one commit (`1c11c41`), FSE'26 RCABench on all 1 422 cases. The control reproduces the published
bare-dispatch reading exactly, so the deltas below are same-commit deltas and not remembered ones.

| arm     | dispatch                           | Top@1            | Top@3 | Top@5 | saved | broke | net      |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | -------- |
| control | `stability_weight=0`               | 1 141 **80.24%** | 1 228 | 1 249 | —     | —     | —        |
| A1      | `scope=fleet, weight=0.1`          | 730 **51.34%**   | 1 045 | 1 123 | 19    | 430   | **−411** |
| A2      | `scope=fleet, weight=0.4`          | 270 **18.99%**   | 603   | 782   | 12    | 883   | **−871** |
| A3      | `scope=fleet_unbinned, weight=0.1` | 1 112 **78.20%** | 1 230 | 1 256 | 21    | 50    | **−29**  |

Runs `44210815387`, `44210819354`, `44210824103`, `44210828265`. The full reading, the prediction audit and the
`Top@3`/`Top@5` asymmetry live in `stability-dispersion.md` §6; this entry records the closure and the three defects
the closure exposes.

### 305.1 The lever is the measurement a weight table hides

| arm               | top-1s changed | breakages installing a candidate the control ranked outside its top-5 |
| ----------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A1 `fleet 0.1`    | **449**        | 340 / 430 = **79.1%**                                                 |
| A2 `fleet 0.4`    | **895**        | 790 / 883 = **89.5%**                                                 |
| A3 `unbinned 0.1` | **71**         | 11 / 50 = **22.0%**                                                   |

At the same weight the family-binned residual moves **6.3×** as many decisions as the unbinned one, and four of
every five of its breakages install a service the rest of the engine had ranked sixth or worse. The term was never
a perturbation on this ranking: **it was the ranking.** A3, at the same weight, is a perturbation — 78% of its
breakages are `rank1 ↔ rank2` swaps — which is why it loses 29 cases instead of 411 while _gaining_ 7 at `Top@5`.

The criterion's second clause (zero regressed families) is nowhere near satisfied and is measured separately: of the
`25` fault families A1 improves **1** and regresses **22**, A2 improves **0** and regresses **22**, A3 improves **2**
and regresses **12** — and A1's single improved family is `DNSRandom`, a family with **one case in the corpus**.

### 305.2 The residual has information; the standardisation has no portable scale

`A2` puts the term in charge of 89.5% of the decisions it touches, so its `18.99%` is as close as this artifact
gets to the residual's standalone top-1 rate — far above the `~5%` a random order over 20–50 candidates scores, and
61 points below the composite. So the closure is **not** "`cv` carries no order information". It is:

```
fleet      : peers share units  →  cv values cluster  →  MAD → 0  →  residual → ±10²   (valid, unbounded)
unbinned   : peers mix units    →  MAD is cross-family →  residual ~ O(1)              (bounded, invalid)
```

Validity and scale are **the same fact about the choice of reference**, and the pre-registration argued only
validity. It anchored the weight at `0.1` by comparing it to the base term's `1` — an anchor on the weight axis,
never on the product axis — and then predicted that a quantity with "no ceiling" would gain more at `0.4`. The
quantity with no ceiling did move more; it moved the ranking. A MAD-standardised residual is a **significance**
statistic, and multiplying a `t`-like number by a weight calibrated for bounded shares is a unit error.

### 305.3 The falsifier fired, and its second sentence is false

The pre-registered clause — "if both fleet points are at or below the control, the axis closes **as a class**" —
is satisfied (`51.34%`, `18.99%`, both under `80.24%`), so the axis closes and no third transform of `cv` is
dispatched under this pre-registration. The sentence attached to that clause — "not 'this residual is wrong' but
'the dispersion statistic, in either reading, is not what decides these rankings'" — is refuted by the same
artifacts: the term decided **449** rankings at `0.1` and **895** at `0.4`.

This is §303's defect a second time, which makes it a pattern rather than an accident: **a compound falsifier
yields one measured verdict and one unmeasured sentence, and the sentence is the one a later reader quotes.** From
this entry forward a falsifier states one clause, and any mechanism claim it wants to make gets its own entry with
its own artifact.

### 305.4 Three pre-registration defects, named so the next one does not repeat them

1. **An unmeasured anchor.** "`0.1`, an order of magnitude below the base term's `1`" compares two numbers on
   different axes. The quantity that had to be anchored is `weight × residual`, and its typical magnitude was never
   measured before the ladder was chosen — the one measurement this iteration could have taken offline and did not.
2. **A bucket that cannot be populated.** Prediction 3 said the losses would sit on cases whose node is alone in
   its metric family, "ABSENT and therefore inert rather than wrong". The guard that makes the term absent is the
   same guard that removes it from the sum, so that bucket produces **no losses by construction**. Inert and wrong
   are not two regions of one axis; they are mutually exclusive by the code.
3. **An argument about validity used to predict a magnitude.** Prediction 4 ordered A3's regressed-family count
   _behind_ A1's "because unbinned peers mix families whose `cv` distributions do not overlap". That is a
   distributional claim producing a scale prediction, and the artifacts reverse it (`50` against `430`) for the
   reason in §305.2. Mixing families is what _bounds_ the residual.

### 305.5 What is closed, what stays open

Closed **as a class**: the dispersion statistic as a ranking term, at any weight on the ladder, under either
reading. Rejected on the primary statistic, both fleet points, no golden half read (the criterion is an AND and the
FSE'26 half failed first), so `stabilityScope = 'fleet' | 'fleet_unbinned'` ships **unreachable by default** and
keeps its tests as the record of what was tried.

Not closed, and now specified: a **bounded** squash of the same residual (`tanh`, or a clip at three MADs), whose
weight would mean "the largest contribution this term can add" and would therefore be portable across the binning
key. It is a third transform of `cv`, so this pre-registration forbids dispatching it; it also is not what the
falsifier prescribes next — the 11 bucket-C cases, whose truth leads on **nothing** and which no re-weighting of an
existing term can reach. Order of work: bucket-C audit first, then a fresh pre-registration for the bounded form
with its weight stated in _contribution_ units and that magnitude measured **before** the arm.

Also open, as an instrument defect rather than a finding: the promised count of the 163 stability-singleton cases
that flip was **not** produced, because iteration 301's term dump — which carried the bucket-A labels — was not
retained. An artifact that is thrown away cannot be re-read, and this is the second time in three iterations a
census had to be rebuilt from the corpus for that reason.

## §306 — The depth ladder closes at 49, and three attempts to beat the ranking were noise

| record          | what it measures                                                                     | artifact                                 | cost                                       |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `rank-depth.md` | ladder to 49, the permutation, the gap calibration, three refusals, the corpus count | `--depth-out` + `--terms-dump` + one A/B | 15 m 29 s + 14 m 5 s, **zero model calls** |

`benchmarks/src/ranking-depth.ts` has measured the per-case depth since iteration 262 and
`docs/agentic-headroom.md` §10 quoted its `@20` rung as the reachable ceiling. What it could not do is close: the
ladder ran to `20` and the orders run to `49`, so `absent` meant "not in the first twenty" and the `7.9 %` left
over at `@20` could not be attributed to "ranked too low" or to "not ranked". `DEPTH_TOP_LIMIT` now runs to `50`
and the ladder carries `25, 30, 40, 50`.

### 306.1 Every answer is inside the order

| K     | 1       | 2       | 3       | 5       | 10      | 12      | 20      | 25      | 30      | 40      | 45           |
| ----- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------- | ------------ |
| cases | 1 141   | 1 190   | 1 228   | 1 249   | 1 278   | 1 287   | 1 310   | 1 327   | 1 345   | 1 400   | **1 422**    |
| share | 80.24 % | 83.68 % | 86.36 % | 87.83 % | 89.87 % | 90.51 % | 92.12 % | 93.32 % | 94.59 % | 98.45 % | **100.00 %** |

**`absent = 0` on all 1 422 cases.** The truth is at rank `45` at the worst, in orders of up to `50`, so no re-ranking at any width is
blocked by a missing candidate: the 281 misses are orderings, and every rung below `94.59 %` is a **presentation**
choice. What stays true is that the `87.83 %` in `agentic-layer-plan.md` §6 is the **elimination** ceiling and is
correct as one; the clause after it omitted its own width, and the width is `maxCandidates`, a flag accepting `[1, 50]`.

### 306.2 The two relational passes are worth +68, confined to rank 1

| K          | 1     | 2     | 3     | 5     | 10    | 20    | 30    |
| ---------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| engine     | 1 141 | 1 190 | 1 228 | 1 249 | 1 278 | 1 310 | 1 345 |
| score-only | 1 073 | 1 184 | 1 227 | 1 249 | 1 278 | 1 310 | 1 344 |

`terms-dump.ts` already recorded the `+68`. That it is **confined to the first position** is new, and it is the
finding: a contribution that lives entirely in the ordering of the first two plots is a **direction** statement
(which endpoint is the source), not a **magnitude** one, which is the opposite of what a term can be — a term is
affine in its weight and the weight axis is a measured plateau (`stability-dispersion.md` §6, `+8/1 422`). The
apparatus's measured contribution and its shipped form agree.

### 306.3 The score gap is a calibration curve, and the smallest-gap band is a twin

| gap      | `[0,.005)` | `[.005,.01)` | `[.01,.02)` | `[.02,.05)` | `[.05,.1)` | `[.1,.3)` | `[.3,∞)`   |
| -------- | ---------- | ------------ | ----------- | ----------- | ---------- | --------- | ---------- |
| cases    | 9          | 18           | 76          | 93          | 95         | 372       | 759        |
| accuracy | 44.4 %     | 27.8 %       | **14.5 %**  | 52.7 %      | 74.7 %     | 73.4 %    | **95.9 %** |

`gap ≥ 0.3` is 759 cases (53.4 % of the corpus) at 95.9 %. `gap < 0.02` is 103 cases — **7.2 % of the corpus
holding 83 of the 281 misses, 29.5 % of them** — at 19.4 %, and the `[0.01, 0.02)` band alone scores 14.5 %.

The band has a mechanism. In those 103 cases the truth is first in 20, **second in 9**, **third in 18**: twice as
often third as second. A small gap is not the engine hesitating between a cause and a near-cause — it is scoring
**two nodes of one shape** alike while the answer lies behind both. Swapping the top two scores 8.7 % against the
19.4 % already achieved, which refutes the obvious repair for free and says the repair must add evidence rather
than reshape the tie.

### 306.4 The failure-flow channel, refused three ways

On the 173 cases outside the top five, ordering by `failedEdge` alone puts the truth first in **78 (45 %)** against
the composite's 0 by construction; as a complete order it scores **676/1 422 (47.54 %, −465)**, and its
jurisdiction form (re-order only the stratum the term measured, the pattern `emission` ships with) scores `−186`.
A gated switch to it is `+54` tuned on all 1 422 and **+4 / +5** tuned on one half and read on the other, against a
bootstrap 95 % interval of `[+6, +21]` on the full-corpus optimum: fifty cases of fit, four of signal.
Single-channel recall over the same cases is not ranking power — `temporal` holds 148 of 173 in its top 20 and
scores **44/1 422** as an order. The information exists in several channels and **no single channel orders it**.

### 306.5 The shape attribution survives the A/B it had never been given

`failureAttribution = 'shape'` shipped on a **cost** argument ("identical where there is no evidence"), never on a
benefit. Measured where the evidence exists:

| arm               | Top@1               | cases | flips         |
| ----------------- | ------------------- | ----- | ------------- |
| `shape` (shipped) | **1 141 / 80.24 %** | 1 422 | 3 won, 0 lost |
| `counts`          | 1 138 / 80.0 %      | 1 422 | 0 won, 3 lost |

All three flips are `novel > 0` cases (two `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` at 1 487 and 2 014 novel failures, one
`HTTPRequestReplacePath` at 73) and none of the 1 219 `novel == 0` cases moves — the design claim, confirmed
exactly. An earlier reading in the same iteration pointed the other way (the 127 `ReplaceMethod` cases **with**
novelty at 66.1 % against 84.1 % for the 63 without) and is recorded so it is not re-derived: that is a difference
between **populations**, not between readings. A subgroup rate is not a counterfactual, and the mistake was made
and corrected inside one day.

### 306.6 What was repeated, and the lesson that is worth more than the reading

`rank-depth.ts` was written in this iteration as a new module before `ranking-depth.ts` was read, and it did what
the existing file already did — `firstHitDepth`, `recallLadder`, `DepthDump`, and a rung list that already reached
`20`. It was deleted rather than merged, and the reading it was built for came from the existing instrument with
one constant changed. **The repository's instruments are not discoverable from the documents that cite their
output**: `ranking-depth.ts` is named in `agentic-headroom.md`'s prose and in `benchmarks/vitest.config.ts`'s
coverage list, and in neither place is it findable by someone asking "what already measures rank depth".

Before building the next instrument: read `benchmarks/src/` and `benchmarks/vitest.config.ts`'s `include` list
first. The second lesson is the one iteration 302 learned at a different stage: **before concluding that a bound
is a property of a method, find out what measured it, at what width, and whether the width was a parameter.**

### 306.7 The corpus against its own paper

RCABench's abstract states **1 430** validated failure cases; this corpus holds **1 422** across seven category
shards (HTTP 796, Network 254, Resource 173, Pod 123, JVM 73, Time 2, DNS 1). The difference is **8 cases
(0.56 %)**, unexplained by the Zenodo record, and it moves no conclusion here. `Time` holds 2 cases and `DNS`
holds 1, so a per-family claim about either is a claim about two cases and one case.

## §307 — The pass that was on and inert, and the promotion gate that is worth nine cases

| record                      | what it measures                                                            | artifact                                                                  | cost                                        |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `containment-order.md` §20  | the silent no-op: 15 cases, 1.06 pp, and the two fields that end it         | two full 1 422-case runs, one with `--fault-free-profile` and one without | 13 m 48 s + 13 m 48 s, **zero model calls** |
| `agentic-promotion-gate.md` | where the model's ranking is worth reading, and the two defects that hid it | replay of the recorded nominations against the engine's own order         | **zero model calls**, ~4 s                  |

Both records came out of one question asked of an artifact that already existed: _why does this sandbox read
`1 141` where every document in the repository reads `1 156`?_ The answer was not a regression.

### 307.1 Fifteen cases, one missing input, and a record that could not say so

The containment order reads the fault-free profile for its per-service latency excursions. With no profile
`latencyExcursions` returns an empty map and `inspectContainmentOrder` returns the ranking **unchanged**, without
an error and without a line saying so. `fse26-run-config.ts` excluded the profile from the recorded configuration
because — in its own words — the artifact's content "is determined by the profile FILE and by the two fields that
ARE reported (`faultFreeWeight`, `faultFreeSelection`)". That is true of the fault-free _term_ and false of the
containment _order_, and with `faultFreeWeight` at its shipped `0` the term is silent, so the two runs were
byte-identical under every reported field.

|       |    with the profile |      without it |
| ----- | ------------------: | --------------: |
| Top@1 | **1 156 (81.29 %)** | 1 141 (80.24 %) |
| Top@3 |               1 228 |           1 228 |
| Top@5 |               1 249 |           1 249 |

Top@3 and Top@5 are identical to the digit and every per-channel score is bit-identical: all fifteen are
`rank 1 → rank 2` swaps. The record now carries `faultFreeProfileDigest` and `containmentExcursions`, both on
`REPORTED_CONFIG_FIELDS`' capability half, and a run in the silent state prints a warning naming the cost.

**What this cost the investigation.** Three hypotheses were held and discarded before the real cause was found —
a code regression between two commits, a CI-versus-local environment difference, and a Node or timezone
difference — and each was testable only because a full run is 14 minutes rather than an afternoon. The 1 156 was
reproduced bit-for-bit (`tests`, per-fault-type counts, guard lines) by adding one flag.

### 307.2 Two defects in my own instrument, found before the number was reported

**A relative gap divided by a leader's score.** The first version of the promotion gate conditioned on
`(s₁ − s₂) / s₁`. On this corpus the published order is **not score-sorted** — the containment pass reorders
adjacent caller/callee pairs after scoring — so on 83 of 1 422 cases the published first candidate scores below
the second and the ratio is negative; those cases are not "the engine is unsure", they are "a rule already acted".
The denominator is also unsound because the pool penalty can take a candidate's score to or below zero. The
statistic is now `(s₁ − s₂) / (s₁ − s_min)`, over the case's own spread.

**A spread taken from a truncated list.** The same rule selects 29 cases from a five-wide artifact and 122 from a
fifty-wide one. One threshold, two denominators, and the denominator was the artifact — the same class of error
§306 found one layer up, where a method ceiling turned out to be a reporting width.

### 307.3 The promotion gate, and the first positive reading from a model arm

The model's first choice is taken over the engine's only when the published pair is score-sorted **and** the top
two are within 3 % of the case's spread.

| override rule                                               |    net |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -----: |
| **the model's first choice, gated**                         | **+9** |
| the model's first choice, ungated (191 overrides)           |    −53 |
| the engine's second candidate, always                       |    −17 |
| the engine's third candidate, always                        |     −3 |
| a random candidate among the five shown (mean of 500 draws) |  −14.1 |
| … its best draw of 500                                      |     −8 |

122 cases fall in the band, the engine is wrong in 98 of them, the gate overrides 56, and 15 of those fix the case
against 6 that break it — 71.4 % precision on the overrides that change an outcome. Cross-half by case-id hash:
**+5 / +4**. Bootstrap over the cases: 95 % CI **[+1, +18]**, `P(net > 0) = 0.975`. The threshold is a plateau
rather than a spike (`0.02` → +6, `0.03` → +9, `0.05` → +7), and the optimum does **not** transfer — tuning on one
half picks a threshold that reads negative on the other — so the rule is stated as a plateau and the confirmatory
arm must pre-register a threshold.

This does not contradict `agentic-fusion.md`'s finding that no operator rescues the proposal set; it bounds it. The
model is at chance globally (1 103 against the engine's 1 156 verbatim) and well above it where the engine is nearly
undecided and no structural rule has intervened, which is a statement about _where_ to read a ranking rather than
about which operator to use.

### 307.4 The width axis, priced before it is dispatched

|                                                                    |               reading |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------: |
| width-5 ceiling (`Top@5`)                                          |       1 249 (87.83 %) |
| width-20 ceiling (`Top@20`)                                        |       1 310 (92.12 %) |
| cases a width-20 arm newly exposes (ranks 6-20)                    |                    61 |
| the model's conversion on answers it already sees at positions 2-5 | 34 of 93 = **36.6 %** |

The last row is the one that changes a decision: the information a wider list would expose is of a kind the model
already converts when it can see it, so width is not the binding constraint and the fusion is. The width arm
remains worth dispatching, but as a joint test with the gate rather than as a standalone.

### 307.5 The deep tail is a different population from the band

112 cases sit beyond rank 20 and **77 of them are two fault types** — `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` (46) and
`HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` (31), 19.9 % and 16.3 % of their families. Their answers carry a median 0.14-0.30
against a leader's 0.86: buried, not ambiguous. That is the opposite of the band in §307.3, where the ratio is
0.60 and the answer is a plausible rival. Two different failures, two different repairs, and reporting them as one
"deep tail" would have hidden both.

### 307.6 The prescription axis, and the competitor that names it

`arXiv:2610.35767` (PKU + BUPT, 2026-10-26) reports its arms as a function of the **prescribed-call ratio** and
finds the ordering monotone: simple harnesses (ratio `0`) 65-77 % `PR@1`, published agents (`0.10`-`1.00`) 16-53 %,
non-LLM methods 6-39 % with the best at 38.9 %. This project has three points on the same axis, from one system on
one corpus: elimination **−602**, nomination ungated **−53**, nomination gated **+9**. The direction is the reading
and the magnitudes are not comparable — different controls, different artifacts, and "prescription" is not one
scalar — but it makes the gate the end of a monotone trend rather than an isolated threshold, which is the best
available answer to "is +9 an artefact".

The sweep that found this also **rediscovered an entry already on file**: RCAtlas has been in
`sota-populations.md` since an earlier iteration, with three root-cause levels and a leakage audit this search did
not surface. Recording it because the failure mode is the one §307's own §8.8 names one surface over: _read what
the repository already says before writing what the web says._

## §308 — The gate reproduces at +9 on production code, and the guard around it was one candidate too strict

§307.3 measured `+9` with an analysis script. `docs-repository:preregistration-304.md` fixed the threshold at `0.03` and named four
predictions; this section is the confirmatory run, on the gate as a module (`packages/ai/src/agent/promotion.ts`,
`gatePromotion`) with a `--promotion` flag and the arm wired into `scoreNomination` so that the control and the
treatment are one loop rather than two.

### 308.1 The four predictions

| #   | as registered                                 | reading                   |
| --- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| G1  | net ≥ **+5**                                  | **+9**                    |
| G2  | both id-hash halves positive, `\|A − B\| ≤ 6` | **+5 / +4**, difference 1 |
| G3  | overrides ≤ band                              | **56 ≤ 122**              |
| G4  | end to end as `1 156 + net`, fraction printed | **1 156 → 1 165**         |

The falsifier does not fire, so the axis stays open and arm W is authorised. `docs/agentic-promotion-gate.md` §9
carries the readings and the artifact provenance; the one number that makes the replay a confirmation rather than a
second opinion is that the terms dump is **byte-identical** to the one §307 was computed from
(`md5 4b1dadd057f4b52e1b242c40c39aba19`), from a run that cost $0.00 and 15 m 52 s because it asks only the engine.

### 308.2 The defect was in the guard, and it was one candidate too strict

The first run of the confirmatory code read **band 121, engine wrong 97, `orderDisagreement` 17** — every number one
below §307's. The guard refuses to gate a case whose full order disagrees with the population's, and it compared the
whole five-candidate prefix. Seventeen cases differ, and the distribution of the first differing position is the
whole finding:

| first differing position |     1 |     2 |   3 |     4 |      5 |
| ------------------------ | ----: | ----: | --: | ----: | -----: |
| cases                    | **0** | **0** |   0 | **2** | **15** |

The gate reads `full[0]` (the answer), the pair `(full[0], full[1])` (the margin) and `min(score)` (the denominator).
Two of those three live in positions 1 and 2, and neither position ever differs. So the correct condition is
`full[0].service === engine[0]`, and the readings return to `122 / 98 / 56 / 15 / 6 / 35 / +9` — bit for bit §307's.

This is the fourth appearance of one shape in this line of work, and it is the first one where the over-strict
quantity was a **guard** rather than a statistic: §305 was a unit error, §306 was a reporting width taken for a
method ceiling, §307 was an input missing from a record. A guard that demands more agreement than the measurement
uses does not make the measurement safer; it deletes cases and reports the deletion as a smaller population.

### 308.3 Why the tails differ — a property of the terms dump, not of either writer

A structural pass permutes **adjacent pairs of the list it is handed**, so the pass over a 50-wide order and the pass
over the same run's 5-wide top five are two permutations of two different lists. They diverge exactly where a
candidate exists in one and not the other: a 50-wide order has a sixth candidate that a five-wide one cannot promote
past its fifth, and a five-wide one has a boundary the 50-wide one does not.

`terms-dump.ts` already states that the array order is the engine's answer and that the scores do not determine it.
The boundary condition this run adds is: **the array order is the engine's answer at that width.** A consumer
reading the terms dump as "the published order, longer" gets positions 1 and 2 right — which is all a margin rule
reads — and can get positions 4 and 5 wrong, which no margin rule reads.

### 308.4 What is not claimed

The `+9` is the same `+9`. A confirmation that moved the number would have refuted the earlier one, and the value of
this run is that a second implementation through a different entry point agrees to the case. It is still in-sample:
the threshold was chosen on this corpus, the halves are the only internal replication, and `81.92 %` remains
8.1 pp below the published RCABench best.

### 308.5 The gate placed in the failure decomposition, which closes its own axis to 9.7 %

`arXiv:2609.36686` decomposes a ranking's accuracy as `Top@k = Retrieval@K × Rerank@k`. That decomposition is
already an instrument here (`ranking-depth.ts` prints `Retrieval@K`) and the gate had never been placed in it. On
the artifact arm G replays:

| quantity                           |                                    reading |
| ---------------------------------- | -----------------------------------------: |
| `Retrieval@5`                      |                  `1 249 / 1 422 = 87.83 %` |
| `Rerank@1 ∣ Retrieval@5`, gate off |                  `1 156 / 1 249 = 92.55 %` |
| identity                           | `0.878340 × 0.925540 = 0.812940` = `Top@1` |
| `Rerank@1`, gate on                |                  `1 165 / 1 249 = 93.27 %` |
| reranking headroom at width 5      |                    **+93 cases, +6.54 pp** |
| the gate took                      |                        **9 of 93 = 9.7 %** |

Three consequences, and the third is the one that changes the roadmap.

1. **A perfect reranker at width 5 stops at `87.83 %`**, which is 2.17 pp below the published `90.0 %`. So the
   8.1 pp gap is two gaps: 6.54 pp reranking and 2.17 pp that no threshold, at any model quality, can buy on a
   five-wide list.
2. **The gate is 9.7 % through its own axis.** Nine of ninety-three. The remaining eighty-four are cases where the
   answer is visible at positions 2-5 and the model's first choice is wrong, and §7's `36.6 %` conversion says the
   model does convert them when it can see them — so a better _admission rule_ has room and a better _threshold_
   does not. The next lever on this axis is a verifier, not a wider band.
3. **Width crosses the published best, and the projection is now derived.** `Retrieval@20 = 92.12 %`, so holding
   `Rerank@1` at `92.55 %` gives `0.921238 × 0.925540 = 85.26 %` — the same `85.3 %` `docs-repository:preregistration-303.md`
   projected by a different route, which is the first independent confirmation of it. And a **perfect** reranker at
   width 20 reaches `92.12 %`, above the published `90.0 %`: the road is width plus reranking, not a larger
   backbone, and `Rerank@1` needs only `97.7 %` of retrieved cases to match it.

The care this needs is stated in `agentic-promotion-gate.md` §10.2 and one item is worth repeating here:
`Retrieval@50 = 100 %` on this corpus, so `92.55 %` is a conditional rate and quoting it without its denominator
would be the mistake that paper warns about.

## §309 — The width axis gets an instrument, and the instrument had two owners

`agentic-promotion-gate.md` §10 put the gate in the failure decomposition and left one number unanswered: the
ceiling at width 5 is `87.83 %`, the ceiling at width 20 is `92.12 %`, and the published best is `90.0 %`. So
"does presentation width help" is not a matter of taste — it is the difference between a road that cannot reach
the target and one that can. Answering it needs one thing this repository did not have: **an artifact holding
twenty candidates.**

### 309.1 The flag, and the property it has to have

`--fingerprint-top-k` widens the elimination fingerprint. `docs/agentic-presentation-width.md` owns it; what
belongs here is the property and the measurement of it.

The arm is differenced against arm G, whose control is `1 156 / 1 422`. A run whose published width could be
dispatched would move `Top@5` as well as the window, and then no reading of the delta would say which of the two
moved. So the flag widens the ARTIFACT: the published ranking stays `analyze(graph, 5)`, computed before the field
is read.

Verified rather than argued, by running both widths over the whole corpus and comparing the artifacts:

| artifact                    | width 5               | width 20   |
| --------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------- |
| `per-case.ndjson`           | `2778b294de9f…`       | identical  |
| `terms.ndjson`              | `4b1dadd057f4…`       | identical  |
| `results.json`              | `068d1af8d96f…`       | identical  |
| `Top@1` / `Top@3` / `Top@5` | 1 156 / 1 228 / 1 249 | identical  |
| candidates carried          | 7 110                 | **28 440** |

### 309.2 The defect: the width had a second owner, and it won silently

The first run of the widened instrument printed `requested width 20 (published 5)` and wrote **7 110 candidates
over 1 422 cases — exactly five each.** `buildCandidateFingerprints` capped at
`DEFAULT_FINGERPRINT_OPTIONS.maxCandidates = 5`, after the widest order the runner could hand it. The flag lost and
the log reported the number it had asked for.

This is §307's shape one layer down. There the missing input was a profile file the artifact could not name; here
it was a default inside the flag's own consumer. Both produced a run that reported a configuration it had not
measured, and neither produced an error.

The repair is removal rather than plumbing: the builder now carries **the order it is given**, so the width has one
owner — the caller's slice — and its test counts candidates instead of sampling them. A test asserting "the first
two of a three-candidate order are carried" passed throughout the defect's life; a test asserting the count would
not have.

### 309.3 What the widened population moves, and what it does not

The dump is the engine's answer **at that width**, and a structural pass permutes _the list it is handed_, so a
twenty-wide order is not the published five plus fifteen:

| width 5 vs width 20            |  cases |
| ------------------------------ | -----: |
| position 1 differs             |  **0** |
| position 2 differs             |  **0** |
| first difference at position 4 |      2 |
| first difference at position 5 |     15 |
| any of the first five differs  | **17** |

Seventeen in 1 422, at the same positions as the fingerprint-versus-terms discrepancy `agentic-promotion-gate.md`
§9.3 recorded. The control is untouched (`engineOrderOf` reads position 1, which never differs, and the gate-off
arm over this population reads `1 156`), and the arm's prompts are _not_ a strict superset of arm G's — on 1.2 %
of the corpus the last two visible rows are ordered differently. That is stated because a reader who assumed
otherwise would be reading a cleaner experiment than the one that ran.

### 309.4 The price, corrected before dispatch

`docs-repository:preregistration-305.md` registered `~4.0 M` prompt tokens, extrapolating the width-5 measurement
of 2 772 tokens per case. The per-case cost is not a constant: it is a function of the table, and the table is what
the flag changes.

|                               | width 5 |    width 20 |
| ----------------------------- | ------: | ----------: |
| table rows over the corpus    |  63 897 |     255 181 |
| ratio                         |       — |    **3.99** |
| projected total prompt tokens |  3.94 M | **15.74 M** |

So the arm costs about four times what was registered. The error is the one this line of work keeps making — a
quantity measured at one width applied at another — and it is recorded here rather than at the end, because the
point of pricing an arm is to be able to decline it.

### 309.5 The arm was dispatched, and the study job refused it — correctly

Run `44284042634` ran the widened instrument over the whole corpus and the study job **exited 1 at step 14**:

```
DISAGREEMENTS: 17 (first: ts0-ts-basic-service-request-abort-5dlq8r)
Refusing to score: the two artifacts are not from the same run.
```

The guard is `agentic-headroom`'s join between the fingerprint dump and `per-case.ranked`, and it is an INDEX
join: it assumes the two files describe the same order case for case. That assumption was never written down,
which is why the flag was allowed to break it. A widened order is a different order at positions 4–5 on 17 of
1 422 cases (§309.3), so the join saw two runs that never coexisted.

**The repair is a second file, not a weaker guard.** `--presentation-out` now carries the widened order and
`--fingerprint-out` goes back to being the published one, so each dump holds one contract and the join keeps its
assumption. Three tests hold the split: the parser refuses a width without the presentation dump, the width is
asserted not to appear on the engine's command line, and the census names the new flag as an artifact only a study
workflow — never a benchmark cell — may produce.

The second half of the repair is the part a reader should check. Separating the files leaves the join unable to
answer _"is this dump from the run being scored?"_, because the field it compared — the candidate array — is the
one a widening changes. So the presentation records the order the run published beside the order it presents, and
`joinHeadroom` compares THAT, in full: `published` equals `per-case.ranked` on 1 422 of 1 422 cases, and position 1
is identical on 1 422 of 1 422. A presentation whose recorded order disagrees is refused exactly as a stale
published dump is, and a shorter recorded order is refused too — two widths publish different-length orders, and a
prefix compare would accept one entry against five. The widening's own invariant is enforced where the extra rows
come from: `fingerprintSourceOrder` refuses an order that DROPS a published candidate, which is the property that
makes twenty rows a superset view rather than a different one.

The general shape is §307 and §309.2's again, at a third layer: **the earlier two failures were a decision with no
owner and a decision with two; this one was a file with two contracts.** All three produce a run that reports
something it did not measure, and none of them produces an error the run itself can see — the disagreement had to
be found by a reader that joined two artifacts.

### 309.6 What the ladder already answers, before any run

`docs/agentic-presentation-width.md` §9 turns `Retrieval@K` into a curve over the whole corpus at `$0` of API
spend, and it moves the next width arm:

|         K |     1 |     2 |     3 |     5 |    10 |    15 |    20 |    25 |    30 |    40 |    50 |
| --------: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----: |
| reachable | 1 156 | 1 192 | 1 228 | 1 249 | 1 278 | 1 294 | 1 310 | 1 327 | 1 345 | 1 400 | 1 422 |

Width 5 → 20 buys **61 cases over 15 slots** (4.1 per slot); width 30 → 40 buys **55 over 10** (5.5 per slot), which
is the shoulder of the curve and the better next arm if the axis survives at all. And the 17-case permutation does
not change this: the ladder taken over the fingerprint's own order equals the ladder taken over the fifty-wide
terms dump at every rung, and the set newly reachable between 5 and 20 is _the same 61 cases_ by identity.

## §310 — The width axis closes at 20, and it closes net-neutral rather than inert

`docs-repository:preregistration-305.md` authorised arm W (width 20, gate `0.03`) behind a single falsifier: _if its `Top@1` is at
or below arm G's, the width axis closes as a class at 20_. `44299700032` ran it on `87fcdf0`, 1 422 cases,
`deepseek-chat` asked and `deepseek-flash` served (the endpoint's own reply, as in every arm since
`docs/agentic-eliminator.md` §140), 13.95 M prompt tokens, 4 m 42 s of model time.

### 310.1 The four predictions, and the falsifier

| #   | as registered                                                            | reading                                                       | verdict                              |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| W1  | `Top@1` ≥ 1 165 + 12 = **1 177**                                         | **1 165**                                                     | **FAILS**                            |
| W2  | overrides ≤ 56 + 61 = **117**                                            | **32**                                                        | bound holds, **reason refuted**      |
| W3  | band unchanged at **122**                                                | **122**, engineWrong **98**                                   | holds — plumbing check only          |
| W4  | `promoted` rises, `agrees` falls by the same amount, `reversed` ≥ **26** | promoted **32** (arm G 56), `reversed` **14**, `agrees` 1 313 | **FAILS, in the opposite direction** |
| —   | falsifier: `Top@1` ≤ arm G's **1 165**                                   | **1 165**                                                     | **FIRES**                            |

W2 is the interesting miss. The bound was written as an upper limit and the reading is far below it, so the
prediction "passes" while the sentence justifying it — _a wider list gives the model candidates it did not have, so
it will use more of them_ — is refuted by the same number. Overrides fell by 24. A bound that holds for the opposite
of its stated reason is a prediction that should be counted as a miss, and it is counted as one here.

W3 held to the digit and could not have failed: `(s₁ − s₂)` is read from positions 1 and 2, which the widening
provably does not move, and the spread is read from the terms dump, which is byte-identical. It is recorded as a
plumbing check, which is how it was re-stated before dispatch.

### 310.2 What the null is made of

`+9 = +9` is not inertness. The 11 fixes split by where the truth sat in the published five:

| truth inside the published five                     | fixes |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----: |
| yes — at ranks 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5                     | **6** |
| **no — absent, presented at ranks 6, 9, 9, 14, 17** | **5** |

and the exchange rate is symmetric: arm G's `15 fix / 6 break` became `11 / 2`. **Five cases were answered that a
five-wide table cannot produce, and four were lost that it could**, with the model becoming more conservative
(56 → 32 overrides) and more accurate when it acted (71.4 % → 84.6 %).

The five are named in `agentic-presentation-width.md` §10.1 rather than counted, because a claim that a wider window
is reachable should be checkable case by case.

### 310.3 The mechanism, and why it is a fact about the model

The engine is untouched — the control reproduces `1 156` to the digit, and `band / engineWrong` reproduce `122 / 98`.
Everything that moved is in the model's behaviour, and the two movements point in opposite directions:

- given twenty rows, the model names the engine's leader **more** often, so the gate has fewer disagreements to
  arbitrate;
- when it does name something else, it is right more often.

The gate's admission rule is scaled to `(s₁ − s₂)`, which the model's conservatism does not change; what changed is
how many cases ever reach it. So the width did not fail to produce information — it produced it on 61 new cases and
suppressed it on the cases where a fifth row used to be enough to disagree.

This is also the direct answer to `agentic-promotion-gate.md` §10.2's open question about `Rerank@1` across widths:
it is **not** constant. At width 20 it reads `1 165 / 1 310 = 88.93 %` against `93.27 %` at width 5, and that fall is
arithmetic (same numerator, denominator +61) rather than a worse reranker.

### 310.4 What closes, and what the closure does not say

Closed, as registered: **no arm that widens `maxCandidates` is dispatched under this pre-registration, at any width
≤ 20, on this protocol.**

Not said by the closure, and worth naming so it is not over-read:

- **Not "width is worthless".** Five cases came from population only width 20 reaches. The falsifier is about the
  **net** on this protocol with this admission rule.
- **Not width 50.** `docs-repository:preregistration-305.md` wrote the falsifier at 20 on purpose, and the ladder puts the shoulder
  at `30 → 40` (+55 cases over ten slots). That is a different arm with a different cost (≈ 25 M tokens) and it is
  not authorised here.
- **Not the admission rule.** §10.1's second consequence said a better threshold has no room left and a better
  _rule_ has 84 cases of it. Arm W's census sharpens that: the rule now arbitrates 32 disagreements instead of 56,
  so a rule that is a function of the case rather than of the pair has less to arbitrate and more to gain per
  decision.

`docs-repository:preregistration-306.md` is the document that picks up from here, and its decision rule selects arm T (a
system-level topology brief) on this outcome — the falsifier fired, so the branch is fixed independently of
preference.

### 310.5 Two configuration facts the readback found, and neither is about width

Arm W's artifacts were read twice: once for the arm, and once to check that the run described the configuration
this repository believes it ships. It does not, in two ways.

**(a) The standing FSE'26 cell is anchored on a corpus two caches old.** `docs/sota-comparison.md` §0a carries
`1 073 / 1 422 = 75.46 %` from run `42729721072` at `4d0050d7`, whose manifest is `builtAt 2026-11-10`, converter
`f72899e5…` (`rcabench-pod-v1`). The push-triggered FSE'26 battery on `1c11c41` (run `44210828265`, artifact
`fse26-results`) reads **`1 112 / 1 422 = 78.20 %`** on a manifest `builtAt 2026-11-16`, converter `b7fca80e…`. The
39-case difference is **engine and corpus at once** and is NOT decomposable here: the provenance gate refuses a
cache whose converter digest does not match the checkout, so the old corpus cannot be re-run under today's engine.
It is recorded rather than re-anchored, because writing +2.74 pp into the standing table would attribute to the
engine a movement that may belong to the converter.

**(b) The containment pass is worth +44 cases when it can speak, and the published cell is the one where it
cannot.** On the _same_ manifest (`b7fca80e…`, 1 422 cases) and the same engine defaults, two workflows disagree:

| workflow                                               | profile                                                       |               Top@1 |           Top@3 |               Top@5 |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------: | --------------: | ------------------: |
| `fse26-benchmark.yml`, run `44210828265`               | **none** — the surface refuses `--fault-free-profile` by name |     1 112 (78.20 %) | 1 230 (86.50 %) | **1 256 (88.33 %)** |
| `benchmark-agentic.yml`, run `44299700032` measure job | built from the corpus in the same job                         | **1 156 (81.29 %)** | 1 228 (86.36 %) |     1 249 (87.83 %) |

So the pass concentrates answers into position 1 — **+44 at Top@1, −7 at Top@5** — which is what a pass that
permutes the list it is handed does: it swaps some answers up to the front and some out of the five. The published
cell quotes the configuration where the pass is inert, because a benchmark dispatch may not name a profile (a
dispatch that could would name a stale band, §307's rule). The **+44 is three times the +15** recorded when the
pass shipped (`docs/containment-order.md` §20), on a configuration that has since gained the pod-lifecycle channel,
the transient-guard policy and the failed-edge gate.

**This is the road item the width arm displaced, and it is cheaper than any arm**: the surface already has the
corpus and already runs the builder for nothing in the other workflow. Building the profile inside the benchmark
surface — from the corpus it just downloaded, keyed by the same digest — makes the cell the configuration the
engine actually ships, and it costs one engine run and no model calls. It is recorded here as a defect in the
published cell rather than as an arm, because that is what it is.

> **CORRECTED BY §314, and both readings above are affected.** (a) `44210828265` is not the bare dispatch on
> `1c11c41`; it is **arm A3** (§305), whose control `44210815387` is the run that reads `1 141`. There is no
> push-triggered FSE'26 battery on this workflow at all — every run of it in the archive is a `workflow_dispatch` —
> so the sentence "the push-triggered battery reads `1 112`" describes a run that does not exist and an arm that
> does. (b) The shipped configuration with the pass inert reads **1 141 (80.24 %)**, not 1 112; the repair is worth
> **+15**, not +44, and Top@3/Top@5 are identical on both sides. The defect is real and the repair is right; only
> the price was misread, and it was misread because a run id was taken from a table instead of from the artifact.

## §311 — What the model is TOLD: the topology brief, built and guarded before the arm runs

`docs-repository:preregistration-306.md`'s decision rule selected arm T on the outcome of arm W: the falsifier fired
(`1 165 ≤ 1 165`), so the width class closed and the next lever is not more rows but better evidence for the rows
already shown. This entry records the instrument — `docs/agentic-topology-brief.md` §1–§7 — and the two things it is
constructed to make impossible. The readback is a later entry, on the rule §309 and §310 established.

### 311.1 The one input the prompt lacks, and where the engine already encodes it

A prompt row carries the channels that moved, their bands, their rates and their onsets. It carries no edge. The
engine encodes edges in exactly one place — the containment pass inverts an adjacent pair only when it is a direct
call edge (`docs/containment-order.md`) — so the missing input is not a modelling opinion about what would help; it
is a quantity the system already computes and the question does not ask about.

### 311.2 Why the brief is constant over the corpus, and what that buys

A per-case rendering of "the edges among these candidates" is a per-case input, and a per-case input can carry the
answer without printing it. Auditing such a rendering would mean enumerating every function of the label it might
have learned. So the brief is the **union** graph, rendered once: one string, byte-identical for every case, asserted
over a population whose fault types, orders and labels all differ, and asserted again under a relabelling of every
case's accepted set. The guard is therefore a property of the population and not of a code review, and the digest
moves with the bytes.

### 311.3 The empty default is load-bearing

`NominationOptions.topologyBrief` defaults to `''` and the prompt is then **byte-identical** to the one every
published nomination number was measured on — the same digest, asserted against a freshly built options literal
rather than against a remembered hash. Required rather than optional, for the reason the width's second owner was
deleted (§309.2): a field a caller may omit is a caller that can silently measure the control, and "no change" is the
one result that cannot be told apart from a mistake.

### 311.4 What it costs, measured at dispatch rather than assumed

`chars × cases`, and the run prints both numbers beside the digest. The width's first pricing was wrong by 3.99×
(§309, `docs/agentic-presentation-width.md` §5) because it multiplied a per-case constant that was not constant; this
instrument's price is a function of the corpus's distinct edge count, so it too is printed rather than claimed.

### 311.5 The instrument is derived, and the falsifier says what that means

`arXiv:2609.36686` moves a reranker +7 to +18 points with a description a human wrote. A brief derived from a union
graph states structure and cannot state purpose, so a failure here refutes "the derivable part is enough" and not the
paper. The hand-written document stays open, priced separately, and needs its own provenance argument because no
dispatch can reproduce it.

### 311.6 What was repaired on the way: the two owners of the prompt options

The nomination runner built `NominationOptions` twice — once inside the proposal branch and once for the digest
check — and the two literals had to agree or every recorded answer would read as `STALE`, a report about the artifact
instead of about the build. The brief added a fourth field, i.e. a fourth chance to disagree, so the two literals are
now one object built before either use. This is §307's shape a fourth time: **a decision with two owners**, found
because a field was added to both.

## §312 — The published FSE'26 cell was measuring a configuration the engine does not ship

§310.5 recorded this as a defect in the cell rather than as an arm. It is repaired here, because it is cheaper than
any arm and because a published number that understates the engine by 3.1 pp is worse than a number that is merely
old.

### 312.1 The measurement the repair rests on

Same corpus manifest (`b7fca80e…`, 1 422 cases), same engine defaults, two workflows, and the only difference is
whether the run could supply a fault-free profile:

| workflow                        | profile               |               Top@1 | Top@3 |     Top@5 |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------: | ----: | --------: |
| `fse26-benchmark.yml`           | none                  |     1 112 (78.20 %) | 1 230 | **1 256** |
| `benchmark-agentic.yml` measure | built from the corpus | **1 156 (81.29 %)** | 1 228 |     1 249 |

> **THIS TABLE IS WRONG, AND §314 SAYS HOW.** The `none` row is not the shipped configuration. `44210828265` is
> **arm A3** of §305 — `stabilityScope=fleet_unbinned, stabilityWeight=0.1` — and it was read as a bare dispatch
> because the run id was quoted from the arm table's last row instead of from the artifact's own `Config:` line. The
> shipped configuration with the pass inert reads **1 141 (80.24 %)**, so the repair is worth **+15**, not +44, and
> Top@3/Top@5 do not move at all. The defect is recorded rather than rewritten because the reasoning that produced
> the repair does not depend on the size of the effect, and because a correction that erases its own wrong number
> is a correction a later reader cannot check.

The containment pass ships ON (`DEFAULT_CONTAINMENT_ORDER`) and reads the corpus's per-channel excursions to decide
whether an adjacent pair is inverted. **Without a profile it has nothing to read**, so the published cell was
reporting the pass as "no change" — a statement about a missing file, not about the engine. The +44 / −7 shape is
what a pass that permutes the list it is handed does: it moves answers up to the front and a few out of the five.

### 312.2 The repair, and why it is an action rather than four more steps

`fse26-benchmark.yml` now builds the profile from the corpus it just downloaded and passes it. The four steps that
did this in the agentic workflow became `.github/actions/rcabench-profile`, and **both** workflows call it, on the
rule `.github/actions/rcabench-shards` established: two copies of a guard are a guard enforced in one place and
skipped in another. A second copy of a cache-key derivation is worse than a copied guard, because a key that hits on
a changed builder publishes a stale band under a green check.

The action has exactly one input, the corpus root. Its **path is not an input at all**, which is the stronger form of
the rule that kept `faultFreeProfilePath` out of every dispatch: a caller that could place the profile could place
one fitted on another corpus, and that artifact is indistinguishable downstream from a measurement of this one. The
census's third table (`OPERATIONAL_OPTIONS_REACHABLE_FROM_NEITHER`) is therefore **empty**, and a fourth states the
replacement — reachable from a workflow, nameable by no input, and only alongside the action that derives it.

### 312.3 What the published cell will read, and why it is not re-anchored in this commit

The next push-triggered battery produces the number. Writing `81.29 %` into the standing table before that run exists
would be replacing a stale transcript with a projection, and this repository's rule for a cell is that it is quoted
from an artifact. So this entry records the instrument change, names the reading it expects, and the cell is
re-anchored by the commit that reads the run — with both figures printed, because Top@5 moves the other way.

**Both of those sentences are corrected by §314.** The run exists (`44333449830`) and it reads `1 156 / 1 422 =
81.29 %` — the prediction held to the case — but **Top@5 did not move the other way** (`1 249` before and after), and
the `+44` this entry priced the repair at is `+15`. The repair was right for the reason given here; the size of what
it buys was read off a control that was an arm.

## §313 — Arm T reads 1 166: the brief bought precision, not yield, and missed T1 by nine cases

Arm T was dispatched as `44329808264` on `b77e920` — `topology_brief=auto`, `promotion=0.03`,
`model=deepseek-chat` — and both jobs are green: the measure job derived the brief from the corpus's own call graph,
the study job asked the model on all 1 422 cases. The instrument is §311's; this entry is the reading, judged against
`docs-repository:preregistration-306.md`'s T1–T4 and its single falsifier.

### 313.1 The artifact, and the control it is differenced against

|                                 | control — arm G, no brief | arm T, brief `auto` |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------: | ------------------: |
| engine Top@1                    |                     1 156 |               1 156 |
| band (cases)                    |                       122 |             **122** |
| engine wrong inside the band    |                        98 |                  98 |
| model overrides inside the band |                        56 |              **39** |
| … fix                           |                        15 |                  12 |
| … break                         |                         6 |               **2** |
| … neutral                       |                        35 |                  25 |
| **net**                         |                    **+9** |             **+10** |
| conditional precision           |            71.4 % (15/21) |  **85.7 % (12/14)** |
| end to end                      |           1 165 (81.92 %) |  **1 166 (82.0 %)** |
| half A / half B                 |                   +5 / +4 |             +6 / +4 |

The engine side reproduces arm G's control to the case (`1 156 / 1 422`, band 122, engine-wrong 98), so the two
columns differ in one thing: whether the prompt carried the section. The brief itself is 4 050 chars (~1 013 tokens)
over 48 services and 139 call edges, digest `2826885ae00c3238`, byte-identical for all 1 422 cases — the population
guard of §311.2 printed at the point of use rather than asserted in a test.

### 313.2 T1 fails, and the falsifier does not fire, by one case

T1 asked for **≥ 1 175** (arm G + 10) and the arm read **1 166**: nine cases short. The falsifier was written as
_"if arm T's `Top@1` is at or below arm G's, the system-level-brief axis closes as a class"_, and `1 166 > 1 165`,
so **the axis stays open by exactly one case**. That is the least comfortable verdict in this register: a channel
priced at 1.44 M tokens produced a net indistinguishable from the arm without it, and the sentence that would have
closed it missed by a single case. Recording the margin rather than the verdict is the point — `docs-repository:preregistration-307.md`
fixed arm A as the next arm in **all three** of T's branches, so nothing downstream depended on this reading, which
is exactly the condition under which it can be reported without a thumb on the scale.

### 313.3 What the brief actually did: it made the model decline

T2 predicted the outcome mix would move **toward** overruling — `promoted` up, `agrees` down, `reversed` not up by
more than 10. The sign is the opposite on the one quantity the two arms share:

| inside the band, threshold 0.03 | arm G (register §4) | arm T (this artifact) |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------: | --------------------: |
| model overrides = `promoted`    |                  56 |                **39** |
| … fix                           |                  15 |                    12 |
| … break                         |                   6 |                 **2** |
| … neutral                       |                  35 |                    25 |
| conditional precision           |              71.4 % |            **85.7 %** |
| net                             |                  +9 |                   +10 |

Arm G's four counts are quoted from `agentic-promotion-gate.md` §4, which is a reading of its own artifact; arm T's
are counted from `44329808264`'s. What makes the pair comparable is the other end of each artifact: the engine reads
`1 156 / 1 422`, the band **122** and `engine wrong inside the band` **98** on both, so the gate's arithmetic and the
engine's answers are identical and the difference is the prompt. The census row names differ between the two
renderings (`promoted` versus `overrides`, `band-miss` present only in the newer one), which is why only the
band-internal counts are tabulated side by side.

Seventeen fewer overrides, four fewer breakages, three fewer fixes. So the brief's effect is **suppression with a
better hit rate on what survives**: conditional precision `71.4 % → 85.7 %`, and the breaks it prevented (4) are
worth more than the fixes it lost (3), which is the entire `+1`. The mechanism is legible in the brief's own text:
it says `A -> B` reads "A calls B" and **does not** say which end is the source (§311's refusal, on purpose), so a
model given both ends named can see that its candidate is a caller and that nothing in the row makes it the origin —
a reason to abstain, not a reason to promote. **A channel that raises precision and lowers coverage is a different
object from the one T1 priced**, and T1 priced coverage.

### 313.4 T3 and T4 hold, and they are the two that could have been defects

T3: the band is **122** and `engine wrong inside the band` is **98**, identical to arm G — the gate's denominator is
the case's own spread over the full scored order, which a prompt cannot reach. This was the falsifiable half of T3
and it is the one that would have indicted the gate rather than the brief. T4: `unknown-candidate 0`,
`duplicate-candidate 0`, `declined 0`, `unreadable 0`, `missing 0`, `refusals 0` — the arm did not win by making the
model answer more often, because it answered strictly less.

### 313.5 What it cost, measured against the same corpus at the same width

`5 420 769 + 23 866` tokens over 1 422 cases = **3 829 tokens/case**. The width-5 measurement on this same corpus is
**2 772 tokens/case mean** (`docs/agentic-presentation-width.md` §5), so the brief's marginal cost is **+1 057
tokens/case = +1.50 M tokens** over the corpus — better than a third of the prompt, and it is the only quantity here
that is a difference of two measurements rather than a projection.

`docs-repository:preregistration-306.md` priced the brief at "~300–600 tokens per case; at 1 422 cases that is 0.4–0.9 M prompt
tokens". The measured marginal cost is **1.7–3.8× the registered range**, which is §309's lesson a third time
(`docs/agentic-presentation-width.md` §5, §311.4): a cost written before the artifact is a guess about its size, and
this one guessed low for the same reason the width guessed high — the guesser reasoned about tokens per row while the
quantity is chars of a union graph whose size is the corpus's edge count.

### 313.6 The one thing arm T leaves open, and it is not a rerun at a larger length

The falsifier closed the _derived_ brief "at any length or any rendering" only on failure, and it did not fail. So a
second rendering is admissible. But the reading says the marginal information is not the missing part — 39 overrides
at 85.7 % precision means the model, when it moves, is right five times in six, and the constraint is that it moves
on 39 of the 122 cases where the engine is wrong 80 % of the time. **That is an admission-rule problem, not an
evidence problem**, and it is `docs-repository:preregistration-307.md`'s arm A: the rule that decides _when_ to overrule is reading
`relGap`, a property of the pair, while the case carries properties of its own. §313.3's 25 neutral overrides are
where that arm's headroom is, and arm T's own artifact is the corpus it runs on.

## §314 — The control was an arm, so the repair was priced at three times its worth

§312 shipped a fix and a number. The fix is right: `fse26-benchmark.yml` could not supply a fault-free profile, the
containment pass ships ON, and without a profile it returns the ranking unchanged and says nothing. The number was
wrong, and the way it was wrong is the defect this entry records.

### 314.1 What the artifact says, read from the artifact

The claim was that on one corpus manifest (`b7fca80e…`, 1 422 cases) the two workflows differ by `+44` at Top@1
because one supplies a profile. `44210828265` — quoted as "the push-triggered FSE'26 battery" — is **arm A3 of
§305**: its own `Config:` line reads `stabilityScope=fleet_unbinned stabilityWeight=0.1`. It is the last row of
§305's arm table, and it was read as the control because the run ids in that table are four lines long and the bare
dispatch was not the last of them.

| run                           | what it actually is                         | `Config:` differs from shipped in             |               Top@1 |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------: |
| `43818561923` (`44df4fa`)     | first run on this manifest                  | `containmentOrder=false`, no profile          |               1 141 |
| `44134503641`, `44141794481`  | arm A1/A2 of the self-time family           | `selfTimeWeight=0.05`, scope                  |               1 141 |
| `44141801070`                 | the same family, absolute scope             | `selfTimeWeight=0.05`                         |               1 141 |
| **`44142865215`** (`2122359`) | **the bare dispatch** — no knob differs     | only the two profile fields                   | **1 141 (80.24 %)** |
| `44210815387` (`1c11c41`)     | the stability family's `weight=0` CONTROL   | `stabilityWeight=0`                           |               1 141 |
| `44210828265` (`1c11c41`)     | **arm A3**, quoted as the control           | `stabilityWeight=0.1`, scope `fleet_unbinned` |               1 112 |
| `44333449830` (`802cf3e`)     | the shipped configuration, profile supplied | nothing                                       | **1 156 (81.29 %)** |

**The shipped configuration reads 1 141 with the pass inert and 1 156 with it speaking, on the same manifest.** That
is `+15`, and it is the same `+15` `docs/containment-order.md` §20 recorded at `73dc662` — which should have been the
first clue that `+44` was not a repair's value but an arm's damage: §305 already says A3 costs **−29**, and
`1 141 − 29 = 1 112`.

### 314.2 The case-level census, which is what makes the +15 a mechanism and not a delta

The two per-case artifacts pair on `datapack` for all 1 422 cases. Differencing them:

| shape (rank of truth: inert → profile) |  cases |
| -------------------------------------- | -----: |
| `1 → 1`, tail order differs            |     64 |
| **`2 → 1`**                            | **15** |
| `3 → 2`                                |      2 |
| lost from rank 1                       |  **0** |

So the pass moves **81 of 1 422** rankings and **no case loses a position it held**: fifteen cases gain rank 1 from
rank 2, two gain a position inside the top three, and the rest are permutations below the reported width. `Top@3` and
`Top@5` are therefore identical by construction rather than by luck — a `2 → 1` swap cannot change a top-three count,
and nothing enters or leaves the five. The fifteen are spread over seven fault types (`NetworkPartition` 6,
`HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` 2, `NetworkBandwidth` 2, `NetworkLoss` 2, and one each of three HTTP types), which is the
signature of a rule about _adjacent call edges_ rather than about a fault family.

### 314.3 The defect this is, stated as a rule

**A control is a run whose artifact says it is a control, not a run whose id a table puts in a control row.** §305
wrote the rule for deltas — "the control reproduces the published bare-dispatch reading exactly, so the deltas below
are same-commit deltas and not remembered ones" — and then this entry quoted a delta from a remembered row. Two
runs of one manifest with the _same_ engine defaults is what made §312's comparison a controlled pair; the `Config:`
line is what makes that checkable, and it took one diff of 39 fields to find that the two rows differed in two.

The published consequence is in `docs/sota-comparison.md` §0p-ix: the cell is re-anchored to **1 156 / 1 422 =
81.29 %**, the inert reading is named as **1 141**, and the `+44` is retired everywhere it was printed — the action's
header, both workflows' comments, and the census test's docblock. The repair's justification is unaffected: the
published cell was still the one where the pass was inert, and it is still the case that a dispatch could not name a
profile. **A right fix priced at three times its value is still a fix; a wrong price is still a wrong number.**

## §315 — Arm A reads 1 144: counting channels measures how much moved, not what caused it

`docs-repository:preregistration-307.md` registered the evidence-differential admission rule after arm T: admit the
model's first choice when it owns **strictly more** out-of-band channels than the leader, counting only channels
whose fault-free rate is below the case's median. A1 is the count, A2 adds "and the rarer of the two is rarer still".
This entry records the implementation (`gatePromotion`'s second mode), the two readings, and the closure.

### 315.1 The readings, on arm T's own artifact, at $0 of model spend

Both arms re-score the 1 422 nominations and fingerprints `44329808264` already holds — no dispatch, no tokens. The
control is the same run's engine answer, so every delta below is over one denominator.

| arm                   | overrides | fix | break | neutral | precision |              Top@1 |     net | half A | half B |
| --------------------- | --------: | --: | ----: | ------: | --------: | -----------------: | ------: | -----: | -----: |
| control (gate off)    |         — |   — |     — |       — |         — | **1 156 (81.3 %)** |       — |    569 |    587 |
| **A1 count**          |        63 |  13 |    25 |      25 |    34.2 % |     1 144 (80.5 %) | **−12** |    568 |    576 |
| **A2 count + rarity** |        43 |   9 |    15 |      19 |    37.5 % |     1 150 (80.9 %) |  **−6** |    570 |    580 |

Every prediction failed except the one that stated an ordering:

| prediction                                                        | registered        | measured   | verdict                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| A1-P1 `Top@1 ≥ 1 177`                                             | 1 177             | **1 144**  | fails by 33                                    |
| A1-P2 overrides `< 56` and `> 20`                                 | 21–55             | **63**     | fails — the rule is not stricter than the band |
| A1-P3 precision `≥ 80 %`                                          | 80 %              | **34.2 %** | fails at half the band's 71.4 %                |
| A1-P4 breaks `≤ 6`                                                | ≤ 6               | **25**     | fails by 19                                    |
| A2 ordering (fewer overrides, higher precision, between A1 and G) | 43 / 37.5 / 1 150 | exact      | **holds**                                      |

A2's ordering holding while every absolute claim failed is the shape of a prediction implied by the _construction_
rather than by the rule: "A2 is A1 with a narrower criterion" is true of any monotone narrowing, including one that
narrows the wrong quantity.

### 315.2 The falsifier fired, and it is the third arm in a row to lose

> "If arm A1's `Top@1` is at or below arm G's `1 165`, the evidence-differential admission class closes."

`1 144 ≤ 1 165`, so the class closes: no arm that admits on a count of out-of-band channels is dispatched under this
pre-registration, at any count or any rarity weighting. This is the third model-side arm to lose — `agentic-fusion.md`
§3–4 (mixed rankings), arm W (width, net-neutral) and now a rule over the model's own answer — and it is the first
where the loss is **not** attributable to the prompt: the nominations were arm T's, whose overrides the band admitted
at 85.7 % precision. The same 39 answers, admitted by a different rule, are worth −12.

### 315.3 Why it fails, stated as the mechanism rather than the number

The rule's census is the diagnosis. Of 1 422 cases it declines on 22 ties and 44 where the pick is _behind_, and it
promotes 63 — four times the band's 39 at the same precision regime. Inside those 63, **25 are neutral and 25 break
against 13 fixes**: the pick is a service whose channels moved at least as much as the leader's, which on this corpus
is what _every_ candidate in a fault window looks like. Mean out-of-band channels per candidate is **7.31 of 8**, so
"more moved channels" is not a discriminating statistic — it is the corpus's ambient condition, and the median filter
on the fault-free rate removes 40 % of it without restoring any discrimination.

The band's statistic is a _margin_, and a margin is comparative by construction: it asks whether the engine's own
score has separated these two candidates, and the score already integrates magnitude, onset and the caller/callee
asymmetry the containment pass enforces. A raw count discards all three. **The rule was registered as "the case
