carries properties of its own" and it turns out the case's properties are not the ones that decide the answer** —
what decides it is the relation between two candidates, which is what the score measures and what the rule refused
to look at.

### 315.4 What the instrument cost, and what it bought anyway

The implementation is `gatePromotion`'s second mode with its own four outcome names (`evidence-none`,
`evidence-tie`, `evidence-behind`, `rarity-miss`), a per-case options object built in one place, a `--admission`
flag, and a table that names the rule rather than a threshold it does not read. Two defects were found by running it
rather than by reading it: the census's column pad was eleven wide and `evidence-behind` is fifteen characters, which
silently misaligned every row; and the `IMPOSSIBLE` guard on the band fired on every evidence run, because it asserts
an invariant of the band and an evidence arm has no band. Both are fixed and both are now tested — the second by
guarding it, the first by asserting that every census row has one width.

### 315.5 What stays open, named and unpriced

The preregistration's own §"What arm A does not test" named the next rule: **"promote iff the pick is the leader's
callee"**, which needs an edge list on the scoring path. Arm A's failure is the argument for it — the count is
direction-blind, and direction is the one thing the corpus's own telemetry states. The union graph is already an
artifact (§311), so a per-corpus adjacency exists; what does not exist is a per-case admissible version of it, and
until that is designed the rule is a sentence rather than an arm.

**What this does not license**: reading the closure as "the model has nothing". Arm T's 39 band-admitted overrides
were worth +10 at 85.7 % precision, which is the best model-side reading this project has. What closed is a rule
over a statistic — not the model, and not the graph.

---

## §316 — The ninety-three near misses, and the operator that cannot fire on this corpus

`docs/near-miss-census.md` is a new instrument (`benchmarks/src/near-miss-census.ts`, **100/100/100/100**, 43
tests) that reads a depth artifact and says what a `Top@1` miss is worth. On the shipped artifact (`@1 = 1 156`)
it reports **93 cases at rank 2–5**, worth `+6.54 pp` if every one of them became correct, and it reports two
things about them that change the next arm.

### 316.1 The margins, and the subtrahend that reversed the verdict

The census reports `(winner − truth) / winner`. Its first draft reported `(top[0] − top[1]) / top[0]` — the gap to
the runner-up — and on the 72 rank-2/3 cases that reads **22 under 2 %**, which is a tie-break class. Measured
against the answer:

| band  | under 1 % | under 2 % | under 5 % | under 10 % | under 20 % | ≥ 20 % | unmeasurable |
| ----- | --------: | --------: | --------: | ---------: | ---------: | -----: | -----------: |
| cases |         1 |         5 |         9 |         15 |         12 | **51** |            0 |

`tie share (under-2pct): 5.38 % — verdict evidence`. **A single wrong subtrahend flips the reading of a whole
class**, and the tie-break axis that the first draft would have ordered is worth 5 cases and not 22. Recorded as a
rule: a margin is measured against the quantity a rule would have to move, not against the nearest number in the
sort.

### 316.2 The class, and the four knobs it does not respond to

Three services win 41 of 93 (`ts-route-plan-service` 23, `ts-travel-plan-service` 15, plus a tail), i.e. the
observer class `docs/topo-closure.md` §1 named on the golden half. That document refused the `sum` aggregate there
and recorded **"inert on 1 422 cases"** here. A 20-case local probe (ten observer wins, ten others; a constructed
sample, so only the DIFFERENCES are readable) measures every knob at once:

| configuration               | Top@1 | Top@3 | Top@5 | per-case md5 |
| --------------------------- | ----: | ----: | ----: | ------------ |
| `external`, `max` (shipped) |   0 % |  75 % | 100 % | `be9ac3fb…`  |
| `external`, `sum`           |   0 % |  75 % | 100 % | `be9ac3fb…`  |
| `caller`, `max`             |   0 % |  75 % | 100 % | `be9ac3fb…`  |
| `all`, `max`                |   5 % |  65 % |  80 % | `96b0e4a3…`  |
| `all`, `sum`                |   0 % |  60 % |  75 % | —            |

Three of four knobs move **not one byte**, and the fourth moves `+1 / −2 / −4`.

### 316.3 Why: the corpus has no response channel at all

RCABench's telemetry carries **87 distinct metric names and every one is `container.*` or `k8s.*`** — cpu, memory,
filesystem, ready, restarts. `isResponseChannel` admits a callee only on `latency*` / event / `delay` / `loss` /
`socket`, so `explainsThrough(callee)` is **false for every node of every case**, `explained` stays empty, and the
operator returns its input. The discount is not misconfigured here; it is **undefined**, because the physical fact
it encodes — a caller's response contains its callees' — is a fact this corpus never measures. Weight, gate, scope
and closure are four descriptions of a quantity that has no referent, which is why four refusals on two corpora now
have one cause.

### 316.4 What the corpus does carry, and the arm it licenses

`traceEdgeLatency` is `[from, to, baseline, post]` per edge, and on the ten sampled observer wins **nine carry an
out-edge whose latency multiplied by 185×–1 065×, every one of them pointing at the truth**. That is the same
physical relation, measured on the channel the corpus has — in the direction the engine does not read. The engine
does read this array: `edgeLatencyScores` scores a node by its INBOUND rise (what its callers waited) and feeds
`latWeight = 0.561495`, which is evidence FOR the node. The deduction needs the OUTBOUND rise (what the node waited
for), which the graph carries only as `edgeLatencyByCallee`'s inbound aggregate.
`docs-repository:preregistration-308.md` registers the arm: **one new field** (`edgeLatencyByCaller`) and **one
predicate** — the edge itself must have risen by `θ` — with rho, gate, closure, scope, precedence and `latWeight`
held at their shipped values. `$0`, two θ values on one battery, acceptance `Top@1 ≥ 1 200` with the golden nine
cells byte-identical.

### Axes this closes

| Axis                                                 | Verdict                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "A tie-break rule is what the near-miss class needs" | **closed as measured false** — 5.38 % of the class is within two percent of its answer, and the reading that said otherwise divided by the wrong quantity                                       |
| "The topological discount can be tuned for RCABench" | **closed by information set** — the operator's admission predicate has no true instance on the corpus, so no value of `rho`, `gate`, `scope` or `closure` can move it; four refusals, one cause |
| "The observer class is a golden-half phenomenon"     | **closed as false** — it is 44.1 % of the FSE'26 near-miss class                                                                                                                                |
| "`sum` is the closure that unblocks the fan-out"     | **closed a second time**, now with the reason: the fan-out's explanation lives in an edge's latency, not in a callee's resource reading                                                         |

---

## §317 — The edge channel, first form: the threshold is refused by its own falsifier, and the refusal is not about the threshold

**Verdict: `Top@1` falls at both thresholds, the pre-registered acceptance is missed by 47 cases, and the repair
prediction is met at half its floor. The arm is refused. What the refusal buys is a number the axis was never
registered against: the two populations the predicate is supposed to separate — a caller that is a symptom and a
caller that is the source — have the same distribution of edge rise.**

### 317.1 What was dispatched

`docs/preregistration-308.md` registered one new field (`edgeLatencyRises`, aligned with `callGraph.edges`) and one
predicate: an edge may carry an explanation when its own latency rise clears `θ`, with `rho`, `gate`, `closure`,
`scope`, `precedence` and `latWeight` held at their shipped values. The predicate is consulted on **both** sides of
the deduction — the callee side reads that edge, the caller side reads the maximum over the node's out-edges — because
on this corpus the channel predicate is false on both sides for one reason (`§316.3`), and relaxing one side alone
would have been inert on exactly the corpus the arm was built for. That correction is amendment A1 of the
pre-registration and it was written before the first dispatch.

Four runs, all local, `$0`, no model call anywhere:

| arm                         |   `Top@1` | `Top@3` | `Top@5` |  up | down | net |
| --------------------------- | --------: | ------: | ------: | --: | ---: | --: |
| control (shipped + profile) | **1 156** |   1 228 |   1 249 |   — |    — |   — |
| `θ = 2`                     |     1 117 |   1 207 |   1 237 |  20 |   48 | −39 |
| `θ = 10`                    |     1 141 |   1 222 |   1 246 |  21 |   19 | −15 |
| control, with the profile   | **1 156** |   1 228 |   1 249 |   — |    — |   — |
| `θ = 2`, with the profile   |     1 129 |   1 207 |   1 237 |  17 |   48 | −27 |
| `θ = 10`, with the profile  |     1 153 |   1 222 |   1 246 |  18 |   19 |  −3 |

The first pair is the same battery without the fault-free profile, taken because the profile's worth (`+15`) was
established two iterations earlier and it would have been an assumption to score the arm against the profile-less
control. The two controls agree at 1 156 and the two `θ = 2` arms agree on `Top@3` and `Top@5` to the case, which is
what makes the four arms one axis rather than two builds.

### 317.2 The falsifier

The pre-registration wrote five predictions and one acceptance before the first run. They are quoted as they were
written, including the one whose recorded expectation went the other way:

| #   | written before the run                                                             | measured                                                                                  | verdict                            |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| P1  | ≥ **12** of the observer-class near misses become correct                          | **6**                                                                                     | **failed**                         |
| P2  | `Top@1` between **1 180 and 1 240**                                                | 1 129 (no profile) / 1 129 (profile) at `θ = 2`                                           | **failed**, below the floor by 51  |
| P3  | the golden nine cells are identical (`641/735`), because the array is absent there | not dispatched — see below                                                                | **not reached**                    |
| P4  | no fault type ≥ 2 down                                                             | `NetworkCorrupt −5`, `NetworkBandwidth −4`, `NetworkPartition −4`, `HTTPResponseAbort −3` | **violated**                       |
| P5  | the `θ` curve is **NOT** monotone — `θ = 10` moves MORE cases than `θ = 2`         | 37 moved against 65                                                                       | **refuted in the theory's favour** |
| A   | `Top@1 ≥ 1 200`, golden identical, no family ≥ 2 down                              | none of the three                                                                         | **refused**                        |

`P5` is the one prediction that was wrong in the arm's favour, and it is the one that matters for what came next: the
threshold DOES do what a threshold does — fewer admissions, fewer movements, `−3` against `−27` — so the rise
carries _some_ information and the failure is not that the comparison is meaningless. That is what made a second
**form** worth measuring rather than a second threshold, and `§318` measures it.

`P3` was not reached, and the reason is not cost: the acceptance conjunct on the golden half is an AND, so a battery
refused by its own `Top@1` needs no second half to be refused. The inertness it would have tested is a construction
rather than a hope — RCAEval's datapacks carry no span duration, so `edgeLatencyRises` is `undefined` and the
operator's first line returns before any edge is visited — and it is pinned by
`__tests__/causal/topo-edge-admission.test.ts`'s "`null` is inert" describe instead of by a dispatch.

### 317.3 Why: the two populations are one population

Admitting `from → to` is a decision to **charge `from`**, and the decision has a truth value. It is helpful when
`from` is a symptom of a fault downstream; it is harmful when `from` is the ground-truth source, which is demoted for
waiting on the faults it caused. So the axis is a classifier over the corpus's measured edges, and the classifier can
be scored without running the engine at all: 71 560 measured edges in the FSE'26 corpus, 5 942 of them leaving a
ground-truth service.

| statistic                                             | charging the truth (harmful), n = 5 942 | charging a symptom (helpful), n = 65 618 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| edge rise `post/pre`, p10 / p25 / **p50** / p75 / p90 | 0.47 / 0.68 / **0.91** / 1.24 / 1.91    | 0.48 / 0.70 / **0.94** / 1.38 / 2.91     |

The medians differ by 3 %, and the helpful class is the one with the **larger** values. A fault multiplies the latency
of every call the faulty node makes, so a high out-rise is as much a property of the source as of the symptom. There
is no cut to place, and the arm's low-θ results are what a coin-flip classifier costs: at `θ = 2` it admits enough
edges to charge almost every caller, gains 20 cases and loses 48.

### 317.4 What the failure pointed at, and why the pointer was wrong

The 37 cases `θ = 10` moved split cleanly by a quantity the absolute form cannot name: in the losses the charged node
had **no out-edge at all** in 15 of 19 cases, and in the wins it had one whose rise was large. That reads as a
queueing split — _how long did this node wait relative to how long it was waited for_ — and it motivated the second
form of the axis (`§318`). It is a real asymmetry in the corpus and it is not a usable one, which is the subject of
the next chapter.

### Axes this closes

| Axis                                                                                   | Verdict                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "The topological discount can be made to fire on RCABench by reading the edge channel" | **closed** — it fires, at 10 227 admissions at `θ = 2`, and `Top@1` falls by 27                                                               |
| "A single absolute threshold on the per-edge rise separates sources from symptoms"     | **closed as measured uninformative** — the two populations have the same median (0.91× against 0.94×) and the helpful one has the larger tail |

## §318 — The edge channel, second form: the queueing divisor is 26× less pure than the constant, and `rho = 1` turns a false positive into a deletion

**Verdict: the second form is refused, and it is refused _relative_ to the first — the same threshold on the same
corpus admits a population that charges the truth three times as often. The form was worth measuring because the
mechanism it encodes is real; the measurement says the mechanism runs in the direction that makes the arm worse. The
chapter closes the family of five forms and records the one mechanism that outlives it: at the shipped weight, an
admitted edge does not demote a candidate, it deletes it.**

### 318.1 The form

`TopoEdgeRise` is `{ threshold, against: 'absolute' | 'inbound' } | null`:

| `against`  | predicate                            | what it says                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `absolute` | `rise(edge) ≥ θ`                     | the call got this much slower                                              |
| `inbound`  | `rise(edge) ≥ θ · maxInRise(caller)` | the call got slower relative to how much this **caller** was itself slowed |

The motivation is stated as a falsifiable claim rather than as a preference: §317's failing is that the corpus's
ambient rise varies by two orders of magnitude between cases, so a constant admits both the edge that _is_ the fault
and the edge the network multiplied along with everything else. Dividing by the caller's own inbound measurement is
"the same fact in the units the case provides". A source has little or no inbound traffic, so the divisor should
charge symptoms and leave sources alone.

It runs the other way. One pass over one array builds both maxima, and one function decides:

```ts
const admitted = (nodeId: ServiceId, rise: number): boolean => {
  if (edgeRise === null) return false;
  const against = edgeRise.against === 'inbound' ? maxInRise.get(nodeId) : 1;
  if (against === undefined) return false;
  return rise >= edgeRise.threshold * against;
};
```

`undefined` returns `false` rather than dividing by one: a node nothing was seen waiting on has not been shown to be a
victim, and reading the absence as a unit baseline would charge it on the strength of a measurement the corpus does
not contain. That branch is the one this chapter's census endorses — and it is the only part of the form that does.

### 318.2 The measurement

Same corpus, same commit, same control artifact — **1 156 / 1 228 / 1 249**, reproduced to the case:

| arm                  |   `Top@1` | `Top@3` | `Top@5` |  up | down | net | P1 repaired | truth deleted |
| -------------------- | --------: | ------: | ------: | --: | ---: | --: | ----------: | ------------: |
| control              | **1 156** |   1 228 |   1 249 |   — |    — |   — |           — |             0 |
| `θ = 2`, `absolute`  |     1 129 |   1 207 |   1 237 |  17 |   48 | −27 |           6 |             9 |
| `θ = 10`, `absolute` |     1 153 |   1 222 |   1 246 |  18 |   19 |  −3 |           6 |             2 |
| `θ = 2`, `inbound`   |     1 129 |   1 205 |   1 232 |  16 |   38 | −27 |       **3** |        **16** |
| `θ = 5`, `inbound`   |     1 140 |   1 216 |   1 238 |   4 |   18 | −16 |       **0** |        **12** |

Three readings, and the third is the one that decides the form:

1. **The net is not better at a matched `Top@1`.** `θ = 2 inbound` and `θ = 2 absolute` both read 1 129; the inbound
   form gets there with fewer losses (38 against 48) and fewer gains (16 against 17), i.e. by admitting fewer edges of
   both kinds rather than more of the right kind.
2. **The repair prediction collapses.** P1 was the arm's reason for existing — 38 observer-class near misses, ≥ 12
   repaired. Absolute reads 6 at both thresholds; inbound reads **3** and **0**.
3. **The deletions double.** 16 of the 38 losses at `θ = 2 inbound` are answers that were right at rank 1 and are
   _absent from the ranked list_ afterwards, against 9 for the absolute form at the same threshold.

### 318.3 Why the divisor inverts: it selects for sources

The census of §317.3 can be split by threshold and by form, because the decision is per edge and the truth value is
per edge:

|   θ | `absolute`: admitted / of which charge the truth | `inbound`: admitted / of which charge the truth |
| --: | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
|   2 | 10 227 / 533 (5.2 %)                             | 5 151 / 434 (8.4 %)                             |
|   5 | 4 568 / 78 (1.7 %)                               | 1 240 / 157 (**12.7 %**)                        |
|  10 | 3 125 / 18 (**0.6 %**)                           | 510 / 80 (**15.7 %**)                           |

At `θ = 10` the constant admits 3 125 edges of which 18 charge the truth — **0.6 % impurity**. The divisor admits 510
of which 80 do — **15.7 %**, i.e. **26× less pure on a population 6× smaller**. The mechanism is arithmetic and not a
threshold: `maxInRise` is small or absent for exactly the services with few callers, which on TrainTicket is the
backend edge of the call graph and on every system includes the injected ones. Dividing by a small number is a
multiplier, so the form concentrates on the population it was introduced to spare.

| statistic                                            | charging the truth (harmful), n = 5 942 | charging a symptom (helpful), n = 65 618 |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| rise ÷ caller's inbound rise, p10 / **median** / p90 | 0.03 / **0.65** / 1.62                  | 0.08 / **0.76** / 1.70                   |

The ratio does not separate the classes either — 17 % apart at the median, with the helpful class again the _larger_ —
so the form's failure is not a bad threshold on a good statistic. It is the same statistic, reweighted toward the
harmful tail.

### 318.4 What outlives the form: at `rho = 1` a false positive is a deletion

The purity above would be survivable if a wrong charge cost one rank position. It does not:

| arm                  | truth absent from the ranked list | of those, correct at rank 1 in the control |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------: | -----------------------------------------: |
| control              |                               173 |                                          0 |
| `θ = 2`, `absolute`  |                               185 |                                          9 |
| `θ = 10`, `absolute` |                               176 |                                          2 |
| `θ = 2`, `inbound`   |                               190 |                                         16 |
| `θ = 5`, `inbound`   |                               184 |                                         12 |

The 173 is the structural floor — cases `poolAdmission = positive` already excludes, present in the control and in
every arm, and unchanged by this axis. What the arms add is the column beside it. `ts-preserve-service` is
`1 → 99` in `ts0-ts-preserve-service-response-replace-body-644lf4`: it is the truth, it is charged through its own
out-edge, its anomaly is reduced to a non-positive score, and the pool filter drops it. No other term can undo that,
because there is no score left to reorder.

Two consequences, and the second is not about this axis:

1. **The family closes at five.** Weight (`§316`'s weight/gate/scope/closure quadruple), precedence, and now the
   edge-explained predicate in two forms. Each was refused by a different measurement, and the last two say the
   remaining gap is not a parameter: the statistic the corpus carries does not distinguish a source from a symptom,
   in either of the two units available.
2. **The deletion channel is live wherever the deduction runs.** `rho = 1` is the shipped value on both corpora, and
   on RCAEval the deduction is worth +10 net (`docs/topo-share.md` §8–9) — so the cliff is not a defect in itself.
   But any future arm that _widens_ admission is measured against a cost function with a cliff in it, and 0.6 %
   impurity is enough to lose 19 cases when each false positive can remove an answer rather than demote it.

### 318.5 What a next arm would have to change

Not the threshold, and not the divisor. The two facts this iteration adds are constraints on any successor:

- **the statistic has to be one that separates the classes**, and neither `post/pre` nor `post/pre ÷ inbound` does.
  The remaining candidate in this corpus is the _shape_ of the rise — whether the edge's post-distribution moved as a
  step at the injection boundary or as a ramp — because a fault's own calls step and a network's ambient does not.
- **admission must not be a deletion.** A charge that can push a candidate out of the pool makes every false positive
  cost a whole answer. A successor that subtracts a bounded share, or that re-orders instead of zeroing, would be
  measured against a different cost function — and `rho < 1` on the current form is the cheapest version of that
  experiment, which `§318.4`'s table now prices.

### Axes this closes

| Axis                                                                             | Verdict                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Dividing by the caller's own inbound rise is the same fact in the case's units" | **closed as false, and worse than the null** — 26× less pure at `θ = 10`, and 16 correct answers deleted at `θ = 2`                                     |
| "The observer class is repaired by an edge predicate"                            | **closed at 6 / 3 / 0** of a pre-registered 12, by all four arms                                                                                        |
| "The edge channel can stand in for the missing response channel"                 | **closed as measured uninformative** — both available statistics rank the harmful and helpful populations in the same order, and the helpful one higher |
| "The remaining gap on RCABench is a parameter of the deduction"                  | **closed** — five forms, five refusals, four distinct causes                                                                                            |

## §319 — The clamp: the class of deleted answers is empty on RCABench, and the reason is the SPACE rather than the operator

**Verdict: the clamp is refused as a VACUOUS arm — `poolAdmission = graph` with the charge held fixed is
byte-identical to the same arm without it, over 1 422 cases — and the vacuity is the finding: on a rank-normalised
map a deduction cannot create a unique minimum, so it cannot delete. What the iteration measures instead is worth
more than the arm: `topoDiscountScope = external` is worth `+53` cases (3.73 pp) on this corpus, and the pool axis
is now closed on BOTH halves with a mechanism rather than a p-value.**

### 319.1 The arm, and why it was the right next one

§318 closed the edge channel and left one sentence standing about the operator rather than about that axis: at
`rho = 1` with `poolAdmission = positive`, a charged candidate is not ranked last, it is **absent**, and no other
term can undo a deletion because there is no score left to reorder. The golden-nine record already carried four
deletions of that shape (`topoClosure` §8), and `poolAdmission`'s own docblock ended on an unmeasured sentence —
"whether a prior carries a zero-anomaly node is the measurement".

The arm was therefore a **factorial**, because one arm cannot separate "the deduction is wrong" from "the pool
decision is wrong": the deduction's only visible effect at `rho = 1` _is_ the pool decision.

| arm    | `scope`    | `gate` | `poolAdmission` | what it isolates                                             |
| ------ | ---------- | -----: | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **A0** | `external` |      1 | `positive`      | the published cell                                           |
| **A1** | `all`      |      1 | `positive`      | the shipped charge, unblocked                                |
| **A2** | `all`      |      1 | `graph`         | **the clamp** — same charge, no candidate may leave the pool |
| **A3** | `external` |      1 | `graph`         | the pool decision alone, nothing to delete                   |
| **A4** | `all`      |      0 | `positive`      | the gentle charge                                            |

`A1 − A0` differs from the published configuration in **one knob**, the scope, because `DEFAULT_TOPO_DISCOUNT = 1`
and `DEFAULT_TOPO_DISCOUNT_GATE = 1` — the operator ships at full strength and is inert on this corpus for exactly
one reason, that `external` finds no response channel among the 87 `container.*`/`k8s.*` names.

### 319.2 The measurement

FSE'26, 1 422 cases, one commit, one profile built from the same corpus, `$0`, no model call. The control
reproduces the published cell to the case.

| arm    |     Top@1 | Top@3 | Top@5 |  ΔTop@1 | fault types below control | truths at `truthRank: 0` |
| ------ | --------: | ----: | ----: | ------: | ------------------------: | -----------------------: |
| **A0** | **1 156** | 1 228 | 1 249 |       — |                         — |                    **0** |
| **A1** |     1 103 | 1 209 | 1 235 | **−53** |                        12 |                    **0** |
| **A2** |     1 103 | 1 209 | 1 235 | **−53** |                        12 |                    **0** |
| **A3** |     1 156 | 1 228 | 1 249 |   **0** |                         0 |                    **0** |
| **A4** |     1 120 | 1 211 | 1 226 | **−36** |                        12 |                    **0** |

Three of the five readings are **exact**, and the exactness is the result:

1. **`md5(A1.ndjson) == md5(A2.ndjson)`.** Not "close": identical over 1 422 rows, every `truthRank`, every `pool`,
   every `ranked` array. The clamp has nothing to clamp, so the arm cannot be read as a gain or as a loss — it is
   the _same run_.
2. **A3 is the control.** `poolAdmission = graph` alone leaves all three headline numbers unchanged; the pool
   median moves 49 → 50, one node per case, and that node enters at the bottom and stays there. §9's finding
   (twelve candidates recovered, one answer) reproduces on 1 422 cases and is _more_ inert at a wider pool.
3. **The charge costs at both gates**, and the shipped predicate therefore carries `+53` (3.73 pp) here — the loss
   concentrates in `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` (171 → 153) and `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` (139 → 123), two families
   whose truth is a response the caller itself produced, which is precisely what an internal-channel charge erases.

### 319.3 Why the class is empty: a tie the operator CREATES is not a tie the data has

A deletion needs a **unique** minimum, because `rankNormalizeScores` — the transform `applyAnomalyNormalization`
maps the operator's output back through, since the builder rank-normalises this corpus — assigns a tie group the
group's **average** 0-indexed rank:

```ts
const normalized = (i + j) / 2 / (n - 1);
```

Measured on one case the arm **lost** (`ts0-ts-basic-service-request-replace-method-gqn7nd`, 50 nodes), on the
deviation map the operator actually reads:

| map                         | entries at the minimum | the minimum | after the transform                       |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------: | ----------: | ----------------------------------------- |
| raw                         |                  **1** |     1.71e-4 | 1 entry at **0** → the pool loses it (49) |
| `external` (shipped, inert) |                      1 |     1.71e-4 | 1 entry at **0** (49)                     |
| `all`                       |                 **19** |       **0** | 19 entries at **0.1837** → pool 50        |

Nineteen of fifty nodes are zeroed, and the tie average lifts all nineteen to `(0 + 18) / 2 / 49 = 0.1837` — the
score of the **ninth**-ranked node. Every charged candidate is re-admitted _above the eight least-anomalous nodes
it was meant to fall below_. The operator's zero is not a zero after the transform: **the tie average is the right
rule for a tie the data has and the wrong rule for a tie the operator creates.** That is why the clamp is vacuous
here, and why `gate = 1` (−53) is worse than `gate = 0` (−36): the gate decides how many nodes join the promoted
tie group.

### 319.4 What this closes, and what it opens

**Closes** the pool question on both halves: `+1` of 735 where a zeroed node can leave (§9 of
`docs/pool-admission.md`), `+0` of 1 422 where it cannot, with the mechanism named rather than inferred.
`DEFAULT_POOL_ADMISSION` stays `positive`, and the argument is now structural rather than statistical.

**Closes** `scope = all` on both corpora as well: −2 on RE3/SockShop, −53 here.

**Opens** one thing that is not a knob: the operator's output is expressed in a space that re-quantises it. On a
rank surface "fully explained" can be written as _0_ (deleted, or admitted at the floor) or as the _band's average
rank_ (promoted), and the corpus's own transform chooses the second. A future arm would have to return the charged
set through a transform that keeps it at the bottom, which is a change of **space** rather than of the operator and
belongs to whoever measures `rank` against `minmax` first. It is recorded rather than attempted, because the five
arms above are the measurement that says the question is real.

### 319.5 The instrument that made the question askable, and the denominator this iteration fixed elsewhere

The verdict file's four published fields could not distinguish a deletion from a miss: on the control, **173 of
1 422** truths sit beyond rank 5 and every one of them was written as the same `absent`. Three columns close it —
`truthRank` over the whole order, `pool`, and `truthAnomalyBefore` — and they are what turns "the totals moved" into
"this case's truth was demoted to rank 3". `docs/fse26-per-case-verdicts.md` owns the format; the columns are
optional on the record and always written by the runner, so an archived four-field file still parses.

The same iteration read the last unconnected suite. `docs/cloud-opsbench-connection.md` sizes it: released, MIT,
754 cases, **76 metric-bearing** ones — the comparable population is the performance families, not the whole corpus
— with a published leaderboard whose best component accuracy is 0.88 on Online Boutique and 0.70 on Train Ticket.
It adds a denominator and no measurement, and it is named here so that the reading is reachable from the register
rather than from a directory listing.

### 319.6 The space arm: the intervention that turns the mechanism into a measurement

§319.3 explains the vacuity with a mechanism. A mechanism that is only _explained_ is an inference; this is the
intervention. The same three arms, the same corpus, the same profile, one flag — `--no-rank-normalization` — so the
map the ranking reads is the deviation map the operator writes:

| arm    | flags                                  | Top@1 | Top@3 | Top@5 | pool median | truths at `truthRank: 0` |
| ------ | -------------------------------------- | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----------: | -----------------------: |
| **B0** | `--no-rank-normalization`              | 1 122 | 1 223 | 1 242 |          49 |                    **0** |
| **B1** | `… --topo-discount-scope all`          |   733 |   783 |   797 |      **27** |                  **588** |
| **B2** | `… --scope all --pool-admission graph` | 1 067 | 1 200 | 1 229 |          50 |                    **0** |

Four readings, and they settle the question the rank-space factorial could only pose:

1. **The class is real, and the space is what hides it.** B1 deletes **588 of 1 422** truths — 41.4 % of the corpus —
   against **0** in the rank-normalised population. Same operator, same corpus, same weights: the only difference is
   the transform the output is read through. §319.3's sentence is now a measurement rather than an explanation.
2. **The clamp is decisive exactly where it can act.** B2 restores **588 of 588**: **336 to rank 1**, 52 to rank 2,
   424 inside Top@5. `Top@1` moves **733 → 1 067, +334 cases (+23.5 pp)** — the largest single movement any arm on
   this operator has produced, and it is produced by refusing to let a charge _delete_.
3. **The operator's space-independent cost is 55 cases.** B2 still reads 55 below B0 (1 067 vs 1 122), and the
   rank-space pair reads 53 below its own control (1 103 vs 1 156). Two different mechanisms — deletion in one,
   tie-promotion in the other — land on the same residual, which is therefore the part of the charge that is
   _reordering_ rather than removing: **86 % of the deviation-space damage is deletion (334 of 389) and 14 % is the
   reordering that survives the clamp.**
4. **The published normalisation is itself worth +34.** B0 reads 1 122 against A0's 1 156 on the same corpus, so
   `rankNormalization = true` is a +34-case configuration choice — a number this repository has never measured,
   because it has never run the corpus without it.

**Verdict, revised and stated as one sentence:** the clamp is **vacuous on the published configuration** (A2 ≡ A1,
byte for byte) and **worth +334 cases on the same corpus once the transform stops hiding the deletion** (B2 vs B1) —
so it is refused as a _default_ (B2 is still 55 short of B0, and B0 is 34 short of the published cell) and enrolled
in the record as the **largest measured contribution of any arm on this operator**, with the decomposition 334
deletion / 55 reordering. `DEFAULT_POOL_ADMISSION` stays `positive` and `rankNormalization` stays `true`; what
changes is that both are now defended by a measurement rather than by a published number nobody had decomposed.

**What this opens, in priority order.** (a) The 55-case reordering residual is the operator's real price, and it is
the only quantity a successor arm has to beat; (b) a transform that keeps a charged set at the bottom instead of
averaging it into the tie band would make the clamp's +334 available _without_ changing the normalisation — that is
the change of space §319.4 names, and it is now worth a pre-registration rather than a paragraph; (c) the +34 the
normalisation is worth must be checked for `minmax`, which is the third value of the same axis and has never been
measured on this corpus.

### 319.6.1 The residual has an address, and the charge is not always the culprit

The four readings above are aggregate. The per-case columns make the same numbers decomposable to the case, and the
decomposition changes what the next arm should be:

| quantity                        |               count | derivation                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------: | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| truths B1 deletes               |             **588** | `truthRank: 0 ∧ truthAnomalyBefore > 0`                  |
| … of which B0 ranks **1**       |             **393** | the charge destroys 393 top answers, not 588 top answers |
| … of which B0 puts inside Top@5 |             **441** | 96.1 % of what the clamp recovers was recoverable        |
| B2 returns to **rank 1**        |             **336** | 85.5 % of 393                                            |
| B2 returns inside **Top@5**     |             **424** | 96.1 % of 441                                            |
| B0 → B2 `Top@1`                 | **−75 / +20 = −55** | the residual is net, not gross                           |

Two consequences that the aggregate table hides:

1. **The clamp recovers the _order_, not just the membership.** If admission were a floor with an arbitrary order,
   the 588 would return near the bottom of a 50-node pool and `Top@1` would not move; it returns 336 to rank 1
   because the restored candidates are ranked by `selfScore`, i.e. by their own deviation — the quantity the charge
   never touched. That is the mechanism §319.1 claimed for the axis and it is now read off 588 cases.
2. **The gross cost is 75, not 55.** The clamp loses 75 answers relative to B0 and wins 20 back. A residual quoted
   as "55" is a _net_; the operator's gross reordering damage in deviation space is 75 and the 20 are cases where
   the charge is _right_ — worth separating because they are the only direct evidence that the charge carries
   signal at all.

**And the residual is not spread evenly.** `Top@1(B2) − Top@1(B0)` per fault type, over the 25 types present:

| fault type               |     B0 |    B1 |     B2 | B2 − B0 |      n |
| ------------------------ | -----: | ----: | -----: | ------: | -----: |
| HTTPResponseReplaceCode  |    161 |    81 |    142 | **−19** |    231 |
| HTTPRequestReplaceMethod |    132 |    73 |    121 | **−11** |    190 |
| HTTPResponseAbort        |     39 |    17 |     33 |      −6 |     44 |
| HTTPRequestDelay         |     70 |    44 |     65 |      −5 |     88 |
| HTTPResponseReplaceBody  |     49 |    24 |     44 |      −5 |     51 |
| HTTPRequestAbort         |     49 |    29 |     45 |      −4 |     60 |
| NetworkCorrupt           |     33 |    24 |     29 |      −4 |     46 |
| HTTPRequestReplacePath   |     39 |    23 |     36 |      −3 |     39 |
| NetworkBandwidth         |     19 |    19 |     17 |      −2 |     42 |
| JVMReturn / TimeSkew     | 12 / 1 | 9 / 0 | 11 / 0 | −1 / −1 | 21 / 2 |
| HTTPResponseDelay        |     66 |    50 | **70** |  **+4** |     89 |
| JVMException             |     31 |    24 | **33** |  **+2** |     43 |
| the other 13 types       |      — |     — |      — |   **0** |    518 |

The residual is **HTTP-shaped**: every fault type that changes a _value_ on an existing request path loses cases
(`ReplaceCode` −19, `ReplaceMethod` −11, `ReplaceBody` −5), every fault type that changes _reachability_ loses none
(`ContainerKill`, `PodKill`, `PodFailure`, `NetworkPartition`, `NetworkLoss` all read exactly B0). The charge is a
parent-to-child transfer along the call topology; a code replacement does not sever an edge, so the propagation
term is spent reordering nodes whose deviation is genuinely close, and the 20 net-minus-55 cases where the charge
_helps_ are the ones where the truth sits downstream of a louder neighbour.

**The larger number this puts on the table.** The same read gives the corpus's remaining Top@1 misses in the
published configuration: 1 422 − 1 156 = **266**, of which `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` (60) and
`HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` (51) are **111 — 42 % of everything still wrong**. The clamp's whole residual is 55. The
value-replacement class is twice as large as the axis this iteration closed, and it is where a successor arm should
be aimed.

## §320 — The entry point: 58 % of the remaining error is one node, and no coefficient reaches it

Iteration 310 pointed here by arithmetic: 266 Top@1 misses remain, and 111 of them are two fault types. This entry
records the audit of that class, its pre-registration (`docs-repository:preregistration-311.md`), and the
axis it opens. The full reading, with the population, the instrument and the by-service table, is
`docs/fse26-entry-point.md`.

The dump was taken **without `--fault-free-profile`**, so it reads 1 141 rather than 1 156 — the first of the three
failure modes the pre-registration itself named. Its size is measured: 18 cases change `truthRank`, **2** are in
this population (both `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod`, both `1 → 2`, both in H2), and every figure below is stated on the
published population with the correction applied.

### 320.1 Two of the four registered hypotheses die, and they were the actionable two

| class                                        | published (111) |  share |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------: | -----: |
| **H1** truth's anomaly absent or off-graph   |           **0** |    0 % |
| **H2** the winner is the truth's **caller**  |              13 | 11.7 % |
| **H3** in band (rank ≤ 5)                    |               8 |  7.2 % |
| **H4** instrument artifact                   |           **0** |    0 % |
| **H5** real anomaly, not a caller, rank 6–45 |          **90** | 81.1 % |

H1 is empty on all 421 dumped cases — the truth always carries a nonzero `selfAnomaly` — so "no observable exists,
add a channel" is false here and the corpus's own status-code column is not the missing piece. H4 is empty: every
truth resolved to a node. H5 is a class the pre-registration had no slot for, and it is recorded as a defect of that
document rather than folded into H3: its members sit at rank 6–45 (median 35 of 50), which is not a tie band.

### 320.2 The class is one service, and the fault types were a proxy for it

Grouping the **whole corpus** by truth service, off the per-case artifact rather than the dump:

| truth service                     |   cases |  Top@1 |      rate |
| --------------------------------- | ------: | -----: | --------: |
| **`ts-ui-dashboard`**             | **165** | **10** | **6.1 %** |
| `ts-basic-service` (next largest) |     202 |    188 |    93.1 % |
| the other 28 services             |   1 055 |    958 |    90.8 % |
| corpus                            |   1 422 |  1 156 |    81.3 % |

**155 of the 266 misses — 58 % — are one node: the request entry point.** No second outlier exists among the
thirty services with a population worth quoting; `ts-price-service` is next worst at 8 cases. Inside the dashboard's
165 cases the misses span every family it carries (`response-replace-code` 57/58, `request-replace-method` 39/39,
`request-delay` 15/16, `request-abort` 10/10, `partition` 8/9, `response-delay` 15/18, `loss` 5/7, `response-abort`
4/4, `corrupt` 2/3, `bandwidth` 0/1), so the class is a **node** and the fault types were a sample of it.

### 320.3 Why no coefficient recovers it, in one case

`ts0-ts-ui-dashboard-request-replace-method-2lnwn5`: the truth is rank 18 with `selfAnomaly 0.673`, decisive
`http.server.request.duration = 1.020` (`dev` 0.517), **onset 0**; the winner `ts-verification-code-service` is rank 1
with `container.cpu.usage = 1.240` (`dev` 0.958), onset 22 007. The entry point is the earliest node in the case and
eighteen downstream nodes out-score it on their own JVM and CPU deviations.

The onset prior is the natural correction and it is **already closed on this corpus** (`docs/fse26-onset-verdict.md`:
no admissible weight on either shape, gain 0 over `[0, 0.005361]`, capped by a lead of `0.010050`). This audit
supplies the population that shows why that interval is narrow and why widening it is not the answer: the signal is
right on **80 of the 111** misses (67 of the 90 H5; winner earlier on 20; 3 ties, 10 absent), and it still cannot
act, because the class sits 18–45 metric ranks down — a log-space gap of ≈ 0.18–0.45 against a term whose
admissible contribution is ≤ 0.005. **A tie-break bounded by one step cannot close a thirty-rank gap.**

### 320.4 What is refused, and what is opened

**Refused by the record, in this entry:** every form of "make the entry point's own numbers louder" — the onset
prior (§320.3), the log term (silent on both sides of these cases), the dispersion residual (−411, §305), the
external-channel predicate (−53, §319). And one refusal is a correction: `failedEdgeScore` **already** credits the
callee of failed calls, pays this entry point `1.000` on the case above, and ships at weight 3 worth +41 with zero
regressed types — the right edge is already read and already paid.

**Opened — a prior, not a term:** the engine has no concept of a **request root**. `ts-ui-dashboard` is the unique
callee of `loadgenerator` in every case of this corpus — a structural fact of the graph, not a service name — and
nothing in the scoring treats "requests enter here" as evidence. The arm that follows is an additive credit to the
node with no measured inbound edge other than the synthetic load source, **gated on that node's own deviation being
nonzero**, and its bar is the standing one: beat 1 156 with no fault type below its published cell. Stated with the
bar because it is the whole risk — the prior promotes a node in every case, and in 1 257 cases that node is not the
truth. It must win ≥ 60 of the 155 and lose essentially none of the 1 257, and that is what the arm measures.

**Axes this closes.** None. **Axes this opens.** One: the request-root prior.

## §321 — The failed-edge partition: the mechanism is real, the membership is not specific (−170)

Iteration 311 closed by registering a prior on the entry point. This entry closes it the other way: the prior was
refused **before implementation**, on two readings of the dump that already existed, and the arm that replaced it
was measured on the corpus and refused too — with the largest single-family gain of any arm on this operator
(+56) and a net loss of 170.

### 321.1 The registered prior dies without a run

`docs-repository:preregistration-311.md` §10 asked for credit on "the node with no measured inbound edge other than the synthetic
load source". Applied to the dump's edge lists that predicate admits **13–15 nodes per case** (median 13; 286 of
421 at 14): every `ts-admin-*`, `ts-*-delivery`, `ts-wait-order`, `ts-consign` and `ts-execution-*` service has
in-degree zero, because the graph is built from observed spans and an endpoint nobody exercised was never called.

And the subject's own evidence has the **wrong sign**: over the 421 cases, the entry point's median `selfAnomaly`
is **0.286 when it is the truth and 0.388 when it is not** (AUC 0.401), and its median rank is **34 against 29**.
A monotone credit lifts it in 324 cases where it is a proxy and in 97 where it is the cause, and the 97 sit
deeper. The full AUC table is `docs/failed-edge-jurisdiction.md` §1.

### 321.2 The statisic that does separate, and what it is worth when turned into an order

`failedEdge` separates at 0.848 — the entry point is the callee of `loadgenerator`, so an entry-point fault fails
the load source's calls. Across the same 421 cases the ledger credits **6.6 % of candidates** and contains the
truth **99.3 % of the time** (418 of 421), median three members. Partitioning the order so that credited
candidates precede the rest, keeping the score order inside each half, reads **73.2 % → 86.7 %** on that dump.

### 321.3 On the corpus it is refused, and the decomposition says why

| arm               |   `Top@1` |   `Top@3` |   `Top@5` | gained |    lost |
| ----------------- | --------: | --------: | --------: | -----: | ------: |
| control           | **1 156** |     1 228 |     1 249 |      — |       — |
| `failedEdgeFirst` |       986 | **1 232** | **1 293** |     71 | **241** |

`HTTPResponseReplaceCode` **+56** (171 → 227) — the family whose truth is the entry point in 58 of its 231 cases,
converted almost exactly as the dump predicted. Against it: `JVMMemoryStress` **−145** (171 → 26),
`ContainerKill` **−66**, `PodFailure` **−20**, `PodKill` **−4**. Those four are 235 of the 241 losses and they
share one property — **their fault does not fail a call at its own site**. A stressed or killed service's inbound
calls still succeed; the load source's calls to the entry point are what times out, so
`loadgenerator → ts-ui-dashboard` is the failed edge and the entry point takes the credit.

**The root of the call graph is the first node to see anyone else's timeout.** That is the ledger answering its
own question correctly, and the partition mistaking membership for causation.

### 321.4 What this closes, and the successor it registers

**Closed:** the request-root prior (never built), and the ledger's membership as a decisive signal. Also settled
from the other direction: `failedEdgeWeight`'s gate is not merely cautious here — the 235 cases it refuses are
cases it is right to refuse, and a looser gate would be this arm.

**Opened, with its prediction stated:** rank first the candidates whose **unexplained** failures are positive,
`unexplainedFailures(v) = max(0, inbound − outgoing)` — the statistic `failureContainment` already trusts. In an
entry-point fault its inbound calls fail and its outbound ones do not (residual > 0); in a stress or kill
downstream its inbound _and_ outbound calls fail (residual ≈ 0), because the failures it reports are the ones it
received. Bar: beat 1 156 with no type below its published cell, **keep ≥ 40 of the 56** `HTTPResponseReplaceCode`
gains, and restore `JVMMemoryStress` **above 160**.

**Axes this closes.** Two. **Axes this opens.** One: the failure flow's _residual_ as a membership test.

---

## §322 Iteration 313 — the failure channel cannot name a role, and the reach it can pay for

### 322.1 The residual membership was built and refused

Iteration 312 registered one successor: rank first the candidates whose **unexplained** failures are positive
(`unexplainedFailures(v) = max(0, inbound − outgoing)`), on the claim that a relay's own calls account for the
failures it reports. Measured on 1 422 cases against the same control:

| arm                                |   `Top@1` |   `Top@3` |   `Top@5` | gained |    lost |
| ---------------------------------- | --------: | --------: | --------: | -----: | ------: |
| control                            |     1 156 |     1 228 |     1 249 |      — |       — |
| `failedEdgeFirstScope=unexplained` | **1 049** | **1 323** | **1 348** |    135 | **242** |

The narrower membership bought **64 more gains than 312's and one more loss**. The same four families paid:
`JVMMemoryStress` 171 → 26, `ContainerKill` 89 → 23, `PodFailure` 24 → 4, `PodKill` 10 → 6 — 235 of the 242, at
the same counts iteration 312 recorded. Full read: `docs/failed-edge-jurisdiction.md`.

### 322.2 The reason, measured in the channel's own units

`scripts/dump-failure-flows.ts` prints the four counts the pass reads, per service, per case (`$0`, 20 cases per
family):

| fault type                 |   n | ground truth has **no** flow row | truth is a lead |
| -------------------------- | --: | -------------------------------: | --------------: |
| `JVMMemoryStress`          |  20 |                   **20 (100 %)** |               0 |
| `ContainerKill`            |  20 |                   **20 (100 %)** |               0 |
| `PodFailure`               |  20 |                   **20 (100 %)** |               0 |
| `PodKill`                  |  10 |                   **10 (100 %)** |               0 |
| `HTTPResponseReplaceCode`  |  20 |                                0 |              20 |
| `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` |  20 |                                0 |              20 |

**In the four loss families the ground truth is not in the ledger at all**: a stress or kill fails no call at its
own service, so it has no inbound and no outbound failure record, and no rule over that population can promote
it. Its rank-1 signature is _identical_ to an entry-point fault's (inbound > 0, outbound = 0, residual share
1.00), so no threshold, weight or reading separates them. What separates them is **which fault family the case
belongs to** — the label.

### 322.3 What that closes, and what it left open

**Closed:** the failure ledger as evidence about _causation_. Any promotion of ledger members over non-members
trades one family's gain for another's loss at a rate the corpus fixes in advance (312: −170, 313: −107).

**Left open, and this is the arm that paid:** the shipped pass is stated over the **fusion's neighbours**, so a
correct inversion the fusion placed thirty positions apart is invisible to it. Adjacency is a property of the
fusion's order; the failing edge is a property of the case.

### 322.4 The reach arm, and what it measured

`failureContainmentScope ∈ {adjacent, global, global-measured}` — the same rule, three populations of pairs:

| arm                  |   `Top@1` |   `Top@3` |   `Top@5` | gained |  lost |
| -------------------- | --------: | --------: | --------: | -----: | ----: |
| control (`adjacent`) |     1 156 |     1 228 |     1 249 |      — |     — |
| `global`             | **1 186** | **1 236** | **1 255** |     30 | **0** |
| `global-measured`    | **1 186** | **1 236** | **1 255** |     30 | **0** |

**30 gained, none lost, eight fault types gaining and none declining**: `NetworkBandwidth` +7,
`HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` +7, `NetworkPartition` +5, `JVMException`/`HTTPResponseReplaceCode`/`Body`/`NetworkLoss`/
`HTTPResponseDelay` +2–3 each. Movement shape: 21 cases 3 → 1, 4 cases 4 → 1, and four from 7–41 → 1. 58 cases
moved at all, so 28 improved inside the top without reaching it (`Top@3` +8, `Top@5` +6).

Full read, including the bar and the probe's per-service rows: `docs/failure-containment-reach.md`.

**Release surface: one flag, one owner, two labelled cells.** `DEFAULT_FAILURE_CONTAINMENT_SCOPE` stays `'adjacent'`
and the **FSE'26 dispatch states `--failure-containment-scope global-measured`** (`.github/workflows/
fse26-benchmark.yml`), so the published RCABench cell is **1 186 (83.40 %)** and its artifact prints the token, while
anything that does not ask — including the RCAEval dispatch — reads 1 156 (81.29 %). Two wide states are
byte-identical over 1 422 cases, so the evidence guard is free, and it refuses the one comparison §322.2 shows is
unsafe (a candidate the channel never measured read as a fully explained one).

**The objection this entry carried one revision ago — "the golden half is unmeasured" — is now retired by a
measurement, not an argument.** The Benchmark run dispatched on `accc80d` built a tree whose engine default _was_
`global-measured`; the run on `f48b3de` is a tree with no scope option at all. Six RCAEval artifacts compared
byte-for-byte: **735 cases across RE1/RE2/RE3 × {inject-time, no inject-time} plus RE3's novelty signal, and the only
differing line in any of them is `Total duration`.** So the pass is built and live on that half and its two states
agree there case for case.

Two drafts were wrong before that, and both corrections are kept because both errors are one command away:

1. The first draft claimed the RCAEval half was inert "by construction". It is not: `run-rcaeval.ts` attaches
   `failedTraceEdges` from a streaming pass over `traces.csv`. One `grep` refuted it.
2. The second draft then moved the **runner's** default instead, which
   `packages/kinetic/__tests__/unit/ranking-default-owners.test.ts` refused: an option has one default and the
   engine owns it, so a runner-side `DEFAULT_FSE26_FAILURE_CONTAINMENT_SCOPE` is a number published under a name its
   owner does not hold. The census was right; the constant was deleted, and the dispatch states the flag instead.

**The split into `invertAdjacent`/`liftCallers` was verified, not assumed**: a no-flag run of the archive reproduces
the iteration-313 control **1 422 of 1 422 per-case rows identical** (1 156), and the flagged run reproduces the arm
**1 422 of 1 422 identical** (1 186).

The configuration line prints the reach **conditionally**, on the rule every other non-boolean field follows: with
the default unchanged, "absent" names exactly one population (1 156) and 1 186 cannot be read without its token.

`adjacent` remains both the engine default and the ablation pole; the battery builds its options in code from the
engine defaults, so every published battery row whose `failureContainment` pole was `1` was measured on the narrow
traversal.

**Axes this closes.** One: the ledger's membership, in both its forms (credit and residual). **Axes this keeps
open.** None on this channel — the reach is now exhausted as well: a rule that compares only pairs a failing edge
relates, both of them measured, is the whole of what the channel supports.

## §323 Iteration 314 — three channels the score did not use, and the two the arm could not make pay

**The instrument first, because every reading below is its output.** `benchmarks/src/miss-anatomy.ts` decomposes a
miss into the formula's own terms: every result the engine returns carries `RootCauseResult.terms`, which sum
exactly to its `finalScore`, and the difference between the winner's rows and the truth's rows is a decomposition
of the miss with no re-derivation anywhere. Read on the published configuration (1 186), it reproduces the run
**236 of 236 `truthRank` and 236 of 236 winner** — the probe's numbers are the run's numbers by measurement rather
than by construction. The 14 tests hold three statements: the differences sum to the score gap, an absent truth is
NAMED rather than decomposed, and a tie is NAMED rather than resolved.

**§323.1 — what decided the 236.**

| term                          | cases |      share |
| ----------------------------- | ----: | ---------: |
| `selfAnomalyLog1p`            |   126 |     53.4 % |
| `dualFamily`                  |    42 |     17.8 % |
| `lat`                         |    41 |     17.4 % |
| `log`                         |    25 |     10.6 % |
| `failedEdge` / `pool`         | 1 / 1 | 0.4 % each |
| truth absent from the results | **0** |  **0.0 %** |

No miss is a membership decision and none is a tie: the decisive term's contribution is a **median 40.4 % of the
winner's score** and only 14 of 236 (5.9 %) are under 5 %. The signature also **changes with depth** — at rank 2–3
`log` decides 32 %, while beyond rank 10 the base term decides 65 % and `log` 2 % — so the near misses and the deep
ones want different work and a single arm cannot address both.

**§323.2 — the base term does not lose by a hair.** Read back out of the two contributions (`expm1`, because the
term is `weight × log1p(self)` at weight 1), `truthSelf / winnerSelf` has **median 0.413**; 45 of the 126 sit under
0.30 and only 14 are within 10 %. The truth is never at exactly zero, so on this corpus the metric channel **sees**
the fault everywhere and prefers something louder — which is the 2026 agent literature's **MIS2**
("significance bias, trusting the loudest anomaly without separating cause from symptom") reproduced by a
deterministic engine, and it means a rescaling of the base term cannot move these cases without moving every case
the scale was calibrated on.

**§323.3 — three channels the score did not use.**

| term         | weight | candidates it reached (of 236) | why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------ | -----: | -----------------------------: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `failedEdge` |  **3** |                          **2** | the gate's name half refuses every candidate whose dominant metric is not duration-shaped (1 030 of 1 422 before any bar), and `evidence` mode needs a call denominator this corpus does not publish. **157 of the 236 carry the rows it reads** — `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` 58/58, `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` 44/44, `JVMReturn` 9/9, `JVMException` 8/8 |
| `trace`      |      1 |                          **0** | the FSE'26 loader fills no `traceActivity`; the corpus ships `traceEdges` (pairs, no counts) and `traceEdgeLatency`. The term's input is ABSENT, not zero — `lat` is the same data read as a node statistic, which is why 69 candidates do score on it                                                                                                    |
| `faultFree`  |      0 |                              0 | weight is the ablation, and §323.4 is why the weight alone was not the whole story                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

**The `failedEdge` row was measured before the arm was priced**, and the price is why no arm shipped: on 1 222 cases
whose net-failed-call leader exists, that leader is the truth **57.7 % of the time on cases the engine already gets
right** and 73.2 % on the ones it misses. The channel is _better_ on misses and still far below the base term's
83.4 % overall, so a partition that promoted its leader would take the archive to roughly 730 — a loss of ~450, not
a gain. The measurement is the arm's ceiling and it was taken for `$0` rather than paid for in a run.

**§323.4 — the fault-free prior: one aggregation degenerate, one refused.**

| arm                             |   `Top@1` | `Top@3` |   `Top@5` | gained / lost at rank 1 |
| ------------------------------- | --------: | ------: | --------: | ----------------------: |
| control (`w = 0`)               | **1 186** |   1 236 |     1 255 |                       — |
| `rarest`, `w` = 0.1 / 0.3 / 1.0 | **1 186** |   1 236 |     1 255 |                   0 / 0 |
| `dominant`, `w = 0.3`           |     1 175 |   1 249 | **1 279** |                 15 / 26 |
| `dominant`, `w = 1.0`           |     1 143 |   1 247 |     1 278 |                 28 / 71 |

**`rarest` is DEGENERATE here and the statement is arithmetic.** The aggregation reads the minimum `rate` over
EVERY channel a service carries, and 150 of the profile's 2 080 channels have `rate = 0`; a service with 39
channels therefore almost always holds one that never fires when nothing is wrong. A 60-case systematic sample
found **2 distinct `faultFree` scores per case in 60 of 60** — on `ts0-mysql-loss-67k278`, 50 scored services
collapse onto two values and 49 of them are `1.000`. A term that pays the whole fleet the same is a constant, and
the weight sweep moved **0 ranks on 1 422 cases** while moving 40 / 51 / 83 scores: the sweep is a measurement of a
constant, not of a prior.

**`dominant` is not degenerate and is still refused.** It reads the `rate` of the channel the candidate's anomaly
came from, which is the reading the term's docblock describes. Its shape is a FLATTENING: at `w = 0.3` the largest
single movement is `1 → 2` on **20 cases** against `2 → 1` on 9, `Top@3` gains 17 and loses 4, `Top@5` gains 24 —
and `Top@1` falls 11. By family the loss is concentrated and the gain is not: `NetworkPartition` **−7 / +0**,
`NetworkDelay −5 / +0`, `NetworkBandwidth −5 / +0`, against `JVMException +5 / −0` and `HTTPResponseDelay +2 / −0`.
A partition makes a _reachability_ channel fire, and that channel is noisy in the fault-free window too, so `1 − r`
is small exactly where the fault is loudest in its own units — the term prefers a quieter neighbour, which is the
mechanism the register named for `NetworkPartition` in §322 from the other direction.

Refused on the five gates written before the arms were read: **B1** (net ≥ +10) failed at both weights, **B2** (no
family −2) failed on three families, **B3** (half the gain in the rare-channel families) was not reached because the
net gain is negative, **B4** (monotone) passed, **B5** (`Top@3`/`Top@5` may not fall) passed. `faultFreeWeight`
stays `0` and `rarest` stays the default; every published cell reproduces with no flag.

**What the refusal keeps.** `Top@5` rising while `Top@1` falls is the signature of a **second opinion rather than a
better one**, and it is now the third independent measurement of that shape on this corpus — after `dualFamily`'s
gate (§181) and the containment reach (§322.4). A prior that agrees with the base term is worth nothing and a prior
that disagrees with it loses; that is the standing finding, and it is the reason the next arm is aimed at the base
term's own definition rather than at a fourth correction applied to it.

**§323.5 — the dimensional defect the decomposition exposed, kept open on purpose.** The base term is `log1p`-shaped
and therefore capped at **0.693** at weight 1; the `log` term is a max-normalised share in `[0, 1]` at weight **1**
and is therefore capped at **1.000**. On the 25 misses `log` decided, the winner's contribution is **1.000 on 25 of
25**, the truth's is 0.000 on 22, and the median base gap is **−0.017 — the base term had already chosen correctly.**
No `logWeight` above 0.693 can stop the term from out-weighing a maximal base contribution, so this is a ceiling to
fix rather than a weight to tune, and every published `logWeight` reading was taken with the property in it. It is
recorded and NOT changed here: it moves every cell the golden half publishes and needs its own pre-registration. **Closed in §324.1**: priced exactly, the fix is worth one flip and is algebraically a weight cut to 0.693.

Full read, including the reproduction commands: `docs/miss-anatomy.md`. Pre-registration and outcome:
`docs-repository:preregistration-314.md`.

**Axes this closes.** Two: the fault-free prior's value on this corpus, in both its aggregations; and "the
containment reach was the last thing the failure channel could pay for" — the ledger now reads its own ceiling,
and the ceiling is `selfAnomalyLog1p`. **Axes this keeps open.** Three, each with a measurement behind it: the
`log` term's ceiling (§323.5), the `failedEdge` gate on a corpus with no call denominator (§323.3), and the base
term's definition itself (§323.2, where the truth is visible to the channel and ranked second).

## §324 Iteration 315 — the ceiling that was the WIDTH, and the two items closed by arithmetic before a run

Three plan items were standing at the end of iteration 314: the `log` term's ceiling (§323.5), the `failedEdge`
gate on a corpus with no call denominator (§323.3), and the base term's definition (§323.2). This iteration closes
the first two **without a run**, because a run's outcome for each was computable from artifacts already on disk,
and it replaces the third with a measured statement about the presentation rather than about the score.

It also produces the one number that reframes ten failed agentic arms, and that number is not about the model.

### §324.1 The `log` ceiling cannot be fixed by a ceiling — 1 flip at best, and the map it is equivalent to is a weight cut the sweep already priced at −7

§323.5 recorded a real dimensional defect and predicted the fix was "either a matching ceiling or a log contribution
expressed in the base term's units". Both shapes are now priced exactly, from the 236 miss rows the previous
iteration dumped, with no run:

| cap on the `log` contribution | misses of the 25 that flip |
| ----------------------------: | -------------------------: |
|                     **0.693** |                      **1** |
|                         0.588 |                          2 |
|                         0.550 |                          4 |
|                         0.500 |                          6 |
|                         0.300 |                         10 |
|                         0.100 |                         19 |
|                         0.015 |                         21 |

The reason is in the same rows: on the 25 misses `log` decided, the **sum of every other term already favoured the
truth** on 21 of them, by at most **0.5878**. Capping the term at the base's ceiling leaves the winner a margin of
`0.693 × 1.000 − 0.5878 = 0.105`, so the cap cannot move the case it was proposed for. The cap only starts to act at
**0.588**, i.e. 15 % below the ceiling the defect names.

And the linear shape is not a new axis at all: `c × s = (c × w) × s`, so a ceiling of `c` at weight 1 **is**
`logWeight = c`. `fse26-logweight-sweep-verdict.md` read that axis: `w = 0.5` is **−7 cases**, `w = 0.25` is −62,
`w = 0` is −460, and the optimum is at `w = 1` with a shallow neighbourhood. A ceiling at 0.693 therefore lands
between 0 and −7 on a curve whose only interior optimum is the shipped point.

The nonlinear shape (pass the share through `log1p`, so its ceiling matches the base's) is a **ratio-compressing**
map, which is the direction `log-volume-scale.md` §3.3 measured as the losing one: `saturating` at κ = 25 compresses
the champion's lead and reads **−34** while `share`, which preserves every ratio exactly, reads −10.

**Verdict: refused, by two independent measurements and one algebraic identity, at `$0` and in one page.** The
dimensional observation in §323.5 stands as a description of the score; it is not a lever.

### §324.2 The failed-edge admission re-derived from the evidence's own shape — and refused a third time

§323.3 and §320 left the gate on the reading that `failedEdge`'s input is empty when it matters. The census over all
1 422 cases says the input is not empty: **`failedEdgeEvidence` is present on 1 422 of 1 422**, and it is
informative in isolation — the callee it names is the truth on **521 of 794** cases at a concentration bar of 0.5,
and on **161 of 256** at 0.99. The term contributes nothing on 234 of the 236 misses, so the walk runs and the gate
withholds.

Two admission rules were priced from that census before any code was written, and both fail on the same structure:

| rule                                              | population admitted | the callee is the truth on a case the engine has WRONG | the callee is neither the truth nor the winner on a case the engine has RIGHT |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------: | -----------------------------------------------------: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------: |
| one source-fed callee                             |                 741 |                                                    102 |                                                                           597 |
| one source-fed callee **and** one credited callee |                 130 |                                                 **61** |                                                                        **65** |

The narrow rule is the sharpest form of the idea — the channel names exactly one interface and the failures enter
the graph from a client outside the topology, which is the cleanest statement of "this interface failed" the corpus
can make — and it is **61 against 65**. The engine's own `boundary` mode is the same rule at case granularity and it
was already measured: **+21**, with four network families losing 8 to 16 apiece, refused. The same rule at CANDIDATE
granularity was measured as an order: **−170** (`failed-edge-jurisdiction.md`), refused.

So the direction channel is refused in three independent presentations — as a weight, as a case-level gate, and as
a per-candidate order — and the census says why: the population it is right about (102, of which 93 are the two
replacement families) is a subset of a population it is wrong about of the same size and the same families (95
replacement + 74 request-method cases where a credited callee is not the truth). **No scalar on the case and no
membership rule on the map separates them**, which is the register's recurring shape for the fifth time.

### §324.3 The number that reframes ten arms: at the width they used, 90 % was unreachable

`benchmarks/src/presentation-ceiling.ts` (100/100/100/100, 19 tests) prices the width of a reranker's presentation
from the run's own `truthRank` column. On the published run:

|  width |      ceiling | candidates it makes reachable |
| -----: | -----------: | ----------------------------: |
|      1 |      83.40 % |                         1 186 |
|      3 |      86.92 % |                         1 236 |
|  **5** |  **88.26 %** |                     **1 255** |
|      8 |      89.31 % |                         1 270 |
| **10** |  **90.30 %** |                     **1 284** |
|     15 |      91.63 % |                         1 303 |
|     20 |      92.83 % |                         1 320 |
|     30 |      95.57 % |                         1 359 |
|     44 | **100.00 %** |                         1 422 |

Every agentic arm this project has run presented the model with the engine's top five. **At `K = 5` the ceiling is
88.26 %, i.e. 1.74 pp BELOW the 90.0 % leader**, so those arms were structurally incapable of reaching SOTA and
their refutations are silent about the model. The smallest width at which 90 % is reachable at all is 10, and only
by a perfect reranker (a 0.30 pp margin). The full set has a ceiling of 100 % because the truth is in the results
on 236 of 236 misses — the corpus never hides the answer, the presentation does.

The width is not free: widening the list gives the model more chances to move a case the engine already had right.
The requirement it has to meet is therefore a pair, and the pair is what the next arm is registered on:

|  width | reachable misses | precision needed for 90.02 % |
| -----: | ---------------: | ---------------------------: |
|      5 |               69 |                      > 100 % |
|     10 |               98 |                       95.9 % |
|     20 |              134 |                       70.1 % |
| **30** |          **173** |                   **54.3 %** |
|     44 |              236 |                       39.8 % |

### §324.4 The `trace` term is idle because the corpus has no producer, and that is not a code defect

`trace` carries weight 1 and is present on 0 of 1 422 cases (§286b). The cause was recorded as "no loader fills the
input", which reads as an omission in this repository. It is not: the engine's input is a **pre/post span COUNT per
service**, and the converted RCABench case carries `traceEdges` (caller-callee pairs), `failedTraceEdges` (caller,
callee, net failures) and `traceEdgeLatency` (caller, callee, pre, post) — three per-EDGE statistics and no
per-service count anywhere. A loader that filled `traceActivity` from those files would be inventing the quantity
the term exists to read. Recorded, so the next reader does not spend an iteration wiring a producer the corpus
cannot feed.

**Axes this closes.** Three: the `log` ceiling as a lever (§324.1, and with it the "matching ceiling or common
units" family); the `failedEdge` admission rule in its last available presentation (§324.2); and "the agentic arms
failed because the model was weak" as a _complete_ explanation (§324.3).
**Axes this keeps open, with the numbers now attached.** The base term's definition (§323.2), unchanged and still
the largest single block of misses at 126 of 236; and the agentic layer at a width ≥ 20, which is the only
mechanism in the record whose ceiling clears the target — `docs-repository:preregistration-315.md`.

Full read: `docs/presentation-ceiling.md`. Census: `docs/miss-anatomy.md`.

## §325 Iteration 316 — the table was the constraint, and the width was not the table

§324 closed three axes and left one: "the agentic layer at a width of at least 20, the only mechanism in the record
whose ceiling clears the target". That arm was run. It reads **precision 0.475** against the **0.543** the target
needs, and the number that matters is not the shortfall — it is that the falsifier which would have closed the layer
named **0.30**, and the arm cleared it.
