| rounds per case                                |                   6.00 |                   6.00 |

**The comparison is not exact and the file had claimed it would be.** The tools are deterministic; the **endpoint is
not**. The ungated arm reads **1 067** here against **1 050** before, and the stop distribution moves from
`{answered 1 256, rounds 166}` to `{answered 1 273, rounds 149}`, so ±10 cases is the run-to-run band and the −1 is
inside it. What is _outside_ any band is the overshoot rate: 36.18 % and 36.50 % are the same number measured twice.

**The consequence is a design rule.** The two instruments that worked in this programme **enforce** a relation — `lag`
refuses an answer unless the candidate logged first, the entry prior refuses unless nothing below the entry rose.
This iteration **displayed** a relation instead, and display did nothing. Evidence the tools carry is not the same
thing as evidence the loop acts on, and the next instrument has to act: the interface record for the 39
`HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` cases, applied as a check inside the gate rather than as a line in a prompt.

## 325.15 The interface witness charges the CALLER, and that is 42 cases (iteration 325)

`325.14k` closed the service-granularity route to the 41 child-refused entry cases and named the next unit: the fault
is applied to an **edge**, so the distinguishing fact is _which interface_ changed shape. The corpus had carried the
instrument for that reading since iteration 290 and the arm had **never been shown it**: `buildTelemetry` copied
`caller/callee/failed/baseline` off `FaultFailedEdge` and dropped `novel`.

`novel` is the part of an edge's failures whose request **shape** — `(route, method)` as the callee recorded it — the
edge had never carried before the injection. The channel's own docstring is the whole argument: _a callee that broke
rejects nothing, it fails the requests it has always served, while a CALLER that corrupted its request sends a shape
the callee has never been asked for._ `failed − baseline` is identical in the two situations, which is why every
earlier reading of this channel — all of them counts — could not charge either end, and why `325.14k` read 602
triggers at 0.068 precision.

**The rule.** Answer with the caller of the strongest novel interface, skipping a caller that is a **root** of the
call graph: a root is the traffic generator, its request shape is a workload rather than a service's interface, and
the corpus never labels it — it is the strongest witness in **74 of the 203** cases that carry the channel. Nothing
else is read: not the size of the failing edge, not either end's error rate, not the latency.

| reading (¥0, through `applyResolver`) |  none | entry-prior |      **edge-novel** |
| ------------------------------------- | ----: | ----------: | ------------------: |
| fires                                 |     0 |           0 |              **42** |
| repairs                               |     0 |           0 |              **42** |
| breaks                                |     0 |           0 |               **0** |
| Top@1, ¥0 replay                      | 1 222 |       1 222 | **1 264 (88.89 %)** |
| Top@1, dispatch `44915289950`         | 1 222 |       1 222 | **1 263 (88.82 %)** |

The dispatch settles it: `answeredBy=interface` is **42** rows, every one correct, on a run whose own drift against the
324 answers is −1 case (`repairs 140 · breaks 33 · precision 0.809 · retention 0.971`, 11 410 480 + 52 193 tokens,
+0.04 % the token cost for +41 net cases).

`entry-prior` reads 0 fires because the 324 dispatch already shipped it: a replay that fired again would have counted
the same repair twice, and that idempotence is the check that the two columns are one population.

**The ceiling it was built for.** Of the 41 cases whose truth is the entry and whose children rose anyway, **39** are
repaired — exactly the `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` block. The two left are `NetworkPartition` and `NetworkBandwidth`,
families on which the channel does not speak. The rule is invariant to all three tie-breaks tried, and **no case in
the corpus carries two distinct novel callers**, so "the caller" is not a second decision wearing the instrument's
name.

**And the inverse rule is refused.** The 37 remaining witnessed cases carry novelty **arriving at** the entry with
none leaving it. "A shape the entry has never seen means the entry" fires 37 times and is right **15** — **0.405**
where 0.813 is needed. Recorded rather than dropped, because it is the natural next sentence after the one that
worked and the corpus says the two directions are not symmetric.

**The test that would have saved three iterations.** An instrument has to **charge an END**. `novel` works because it
can only be produced by the caller; the fall (`325.14i`) failed because every service in every case lost throughput;
a count (`325.14k`) failed because both ends can make an edge fail. Classifying a candidate as _asymmetric_ or
_symmetric_ before pricing it would have killed all three failed rules in one line each.

## 326 The premise was read in a channel that is usually absent (iteration 326)

`325.15` closed the request-shape axis and left one sentence standing over the rest of the residue: the entry prior is
the arm's second-largest earner (**+57** on the engine's own answers), and it is also the arm's largest source of
harm — on the 325 artifact it renamed a **correct** answer to the front door on **15** cases, and every one of them
is a case whose failing-interface record said the failure had travelled. This iteration found why, and the reason is the same defect in miniature that `325.14i` found
in the fall axis: **the rule read its premise in a channel that is usually not there.**

### 326.1 The premise, and the two channels that can carry it

The entry prior fires when _the sabotage never went past the front door_. Its reading of that sentence was
`entryChildErrors ≤ 0`: the largest error-rate rise among the entry's **direct callees**. Measured over the corpus,
that channel is silent in **1 053 of the 1 054** cases whose callee rose — the pre-window median is zero, `surpriseOf`
refuses a zero level by design, and `delta` is therefore `0` for a series that went `0 → 100`. So a zero in that
column is mostly an **absent instrument wearing the shape of a measured quiet**, and a rule that reads it as evidence
speaks where it has none.

The corpus carries the same statement in a dense channel and the arm had never read it: `failed − baseline > 0` on an
interface whose **callee** sits in the entry's **reachable set**. That is not a level, it is the event itself — a call
below the door began failing — and it contradicts the premise in exactly one direction.

| on the 325 artifact (`44915289950`)                   |  fires | repairs | breaks |     net |               Top@1 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -----: | ------: | -----: | ------: | ------------------: |
| the entry prior as shipped (`entryChildErrors` alone) |     90 |      67 |     16 |     +51 |     1 263 (88.82 %) |
| plus `belowFails`                                     | **83** |  **67** |  **9** | **+58** | **1 270 (89.31 %)** |

**The reading is pure**: it refuses 7 of the rule's 90 fires and **all seven are breaks**, so not one repair is lost.
The same column on the free artifact (`44909105091`) refuses 7 of 85 and moves that composition from 1 279 to
**1 286**. Two artifacts, two populations, the same seven-case block.

### 326.2 What the arm is without a model, stated for the first time beside it

Two resolvers applied to the **engine's own answer**, with no investigation at all, read **1 256 (88.33 %)**:
1 156 + 57 from the entry prior + 43 from the witness (the 43 are witness cases the engine had wrong). Everything
above that number is the model's contribution, and it is small: **+7** on the arm 325 shipped, **+14** after this
iteration, **+30** in the free-arm composition. The LLM is not carrying this arm; it is refining a deterministic
localiser, and every number this programme has published should be read with that sentence attached.

### 326.3 Five localisers priced at ¥0, and all five refused

The 39-case `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` block — truth is the front door, the only failing interface is the traffic
generator's call to it, and the arm answers a deep service — is the largest single pocket left (**38** of 152
residual misses). Five readings of it were written and priced against the same artifact:

| candidate                                          | kind             |   fires | repairs |  breaks |             net |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------: | ------: | ------: | --------------: |
| the sink of the failing-edge subgraph              | region           |     430 |      66 |     348 |        **−282** |
| that sink, ordered by inflow                       | region           |     510 |      71 |     417 |        **−346** |
| the callee of a case's ONLY failing edge           | level + relation |     129 |      44 |      82 |         **−38** |
| the callee of the highest-count failing edge       | level            |     645 |      55 |     554 |        **−499** |
| the sink of the LATENCY-rise subgraph, ρ ∈ [2, 20] | region           | 183–917 |   10–29 | 156–796 | **−767 … −132** |

**The corpus cannot separate the 39 from the 82 cases that look identical in this channel.** Both groups carry one
failing interface, the traffic generator's, into the front door; in one the front door is the truth and in the other
a silent resource stress sits behind it. The candidate that would fix all 39 breaks 82, and every gate tried on the
difference (the answer's own departure, the answer's location, the entry's inbound failure) separates them by less
than the base rate demands. This is a **granularity** answer, not a threshold answer: at service granularity the two
shapes are the same shape.

What does separate them is **which channels** the answer's departure lives in — `container.*`/`k8s.*` (work the
service did) against `http.*`/`hubble*` (a retry storm passing through it) — and that split prices at **1 277
(89.80 %)** for κ = 200. It is **not shipped**: the κ sweep reads 1 248, 1 274, **1 277**, 1 269, 1 260, 1 250, a peak
at one value on one corpus, which is the selection signature this register has refused before. It is the next axis,
with its own cross-validated pre-registration.

### 326.4 Two decisions one argument was carrying

`runQueryAgent` took `seed` and used it for two jobs: the order the prompt **shows** and the order a refusal **falls
back to**. Every published arm showed what it fell back to, so nothing measured the difference — and the free arm
(`seed: null`) had no fallback _by construction_, which is not a property of a free investigation but of the harness
that ran it. The two are now separate (`fallback`, defaulting to `seed`), and the gap they open is the surface a
product with an engine underneath actually has: show nothing, ship the engine's answer unless the model justifies an
override.

A gate the loop enforces must be a gate the prompt states, so `buildUserPrompt` now takes the incumbent instead of
re-deriving it from the seed, and `gateTableCaveat` reads a new `incumbent` column — an artifact that shows no order
and falls back to one executed every policy in its own table, which is precisely what the free arm's caveat says it
did not.

## 327 The premise read where it is measured: 1 286.3 of 1 422 (90.46 %), and what the 130 cases are made of (iteration 327)

Four dispatches read 326 back. None changed a constant, and every one of them is in the band its pre-registration
wrote before it ran.

### 327.1 Run A confirms the ¥0 replay to four cases

| run                | configuration                                   | pre-registered |                         read | verdict            |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------: | ---------------------------: | ------------------ |
| A `45032001904`    | `seed engine`, `gate lag`, `resolve edge-novel` |     1 270 ± 10 |          **1 274 (89.59 %)** | pass               |
| — pass condition 1 | `answeredBy=entry ≤ 84`                         |           ≤ 84 |                       **82** | pass (325 read 90) |
| — pass condition 2 | Top@1 ≥ 1 265                                   |          1 265 |                    **1 274** | pass               |
| — pass condition 3 | `lag` row `top1@resolved ≥ 88.5 %`              |         88.5 % | **89.59 %** (`resolved` 140) | pass               |
| — falsifier        | Top@1 < 1 263                                   |              — |                        1 274 | **not met**        |

The +11 over 325's 1 263 splits into the resolver's **+7** (what the replay priced) and **+4 of trajectory drift**:
A's gate refused 140 overrides where 325 refused 149, so four cases the earlier run settled on the prior were answered
by the model. A replay prices a RULE; a dispatch also moves the ANSWERS, and this is the first iteration whose two
populations were read separately.

### 327.2 Run B: the free arm with an engine fallback is the highest surface this programme has produced

(§327.4 carries the two repeats that turn this single reading into a measured one.)

| run             | configuration                                                         |               Top@1 | tokens              |       cost |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------: | ------------------- | ---------: |
| B `45032153035` | `seed none`, `fallback engine`, `gate contrast`, `resolve edge-novel` | **1 285 (90.37 %)** | 10 211 554 + 46 183 | **¥20.79** |

The pre-registered band was **≥ 1 280 → SOTA on this corpus, with the surface named**. It cleared by five cases. What
makes the reading more than a leaderboard cell is how it decomposes, and the decomposition is read from B's own gate
table — one artifact, three columns, no second dispatch:

| surface                                        |            seeded A |            hybrid B |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------: | ------------------: |
| the model's own answers (no gate, no fallback) |     1 070 (75.25 %) |   **586 (41.21 %)** |
| + the gate, refusing into the engine           |     1 175 (82.63 %) |     1 077 (75.74 %) |
| + the two resolvers (shipped)                  | **1 274 (89.59 %)** | **1 285 (90.37 %)** |

**1. A gate plus a fallback still loses to the engine on the hybrid arm** — 1 077, i.e. **net −79**, the number the
table prints. Deciding _who speaks_ does not decide _what is true_.

**2. The resolvers' yield scales with the number of wrong answers the surface leaves**: +99 cases on the seeded
surface, **+208 on the hybrid one**, +100 on the engine's own answer (1 156 → 1 256). The free arm's weaker raw answers
are raw material rather than a liability, which is why the arm that answers worst alone ends up highest.

**3. The distance from the engine to SOTA is 129 cases: 100 resolvers, 29 model.** Every published number in this
programme should be read with that sentence attached.

### 327.3 The witness, four populations, 496 for 496

| population                                     | renames | correct |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------: | ------: |
| 325a (free, `lag`)                             |     138 |     138 |
| 326 A (seeded, `lag`)                          |      42 |      42 |
| 326 B (hybrid, `contrast`)                     |     150 |     150 |
| the corpus, applied to the engine's own answer |     166 |     166 |

Three gate policies, two seedings, two corpora-worth of cases and no counter-example. The candidate explanation is
about the **generator**, not the system: a fault that does not change a route's code path cannot produce a request
shape the edge has never carried. It is stated as a target for a theorem with a falsifier in `327`'s
pre-registration, not as a result.

### 327.4 The margin, measured: three runs, 1 285 / 1 287 / 1 287

0.37 pp separated 90.37 % from the published 90.0 %, and the arm's run-to-run band was **±10 cases = ±0.70 pp**
(`325.14l`), so one run placed this surface **at** the frontier and said so. Two repeats of exactly B's configuration
were dispatched with their decision rule registered first:

| run              |                 Top@1 | tokens              |   cost | refusals |
| ---------------- | --------------------: | ------------------- | -----: | -------: |
| B `45032153035`  |       1 285 (90.37 %) | 10 211 554 + 46 183 | ¥20.79 |      619 |
| R1 `45040043777` |       1 287 (90.51 %) | 10 256 007 + 46 047 | ¥20.88 |      573 |
| R2 `45040048386` |       1 287 (90.51 %) | 10 244 354 + 46 083 | ¥20.86 |      605 |
| **mean**         | **1 286.3 (90.46 %)** | —                   | ¥20.84 |      599 |

**Three runs, three passes, a spread of two cases.** The registered rule (mean ≥ 1 280, min ≥ 1 270) is met with both
conditions slack, so the claim is "above the bar on average" rather than "at it" — and the spread is **five times
tighter than the ±10-case band** every earlier arm of this programme was judged by, which is itself a finding: that band
was dominated by the seeded arm's dependence on a five-name prior, and a surface that shows one name (or none) varies by
two cases.

**The gate's decisions moved while its errors did not.** Refusals read 619, 573 and 605 across the three runs, the
model answered 636, 683 and 652 cases, and the accuracy moved by two cases. That is the property a gate has to have to
be worth shipping, and it had not been measured before this iteration.

What remains open is not variance but **population**: 1 422 cases here against a 500-case sample there, with no
published per-case results and no published variance on the other side. That inequality is permanent and is stated with
the number rather than under it.

### 327.5 The counter-intuitive reading of 325a, closed

| arm          | prompt shows | a refusal settles on        |                             Top@1 |
| ------------ | ------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------: |
| 325a free    | nothing      | **nothing**                 |                     755 (53.09 %) |
| 326 B hybrid | nothing      | **the engine's first name** | **1 286.3 (90.46 %)**, three runs |

The 28-point deficit against the non-LLM engine was never a property of the model. It was a harness in which a refusal
settled on nothing and a gate enforced a rule the prompt never stated. **An arm's accuracy is a property of the
settlement, not of the model**, and a harness that ignores its engine when the model speaks is worse than no model at
all.

The four positions a deployment can now choose between — advisor off, model only, hybrid, seed only, engine only — and
the measured Top@1 and price of each, are listed in one place in `llm-switches.md`; this row is the axis those positions
were measured on.

## 328 The witness is not weak on the front door — it is SILENT there, and that is a statement about the generator (iteration 328)

The falsifier 327 §3 registered has been walked, and it did not fire. What the walk found is a stronger statement than
the one it was testing.

### 328.1 332 for 332, and the channel exists if and only if the fault rewrites the request

| arm             | cases | carrying a novel-shape interface | truth IS that interface's caller | on a non-rewrite fault |
| --------------- | ----: | -------------------------------: | -------------------------------: | ---------------------: |
| B `45032153035` | 1 422 |                          **166** |                          **166** |                  **0** |
| A `45032001904` | 1 422 |                          **166** |                          **166** |                  **0** |

Two seedings, two fallbacks, 332 witnessed decisions, no counter-example. But the population is the finding:

> the two families present are `HTTPRequestReplaceMethod` (127) and `HTTPRequestReplacePath` (39) and **nothing else**.

**The novelty channel exists on this corpus if and only if the fault rewrites the request.** That is the generator's
property, exactly as the candidate statement predicted, and it has a consequence the count hides: the witness is
**structurally blind to `HTTPResponseReplaceCode`**, the largest residual family (37 of 137 misses at the B surface). A
replaced response code does not change the request a caller sends, so the instrument that has settled 332 decisions
without an error cannot see the family that needs it most. It is not weak there; it is silent, and silence is the
correct reading of its own premise.

### 328.2 What the front door is worth, and what it costs to read it

The same 1 422 rows, decomposed by whether the entry prior could REACH a case at all — premise satisfied
(`belowFails` false, `entryChildErrors` ≤ 0, no witness), answer not already the entry, and refused only by the
300-unit surprise bar:

| population                                                |   cases | largest families                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------: | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **reachable** — the answer is wrong and the premise holds |  **72** | ReplaceCode 34, RequestDelay 7, Partition 7, ResponseDelay 7, RequestAbort 5        |
| **at risk** — the answer is RIGHT and the premise holds   | **153** | JVMMemoryStress 57, ContainerKill 40, NetworkDelay 18, Corrupt 8, Loss 7, PodKill 7 |

A rule that fired on all 225 would need **precision 0.68** to break even on this population, which is why the bar has
to be selective rather than broad. The two populations are also not symmetric in KIND: the at-risk side is dominated
by families whose answer did the work itself (a JVM heap, a killed container), while the reachable side is dominated
by families whose answer only carried traffic. **That asymmetry is the hypothesis the channel split tests, and it is
the first time it has been stated as a population rather than as an anecdote.**

### 328.3 The model does not name the front door, which refutes an axis before it is priced

A tempting ¥0 axis is to widen the GATE instead of the resolver: admit an override that names the entry when the
premise holds, with no contrast required. The artifact prices it in one pass, because `rawAnswer` is recorded:

| reading                                                                 | cases |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----: |
| rows where the model itself answered the ENTRY with the premise holding | **4** |
| of those, already settled on it (and correct)                           |     3 |
| refused, truth IS the entry (repairs)                                   | **1** |
| refused, truth is not (breaks)                                          | **0** |

**+1 case, on a population of 4.** The model does not propose the entrance: on 1 422 cases it names the front door
four times, which is why the front door has to be INFERRED by a resolver (100 cases) rather than asked for. The axis is
recorded as refuted so that nobody re-derives it, and the number is the reason: an arm cannot be widened into a name
its surface never produces.

### 328.4 The channel split is refused — not by its bar, but by NON-IDENTIFIABILITY

Priced at ¥0 as 327 §2 registered: one corpus walk (`run-channel-split.ts`, 1 422 cases, no model call), the answers
read from run B's artifact, the bar held out.

|       κ |  fold 0 |  fold 1 | repairs | breaks |
| ------: | ------: | ------: | ------: | -----: |
|      30 |     638 |     643 |      26 |     30 |
|     100 |     642 |     642 |      32 |     33 |
| **200** | **644** | **645** |  **40** | **36** |
|     300 |     644 |     644 |      40 |     37 |
|     500 |     641 |     644 |      40 |     40 |
|     750 |     640 |     644 |      40 |     41 |

The shipped surface reads 644 / 641 = **1 285**. Both folds select **200**, so the swap is not what refuses it: the
held-out reading is **+0 / +4** against a registered requirement of **+7 on each**. In-sample maximum 1 289, i.e. +4.
**REFUSED**, and the 326 probe's 1 277 is withdrawn rather than reconciled — the probe no longer exists, and the
instrument now in the tree reads a different number at the same bar.

**Where the +4 comes from, and where it goes.** The bar fires 76 times on the corpus, and the entire net is one family
against another:

| fault                     | cases | fires | repairs | breaks |
| ------------------------- | ----: | ----: | ------: | -----: |
| `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` |   231 |    20 |  **20** |  **0** |
| `NetworkDelay`            |    21 |    15 |   **0** | **15** |
| `NetworkCorrupt`          |    46 |    10 |       1 |      8 |
| `HTTPRequestDelay`        |    88 |     8 |       6 |      1 |
| `HTTPResponseDelay`       |    89 |     6 |       5 |      1 |
| `NetworkPartition`        |    97 |     5 |       1 |      3 |
| `HTTPRequestAbort`        |    60 |     3 |       3 |      0 |
| `NetworkBandwidth`        |    42 |     2 |       1 |      0 |
| `HTTPResponseAbort`       |    44 |     2 |       2 |      0 |
| `PodFailure`              |    24 |     2 |       0 |      2 |
| `JVMCPUStress`            |     2 |     1 |       0 |      0 |
| `PodKill`                 |    10 |     1 |       0 |      1 |

**The hypothesis is exactly right for the family it was written for — 20 for 20 — and exactly wrong for
`NetworkDelay`, 0 for 15.** The two net out to +4.

**Why no bar can fix it.** `NetworkDelay` injects latency on the network: the delayed service consumes no CPU, so its
resource side is quiet, and the arm's answer is the true root. `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` rewrites a response at the
door: the deep service it points at also does no work of its own. **The two situations carry the same evidence.** The
populations confirm it at every bar:

| population               | cases | answer's resource p50 / p90 | traffic p50 / p90 | traffic-only at κ = 750 |
| ------------------------ | ----: | --------------------------: | ----------------: | ----------------------: |
| reachable (answer wrong) |    74 |                **30 / 436** |      897 / 11 148 |                  **45** |
| at risk (answer right)   |   153 |             **551 / 5 596** |      791 / 16 663 |                  **41** |

The medians differ by an order of magnitude and the tails overlap completely: 45 of the 74 cases the rule could repair
and 41 of the 153 it could destroy are traffic-shaped under the LOOSEST bar. A sweep of one number cannot cut a set
that both sides occupy.

**What does separate them, and why it cannot be used.** The only column that separates the 20 repairs from the 15
breaks is the rank the engine gave the TRUTH: every repair sits at rank ≥ 5 and every break at rank 1. That column is
label-aware — it is computed from the answer key — so it is an explanation of the failure, not an instrument. The
label-free echo of it (`answer === engineWinner`) does make the rule safe: it drops the 15 breaks and keeps 4 repairs
(**+4 / −0**), inside the arm's own two-case spread, chosen after these numbers were read. It is recorded as a
candidate for a fresh artifact, not shipped.

**The instrument defect found on the way, because it is the reusable part.** The first dispatch of this axis read
**1 287 at every bar and was reported as a refused hypothesis**. It was not a refusal: the artifact records the
surprise per SIDE (`rawSurprise`, `priorSurprise`) and carries no `answerSurprise` key, so a reader that asserted the
settled column's name produced `undefined` on all 1 422 rows — and `entryAttribution` narrows that field by
MEASUREMENT so an older artifact cannot fire. The rule therefore never ran, and six identical rows looked exactly like
a mechanism that does not exist. `toSplitCase` is the guard: it reads the model's column when the model's answer
stands, the prior's when a refusal settled on the prior, refuses to borrow the other side's measurement for a name it
does not describe, and REJECTS a row carrying neither column by name. **A null and an absent key mean different
things, and only one of them is a measurement.**

**What this costs the next axis.** The channel kind is now a measurement the resolver may not read, because on this
corpus it does not identify the thing it was introduced to identify. The next attempt at the 17 `ReplaceCode` misses
the witness cannot reach needs a NEW COLUMN rather than a new bar: the answer's departure split by _what the traffic
says_ (duration against status) is the only remaining candidate that is not already in the evidence, and it is
untested.

## 329 The column exists and the answer cannot carry it: `ReplaceCode` is 34 for 34 on the truth and 0 for 34 on the answer (iteration 329)

328 closed the channel split naming one untested candidate: split the answer's departure by _what the traffic says_,
duration against status. This iteration tested it, and the test failed for a reason that is worth more than the axis.

### 329.1 The census: 87 families, 4 336 262 records, zero status-like

| reading                      | value                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| label families               | **87**                                                                                                    |
| series records               | **4 336 262**                                                                                             |
| families matching a status   | **0**                                                                                                     |
| the only error-shaped family | `http.response.error_rate` (42 695 records), classified **symptom**                                        |
| HTTP latency families        | `http.server.request.duration` 42 714, `.max` 39 935, `http.client.request.duration.max` 18 510            |

The duration/status split is therefore **not available as a new column**. What is available is a channel this corpus
already publishes, which turns the axis from "return when the data arrives" into "the evidence is insufficient here
and will not improve on this corpus" — a much stronger claim, and the one this iteration can defend.

### 329.2 The measurand: the standardised form refuses on the entire gated population

| column                                     | measured on | readable |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------- | -------- |
| `symptom` (standardised surprise)          | 224 / 224   | **0**    |
| `symptomRise` (absolute rise, per request) | 224 / 224   | **224**  |

An error rate is flat at zero before the injection, so the pre-window median is zero and the standardisation has no
denominator. The refusal is not occasional: it lands on **all 224** cases the rule addresses, which is the first whole
population this programme has found to sit on a measurand's refusal. The profile file records both columns and the
sweep reads the absolute rise against rate floors; the reader **refuses a three-slot line by name**, so the cached
file from 328 cannot be read as a quiet symptom.

### 329.3 The conditioned rule is refused, and the separability check let it through

| reading                            |                                          value |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| population at `κ = 750`            |                 **74 reachable / 150 at risk** |
| precision at every floor of the grid | **0.750** (3 reachable ∧ condition, 1 at risk) |
| separable under the registered 0.68 |                                        **YES** |
| every cell of the 30-cell sweep    |                              **648 / 641 (+3 / −1)** |
| selected cell, both folds          |                              `κ 30 / φ 0.0001` |
| held out                           |                          **+3 / −1** — REFUSED |
| in-sample maximum                  |                         **1 289** (never claimed) |

Priced on **both** artifacts — because a refusal that holds on one file is a reading and a refusal that holds on two is
a statement:

| artifact             | sha256             | its own answers | shipped   | held out  | delta     | in-sample max | verdict |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | --------------: | --------- | --------- | --------- | ------------: | ------- |
| run B `45032153035`  | `993e181f67a9565e` | 1 285 (90.37 %) | 644 / 641 | 648 / 640 | **+4 / −1** | 1 288 | REFUSED |
| run R1 `45040043777` | `572952e8ab856422` | 1 287 (90.51 %) | 645 / 642 | 648 / 641 | **+3 / −1** | 1 289 | REFUSED |

Two findings about the instrument, both reusable. **A precision criterion is gameable by a rare condition**: the
condition here fires on 4 of 224 cases, so 3-to-1 clears 0.68 while meaning nothing — and it reads 0.750 on R1 against
0.800 on B for the same configuration, which is the same defect measured twice. **A grid whose optimum is on its
corner has located the edge of where it was allowed to look**, not an optimum — both folds chose the smallest bar and
the smallest floor, and the floor coordinate is perfectly flat across all thirty cells.

### 329.4 The finding: the column separates the populations on the TRUTH, 34 for 34, and on the answer 0 for 34

Everything above is arithmetic. This is the mechanism, and it is why no bar on this channel can work as a resolver.
Over the 34 gated `HTTPResponseReplaceCode` cases:

| population      | error rate rises above zero | median rise |
| --------------- | --------------------------: | ----------: |
| the **truth**   |                  **34 / 34** |  **9.867 %** |
| the **answer**  |                   **0 / 34** |          0 % |

The corpus is not quiet — the **answer** is, and it must be: the gate settled on that service because it was loud in
another channel, and a deep service that returns no errors is precisely a service whose error rate cannot rise. **A
resolver that reads a column on the answer cannot use evidence that is defined on the truth.** `NetworkDelay` reads 0
fires on 18 for the same reason, so the family the axis was written for and the family it was written against both
fall silent together, and the four fires that remain are `HTTPRequestDelay` (1, break), `HTTPResponseDelay` (1,
repair), `HTTPRequestAbort` (1, repair) and `HTTPResponseAbort` (1, repair).

### 329.5 The signal exists and is oriented — and that is not yet a rule

Three diagnostics at ¥0 on artifacts already in hand, three different questions:

| question                                                                                        | reading                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| is the LOUDEST error rate the truth?                                                             | **no** — 12 of 160 on the gated population (7.5 %); the loudest is `loadgenerator` or the dashboard |
| is the **deepest** rising service, by distance from the entry, the truth?                        | **36 of 39** where the answer is wrong (92.3 %), **1 of 52** where it is right (1.9 %) — precision **0.407** on 91 speaks |
| is the deepest rising service across the resource **and** symptom channels the truth?            | **no** — 26 / 74 reachable at a 300 bar (35.1 %), and **0 / 74** at a 30 bar                        |

The error rate rises on the path from the entry down to the source and **stops there**, so the deepest rising service
is a bound from above on where the source sits. That is a property of the generator and it is the first candidate in
this programme whose failure mode is **orientation** rather than strength. It is also the same shared-evidence disease
328 named, in a second measurand: a rule that speaks on 91 of 224 and is right on 36 cannot be licensed by a split
that is defined by already knowing the answer is wrong. 330 pre-registers the question; it is not answered here.

### 329.6 The reconciliation: 644 / 641 → 645 / 642 was two dispatches, not two instruments

328's log recorded the shipped surface at **644 / 641**; the census log recorded **645 / 642**. A two-case shift in the
comparison column of a published number is chased to ground rather than waved through:

| check                                                         | reading                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| caused by the new symptom column?                             | **no** — 328's 3-slot profiles padded to five reproduce it byte for byte |
| does re-resolution move the artifact?                         | **no** — **0 of 1 422** answers move, on **both** artifacts |
| what does the artifact say its own surface is?                 | `agent Top@1 1285` on B, `1287` on R1, in their own logs  |
| which runs are these?                                          | 328 priced **run B**, the census priced **run R1** — `327.4` |
| how wide is that band?                                         | **±2 cases**, measured over three runs                   |

Both files were then downloaded and priced: B's sha256 `993e181f67a9565e` reads **644 / 641 = 1 285** and reproduces
328's sweep **cell for cell** (638/643, 642/642, 644/645, 644/644, 641/644, 640/644, pooled +0/+4, at-risk **153**);
R1's `572952e8ab856422` reads **645 / 642 = 1 287**. So the difference is the measured dispatch band and nothing else. The instrument was never
wrong; the log was under-determined. Three changes ship to make that impossible to repeat: `surfaceReading` prints
what the artifact says before any rule reads it, to **two decimals** (1 285 and 1 287 of 1 422 are 90.37 % and 90.51 %,
which one decimal renders as one number); the runner prints the artifact's **sha256** beside it; and the runner prints
how many answers the resolvers move on re-application — the invariant that makes the baseline a re-reading rather
than a second opinion, printing `WARNING: the baseline is not the file` when it is not zero.

One number in this register moves with that identification: the at-risk population reads **150** here against 328's
**153**, while reachable reads **74** in both. The at-risk half is defined by the answers being right, so it moves with
the dispatch; the reachable half is defined by the answer being wrong and the gate firing, which is stable.

### 329.7 What ships, and what is closed

| item                                    | state                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ENTRY_PRIOR_TRAFFIC_KAPPA`             | `null` — unchanged since 328                                                            |
| `ENTRY_PRIOR_SYMPTOM_FLOOR`             | `null` — the axis ships disabled, so the rule is byte-for-byte 324–328 behaviour        |
| surface                                 | **1 286.3 (90.46 %)**, three runs — unchanged                                          |
| model spend                             | **¥0** — no arm ran; the census dispatch buys no paid arm and the guard was verified    |
| instrument                              | census, 5-slot profile file, separability check, conditioned sweep, surface reading with digest, re-resolution invariant |

**Closed**: the axis is refused on both of its readings — the column does not exist as a new column (§329.1) and the
conditioning that replaces it repairs 3 and breaks 1 against a requirement of 7 per fold (§329.3). The publishable
claim is the strong one: **`HTTPResponseReplaceCode` is unreachable from per-case evidence read on the answer, on the
response side, on this corpus as it is published** — and §329.4 is the reason, measured 34 for 34 on the other side.

## 330 The bound is real and depth is the wrong way to state it: 0 repairs against 104 breaks, and a control that loses less (iteration 330)

329 left one question: is there a statement the case carries, rather than a knowledge of the answer, that separates
the 39-from-52 asymmetry? This iteration pre-registered one — **the source lies on the path from the entry to the
deepest rising service** — and priced it at ¥0 on two artifacts. It is refuted, and the refutation is more useful than
the axis would have been.

### 330.1 The population is now triple-confirmed, and that is what makes the refutation clean

| reading at the priced bar (750)   | run R1 (1 287) | run B (1 285) | 328 / 329 recorded |
| --------------------------------- | -------------: | ------------: | -----------------: |
| cases the front door addresses    |        **224** |       **227** |           224 / — |
| … the answer gets wrong           |         **74** |        **74** |                 74 |
| … the answer gets right           |        **150** |       **153** |            153 / 150 |
| the rung exists on                |            219 |           222 |                 — |
| **the rung IS the truth** (wrong) |          **0** |         **0** |  329's instrument read 36 of 39 |

Three instruments, three dispatches, one population. **The population was never the disagreement; the rule always
was**, and that is now a measured statement rather than a hope.

### 330.2 The predictions, and the one that held while damning the rule

| prediction                                        | predicted      | read (R1 / B)                  | verdict |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------ | ------- |
| P1 the rung is the truth where the answer is wrong | ≥ 30 / 39      | **0 / 74** and 0 / 74          | **FALSIFIED** |
| P2 the law silences it where the answer is right   | ≤ 10 breaks    | **104 / 106 breaks**           | **FALSIFIED** |
| P3 it fires where the answer is wrong              | ≥ 15           | **60 / 60**                    | **MET** |
| P4 held out ≥ +7 on each fold                      | +7 / +7        | **−55 / −49** and −57 / −49    | **FALSIFIED** |
| P5 the relation beats the randomised control       | control ≤ 0    | rule **−55 / −49**, control **−41 / −39** → difference **−24** | **FALSIFIED, inverted** |

P3 held and it is the reason the axis dies: the bound does fire on 60 of 74 wrong answers, and it is wrong about where
to send them **60 times out of 60**.

### 330.3 The mechanism: depth over a call graph is a diameter statistic

`ts-ui-dashboard` fans out to forty services, so the deepest node of the DAG is a leaf on a branch nobody is failing
on. The rising set is large — 219 of 224 addressed cases carry one — so its deepest member is nearly always the most
distant node in the graph, and the answer is almost never an ancestor of it. **A rise propagates along the route a
call takes; the graph's depth measures the graph, not the route.** That is the whole finding, and it explains why the
control loses less: a pseudo-random member of the same rising set is occasionally near the truth, while the deepest
member is the one node the answer can least plausibly be an ancestor of.

### 330.4 The reach reading, and why it is reported rather than hidden

| population                                   | fires | repairs | breaks |  delta |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----: | ------: | -----: | -----: |
| the front door's population (`addressed`)     |   164 |       0 |    104 | −55/−49 |
| every case, premise or not (`all`)            |   878 |       9 |    779 | −386/−384 |

The relation is not a whole-corpus statement either. The premise does not create the harm; it bounds it to 224 cases,
which is the difference between an axis that fails and an axis that destroys the surface.

### 330.5 What ships, and what 331 inherits

**Nothing ships.** `renamedUnder` has no caller in the product path; the surface stays **1 286.3 (90.46 %)** at
**¥0.0147** per case. The instrument ships at 100 % statements, branches, functions and lines: `channel-ancestry.ts`,
its runner, the `population` parameter that separates the pipeline's population from the relation's reach, and the
control that holds the firing population constant while destroying the relation.

331 inherits a sharper question than it would have had: **the bound has to be stated on the engine's own path — the
containment chain — rather than on the call graph's depth.** A rise travels a route; the chain is the engine's
hypothesis about which route, and it is already written into every artifact. Depth over the DAG measured the
diameter and paid 104 correct answers to learn it.

This row is not a closed axis. It is a **cancelled purchase**, recorded here because the register's job is to stop an

## 331 The head-precedence rule: a loud head is what a conduit looks like (iteration 331)

Pre-registered in `docs-repository:preregistration-331.md` and priced at **¥0** on both artifacts. The rule — *a
resolver may not take an answer away from a head that is itself loud* — was refuted on its mechanism, not on its
margin, and the refutation is a proof rather than a measurement.

| reading | prediction | run R1 (`572952e8ab856422`, 1 287) | run B (`993e181f67a9565e`, 1 285) |
| ------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------: | -------------------------------: |
| P1: of the wrong overrides, the head is loud at κ=300 | ≥ 8 of 10 | **1** | **0** |
| P2: of the right overrides, the head is loud at κ=300 | ≤ 20 % | **37.2 %** (81/218) | 36.7 % (80/218) |
| P3: held-out gain | ≥ +7 each fold | −13 / −4, best cell on the grid corner | −14 / −6 |
| P4: model answers touched | 0 | **0** | 0 |

### 331.1 Why it cannot fire, in one sentence and then in numbers

The guard asks whether the **fusion head** is loud; the front-door resolver asks whether **the answer it is about to
rename** is quiet — at the same bar — so the two questions are negations of each other on the population the rule
targets. On all ten wrongly overridden cases the head **is** the engine winner, so the premise had been read on that
very service, and nine of the ten heads sit at 53.8, 66.2, 96.4, 107.7, 131.2, 156.0, 189.0, 223.9 and 282.6 — all
under the resolver's own bar of 300, which is why it fired. At bars low enough to reach them (κ = 30 reaches 10 of 10)
the guard also fires on **195 of 218** overrides that were right, because a conduit's traffic channel is loud by
definition.

### 331.2 The tenth case, and the residue that becomes 332

`ts4-ts-inside-payment-service-stress-gc2kcm`: head `ts-inside-payment-service` at departure **5 596**, `priorSurprise`
5 596, `rawAnswer` `ts-order-service` at departure **250** — and the front door renamed **the model's** answer, not the
head. The resolver's premise is applied to *the last answer in the chain*, which is the model's whenever the model
spoke; the guard was pointed at a service the resolver never examined. A rule that polices this rename must be stated
over the answer the resolver is about to replace. That is pre-registered as 332 and is not a re-reading of this one.

### 331.3 What ships

The instrument only: `benchmarks/src/head-precedence.ts` (38 tests, coverage 100/100/100/100 across statements,
branches, functions and lines) and `benchmarks/src/run-head-precedence.ts`, which prints both artifacts' digests
before any table. The rule ships nowhere. **Axes this closes.** One: "loudness of the head" as a guard on resolver
precedence. **Axes this opens.** One: the resolver's input is the model's answer, and that is a population nobody has
priced.

## 332 The first hop SHIPS: the boundary of the case separates the door from a leaf the request path never touched (iteration 332)

This is the register's first **shipped** row rather than a closure, and it is recorded here because the numbers it
replaces are in this file. Pre-registered in `docs-repository:preregistration-332.md` and pushed (`990b4666`) before
the reading existed; priced at **¥0** on both artifacts.

> **When the only failing boundary of a case is the door's inbound edge, the answer is the door** — no child of the
> door reports an error, no measured edge below the door failed, and requests failed on the way in by more than 50.

| reading | prediction | run R1 (`572952e8ab856422`, 1 287) | run B (`993e181f67a9565e`, 1 285) |
| ------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------: | -------------------------------: |
| chosen cell, both folds | interior | **50 / 50** | **50 / 50** |
| held-out gain, fold 0 / fold 1 | ≥ +7 each | **+10 / +11** | **+9 / +11** |
| precision at the chosen cell | ≥ 0.75 | **0.800** | **0.763** |
| firings outside the population | 0 | **0** | **0** |
| whole-corpus delta | — | **+21** → 1 308 (**91.98 %**) | **+20** → 1 305 (91.77 %) |

### 332.1 The population, which is the larger finding

| | cases | already right | door is the truth | rule fires |
| - | ----: | ------------: | ----------------: | ---------: |
| nothing below the door fails (`entryChildErrors = 0`, `belowFails = false`) | **318** | 231 | **145** | 58 |
| everything else | 1 104 | 1 056 | — | 0 |

The premise **alone** loses 86 cases (64 repairs against 150 breaks, precision 0.30): it cannot tell a door-self fault
from a **leaf fault the request path never exercised** — `ts-consign-service`, `ts-cancel-service`,
`ts-contacts-service` under stress or pod failure, whose anomaly is real and whose failing calls never reach the door.
Every channel column was measured and refused as a conditioning signal: the door's own-work departure reads 6.74 in the
repairs against 6.18 in the breaks, its traffic reads **53.65 against 98.98** (louder when the fault is elsewhere,
because the rest of the system is still working through it), and the conduit test on the named answer reaches precision
**0.500**. The column that separates them is the failure count on the edge that enters the system: 0.814 precision at
β=50 against 0.414 at β=0.

### 332.2 Why this is not the coefficient §320 refused

§320.4 refused every form of *"make the entry point's own numbers louder"*, and for a measured reason: the entry sits
18–45 metric ranks below the winner, a log-space gap of 0.18–0.45 against a term bounded by 0.005 — *"a tie-break
bounded by one step cannot close a thirty-rank gap."* This rule does not touch the score, does not promote the entry in
any ranking, and does not read the entry's numbers; it reads the case's **failure boundary** and overrides the answer
of every channel when the failure provably never crossed the door. The two statements are compatible, which is why
§320 could be right and this can still pay.

### 332.3 What ships, and the one number that is not yet measured

`ENTRY_FIRST_HOP_BETA = 50`, applied last in `applyResolver` (so it overrides the witness, the front door and the
model, and the loop's single exit cannot forget it), with the evidence column computed in `readEntryPrior` from the
same edge list the `belowFails` clause walks. `null` is the off switch and restores the 324–331 surface byte for byte.
Coverage of the new instrument: `first-hop.ts` at 100/100/100/100 across 29 tests, and the shipped rule is tested
through `applyResolver` itself rather than through the instrument — 307 tests in `query-agent.test.ts`.

**91.98 % is a replayed surface, not a counterfactual — and confirming it needs no dispatch** (iteration 333, §333).
The rule replaces an answer without reading the model's reasoning, so applying it to a published artifact's rows is
exact; and because every changed row is changed **to the door** — a name the case's own failure boundary supplies —
none of those 37 rows costs a model call, while the 1 385 untouched rows take a branch byte for byte identical to the
one that produced the paid answers. The dispatch the plan budgeted at ≈ ¥21 buys nothing here. The rule also pre-empts
the model on the cases it settles, which is ~4 % of the arm's calls saved rather than spent.

## 333 The confirmation costs nothing: the rule answers 37 rows itself and 1 385 rows are already paid for (iteration 333)

The plan's first item was a full-corpus dispatch (**≈ ¥21**) to turn 91.98 % into a measurement, and the queue behind
it was priced at **≈ ¥100**. Both prices were read again, at **¥0**, against the artifacts that already exist. The full
reading, with the five buckets, the residual and the falsifiers, is `cost-audit-333.md`.

> **A surface whose changed rows are named by the case, and whose unchanged rows run the same program on the same
> input, is replayed rather than re-dispatched.**

| bucket | R1 | B | does producing this answer read a model? |
| ------ | -: | -: | ---------------------------------------- |
| repaired (moved to the door, wrong before) | 28 | 29 | no |
| broken (moved to the door, right before) | 7 | 9 | no |
| moved to a door that is not the truth | 2 | 0 | no |
| moved inside a multi-service truth set | 0 | 0 | no |
| untouched (the paid answer stands) | **1 385** | **1 384** | already paid for |

### 333.1 What makes the 37 rows free

`doorAttribution` returns the case's entry service, decided by three of the case's own columns, and it is applied
**last** in `applyResolver`. A dispatch over those rows would pay a completion whose output is then discarded: the
answer is the door whether or not the model agrees.

### 333.2 What makes the 1 385 rows free

When the rule is silent, `doorAttribution` returns `null` and `applyResolver` falls through to the branch it always
took. The `null`-reproduces-324–331 test (§332.3) is the byte-for-byte check, and the column the rule adds is
read-only. The shipping pipeline and the pipeline that produced the artifact are therefore the same program on the
same input for these rows.

### 333.3 The one residual, and its price

The replay assumes a frozen endpoint reproduces the paid answers. `temperature` is 0 and the prompt is fixed, so a
**50-case stratified sample** re-dispatched bounds it at `50 × ¥0.0147 ≈ **¥0.74**`, and reports a reproduction rate
directly. It is optional; it is the only purchase this iteration names.

### 333.4 The rest of the queue

Retrieval (74 misses, truth at engine rank 6–44, median 22) is a **local re-rank** — the engine is deterministic and
calls no endpoint, so widening the seed cannot trip the Zhipu 429 that paused the embedding benchmark. The resolver
scope (10 cases) is a code change over columns already in the artifact. The RCAEval nine-cell replication is a join.
Process-level evidence is **¥2.94** if a venue requires full transcripts, and zero otherwise. **Queue: ¥0, ceiling
¥2.94.**

### 333.5 A counting correction in the runner's table

The per-bar table counted *"the paid answer was wrong"* as a repair, which credits the two rows moved to a door that is
not the truth with a gain they did not earn — 30/7 at bar 50 where the instrument reads 28/7. The table now reads
`replaySurface`, so the table and the surface line cannot disagree. The register's **+21** was always right: it came
from the instrument, and the table was the only place the wrong count appeared.

**Axes this closes.** Two: "confirmation requires a dispatch" as a cost, and "the remaining queue costs ≈ ¥100".
**Axes this opens.** One: model drift as a measured quantity rather than an assumption, priced at ¥0.74.

## 335 The 135 misses are four failures, and only one of them is a budget (iteration 334)

The queue behind 91.98 % had two items — the retrieval block (74 cases whose truth the model never saw) and a
resolver-scope question. Both were read at **¥0**, and the reading split the misses into four populations that every
earlier plan had averaged into one number. The full reading is `retrieval-block-334.md`.

| class | cases | what a budget would buy |
| ----- | ----: | ----------------------- |
| hit | 1 287 | — |
| lost at the rank one | 20 | precedence |
| seen but lost (truth in the seed) | 41 | reasoning |
| **retrieval block (truth never shown)** | **74** | **breadth** |
| absent (truth not a candidate) | **0** | pool |

**Zero absent** closes the pool direction outright: the engine's candidate set is complete on this corpus. Breadth
buys visibility and nothing else — width 5 / 10 / 22 / 44 makes 61 / 75 / 99 / 135 misses visible — and the two bars a
deployed pipeline could read are both refuted here.

### 335.1 Two refutations

* **The engine's own indecision does not identify a block.** The gap between its first two candidates reaches the
  block at precision 0.115–0.170 (§`retrieval-block-334.md` §3); a widening rule keyed on it would spend most of its
  tokens on hits.
* **No single term ranks the block.** Its truth is stronger on `stability` in 64 of 74 cases and on `temporal` in
  43 of 65 — a source against a conduit — but ranking by either term localises 5.4 % and 6.8 % of the block. A
  difference of means is not a decision rule, and this is the third time this register has measured the distinction.

### 335.2 The candidate that is measured and not shipped

> A resolver may not rename a case whose engine leads its second candidate by more than 1.5.

Not 331's guard: that read the ANSWER's loudness (the resolver's own premise backwards); this reads a margin about the
ENGINE. The front door's harm concentrates exactly here — 12 of 81 overrides wrong, median margin 3.34, against 0.03 on
the 69 it got right. Held out on the surface the first-hop rule ships: **+10 / +10**, precision **1.000 / 1.000**,
whole-corpus counterfactual **1 328 / 1 422 = 93.39 %**.

**It does not ship, and the reason is a scope gap rather than a doubt.** The margin lives in `terms.ndjson`, whose
ordering differs from the shipped ordering on **83 of 1 422** cases; the guard touches 13 cases of which **12** agree on
both candidates. A bar computed on a possibly different second candidate is not yet the product's bar. The engine
already computes the gated scores — one local re-run that writes them is **¥0 and calls no endpoint** — and on that
column the reading either reproduces (ship, +20 cases) or does not (refuse).

**Axes this closes.** Three: "the candidates are missing" (absent = 0), "widen when the engine is undecided" (precision
≤ 0.17), and "a single term can order the block" (≤ 6.8 %). **Axes this opens.** One: the gated margin as a product
column, which is the only thing standing between the measured 93.39 % and a shipped one.

## 336 The engine-certainty guard SHIPS: the margin was the wrong pair, and the product now carries the right one (iteration 336)

Iteration 334 withheld a **+20** because its margin came from a score-sorted dump while the product publishes an order
that is not a function of the scores, and the two orders disagree on **83 of 1 422** cases. Both halves of that gap are
closed here at **¥0**, and the rule ships: **1 308 → 1 328 / 1 422 (91.98 % → 93.39 %)**, held out **+10 / +10** at
precision **1.000 / 1.000** on both artifacts. The full reading is `engine-certainty-336.md`.

| closure | how it was closed | what it cost |
| ------- | ----------------- | ------------ |
| the pair | the margin is `score(published[0]) − score(published[1])`, so a negative margin is a real configuration rather than a corrupt row | ¥0 |
| the column | `per-case.ndjson` gains `top1Score` / `top2Score`, and a local engine re-run reproduces the shipped order on **1 422 of 1 422** cases | ¥0 (15 m 56 s, no endpoint) |
| the two sources | `worst \\|score − Σ w·slope\\| = 0.000e+0` over **69 688** candidates, so the dump's score IS the engine's `finalScore` | ¥0 |

**It ships inside `applyResolver`, applied last**, with `ENGINE_CERTAINTY_MARGIN = 1.5` as both the product switch and
the ablation switch (`null` restores 335 byte for byte) and `engineMargin` recorded on every arm row so an artifact can
be asked which cases the rule was allowed to answer for. The reading is flat from **1.0 to 2.0** on both folds of both
artifacts, so 1.5 is inside a plateau rather than on its slope.

**A defect the equivalence test found.** The instrument and the product are two implementations of one statement, and a
grid test (3 answers × 3 engine tops × 6 margins × 8 bars) now requires them to settle on the same name. It failed on
its first run: `certaintyUnder` compared `margin <= bar`, and `NaN <= 1.5` is false, so a **failed measurement** read as
a decided engine. The product had already narrowed by `Number.isFinite`. Fixed in the instrument — `null` and `NaN` are
the same absence — and the test is the fence.

**Axes this closes.** One: "the guard's input is not a product column" — the reason 334 could not ship. **Axes this
leaves open.** The 74 retrieval misses (truth at engine rank 6–44, breadth the only axis that reaches them and both
deployable bars refuted in 334), and model drift (50-case stratified bound, `≈ ¥0.74`, publication-only).

## 337 The 94 misses have names, and no promotion rule buys them (iteration 337)

The surface is unchanged at **1 328 / 1 422 = 93.39 %** and the iteration is ¥0. `benchmarks/src/miss-ledger.ts` (44
tests, coverage 100 / 100 / 100 / 100) classifies every miss from four pinned artifacts and prices the rule families
that could have bought them. The full reading, with the digests of the four inputs and the reproduce command, is
`miss-ledger-337.md`.

### 337.1 The ledger, read from the artifact rather than from a configuration

| class | cases | channel split (model / prior / interface / entry) |
| ----- | ----: | ------------------------------------------------ |
| engine-was-right | 9 | 6 / — / — / 3 |
| seen-not-taken | 37 | 17 / 19 / — / 1 |
| breadth | 48 | 28 / 19 / — / 1 |
| absent | 0 | — |

The boundaries are the engine's own `truthRank` — its rank among **all** candidates — so rank 1 is precedence, 2–5 is
reasoning, 6 and beyond is breadth, and an unranked truth is a pool failure. **Absent is zero again**, on a better
surface than 334's.

### 337.2 `unwidenable 20`: breadth's addressable ceiling is 28

Twenty of the forty-eight breadth misses were settled by a channel that never reads the seed. A widening arm pays tokens
on every case it is applied to and cannot touch those twenty at any width, so the axis's ceiling is **28**, not 48 — the
number the next plan has to be written against.

### 337.3 Four promotion scopings, four negative prices

| rule | fires | repairs | breaks | delta | precision |
| ---- | ----: | ------: | -----: | ----: | --------: |
| model agrees with the engine → publish the engine | 62 | 1 | 59 | −58 | 0.017 |
| engine over the model's channel | 78 | 6 | 60 | −54 | 0.091 |
| engine over any channel | 205 | 9 | 181 | −172 | 0.047 |
| engine over a quiet answer | 83 | 1 | 77 | −76 | 0.013 |

The engine alone is right on **1 156** and the pipeline on **1 328**: the channels earn **+172** by moving away from the
engine, and the nine residues are that trade's price. This is the fourth precedence family refused (§331 loudness, §332
head, §336 margin, §337 promotion) and the first with the price beside the prize.

### 337.4 The stability axis of §336 is closed

The share of the margin carried by its largest single term, on the surface the guard is added to, at bar 0.5: repairs
**0.867 / 1.011 / 1.377**, breaks **0.404 / 1.114 / 1.570** — the breaks' interval contains the repairs', `separates
false`. Structural rather than statistical: every one of the 20 shipped repairs carries ≥ **86.7 %** of its margin on
`selfAnomaly`, so a statistic dominated by the theory's own quantity cannot separate good decisions from bad.

**Axes this closes.** Four: "reclaim the residue by promoting the engine" (four scopings, −54 to −172), "separate the
guard's repairs from its breaks by term concentration" (`separates false`), "a widened seed reaches the breadth block"
(at most 28 addressable), and "the LLM arm is worse than the engine" (the arm reads 1 287 against 1 156; what loses is
the model's naming as the answer, 615 of 1 422). **Axes this opens.** Three, all external: CIE's **conjunctive**
internal × external score (arXiv:2601.21359v2; ours is additive and only bounded), DecompRCA's system-description prompt
(**+7..+18**, aimed at the 37 seen-not-taken), and Cloud-OpsBench's **evidence-closure** metric (754 cases, 29–33 % of
correct answers fail closure).

## 338 What each implementation contributes, and the first competitor with a theorem (iteration 338)

Iteration 338 is **¥0** and the surface is unchanged: **1 328 / 1 422 = 93.39 %** on the arm's answers, **1 156**
(81.29 %) for the engine alone, **1 073** (75.46 %) for the written sum's own order. It adds the table this register has
been missing since the first ablation — what each term in the score contributes, in the target's own units — and it
runs CIE's theorem against our pool. Full reading: `term-marginal-338.md`.

### 338.1 The ledger: two terms carry 541 of 1 073 decisions, eleven are inert

`benchmarks/src/term-marginal.ts` (33 tests, coverage 100 / 100 / 100 / 100) removes one term from every sum, re-orders
every pool and reports the change in Top-1, with the count of *ties* the removal created printed beside it.

| term | marginal | ties | role |
| ---- | -------: | ---: | ---- |
| `log` (binary evidence) | **−341** | 6 | load-bearing |
| `podState` (8.0, 100 % precision on 294 cases) | **−200** | 2 | load-bearing |
| `selfAnomalyLog1p` (the kinetic onset term) | **+5** | **60** | **tie-maker** |
| `lat` | −58 | 2 | load-bearing |
| `failedEdge` | −42 | 0 | load-bearing |
| `dualFamily`, `stability`, `pool` | 0 | 0–2 | decorative |
| six terms at weight 0 and five never measured | 0 | 0 | inert |

Two readings are new and both are uncomfortable.

1. **The kinetic term's marginal is positive, and its gain is ties.** Removing `selfAnomalyLog1p` makes 60 pools tie at
   the top, and the tie is settled by the pool's arrival order — the engine's published order. Its whole range is
   `log1p(1) = 0.6931`, smaller than a single binary `log` bonus (`1.0`) and one ninth of a `podState` bonus (`8.0`).
2. **Where the deviation is the only thing in the pool, it does not identify the root.** Partitioning the corpus by
   whether *any* candidate carries a non-zero evidence term: **1 072 / 1 368 (78.36 %)** where something was observed,
   **1 / 54 (1.85 %)** where only the deviation was. The partition is structural — drawn on the pool, not on the
   winner — so it is not a function of the outcome it explains.

### 338.2 The classifier was wrong and the data said so

The first version called a term `decorative` when its largest possible contribution was below the corpus's median
decision gap (0.6277). It classified `lat` decorative, and removing `lat` costs 58 cases: the cases `lat` decides are
exactly the ones whose gap is below the median. A corpus-wide statistic cannot classify a term that decides a
sub-population, so the roles are now entirely measured — `inert`, `load-bearing`, `decorative`, `tie-maker`,
`harmful` — and the gap is context in the table rather than a threshold. Second instrument defect found by running a
new module on real data; like §336's `NaN`, it was in the instrument and not in the product.

### 338.3 The sum's order is not the engine's order, and the register must say which it quotes

Two relational passes reorder the list *after* scoring, so the engine publishes **1 156** correct first choices while
the written sum's maximum is right on **1 073** — **83** cases of difference. Every marginal above is a property of
the sum. The runner prints both numbers with the count of disagreements on the same line, so neither can be quoted as
the other.

### 338.4 CIE's conjunction: refused on every mode, and the reason is our own decomposition

Three modes of the conjunction (minimum of the normalised axes, product of the normalised axes, raw product) were
measured under **four specifications of the external axis**, all printed by `run-conjunctive.ts` from the same dump:

| external axis | normMin | normProduct | product |
| ------------- | ------: | ----------: | ------: |
| the eight external channels, shipped weights | 800 | 800 | 800 |
| the same eight, at their measured values | **492** | 499 | 499 |
| propagated failure only (`rise`, `temporal`, `collision`) | 193 | 199 | 199 |
| downstream `rise` only | 190 | 201 | 201 |

Additive reference: 1 073. Refused under every specification, on every mode and on both folds.

The structural reason is the finding worth keeping: **the external axis carries weight `0` in the shipped vector on
this corpus.** Six propagation terms are inert (§338.1), so the axis reduces to `lat` (14.5 % of candidates) and
`failedEdge` (5.6 %); the conjunction then ranks the 15 % that carry it and discards the rest. Rebuilding the axis from
the *unweighted* values does not help, and not because it stays sparse — **53 893 of 69 688** candidates carry a
positive external deviation once the values are read. The trend across the four specifications is monotone in how much
of the external axis the conjunction is handed (800 → 492 → 193 → 190), which is the opposite of what a theorem about
that axis predicts. Separately, adding `rise`, `temporal` or `collision` to the additive score at any non-zero weight
gives 209, 60 and 80 cases, flat across 0.02 to 0.4, because those terms are anti-predictive as written.

**Correction.** An earlier draft of this section quoted **745 / 748 / 748** for a "faithful mapping" and 2 400
candidates carrying an external deviation. That specification is not in the repository and no subset of the eleven
non-internal channels the dump carries reproduces it (exhaustive: 2 048 subsets, two internal definitions, no `normMin`
of 745). The number is withdrawn; the four rows above replace it and are the runner's own output.

**Axes this closes.** Three: "adopt CIE's conjunctive score" (three modes, four specifications of the axis, both folds,
all negative), "re-enable the propagation terms to build the external axis" (flat and catastrophic at every weight),
and — the iteration's own specification — "define the external axis as a **pool-relative share** of propagated
failure" (the normalised modes divide by the pool's maximum, so rows 3 and 4 are exactly that, and they are the worst
readings). The last is the decisive one: the dump carries the unweighted values, so the specification was tested before
anyone built it. What closes the direction is the framework's **premise** — CIE scores deviation magnitude and nothing
else, while 541 of our cases are carried by `log` and `podState`, which a conjunction over two deviation axes cannot
see. **Axes this opens.** None from CIE; the next opening is elsewhere.

### 338.5 The published-surface ladder: two terms are one-directional, one is a cliff

Nine local runs (¥0, no endpoint, ~16 min each) moved one weight and re-ran the whole corpus. The baseline reproduces
the published artifact **byte for byte** (`sha256 da336800ec7c0ce1…`), so every delta is the flag's.

| configuration | Top@1 | delta | repairs / breaks |
| ------------- | ----: | ----: | ---------------: |
| shipped | **1 156** | — | — |
| `--self-anomaly-weight 0.5` | **1 159** | **+3** | 5 / 2 |
| `--self-anomaly-weight 0` | 1 158 | +2 | 16 / 14 |
| `--pod-state-weight 4` | 1 155 | −1 | 0 / 1 |
| `--dual-family-weight 0 --stability-weight 0` | 1 156 | 0 | 6 / 6 |
| `--log-weight 2` | 1 148 | −8 | 4 / 12 |
| `--self-anomaly-weight 2` | 1 119 | −37 | 0 / 37 |
| `--failed-edge-weight 0` | 1 110 | −46 | 0 / 46 |
| `--lat-weight 0` | 1 086 | −70 | 3 / 73 |

`lat` and `failedEdge` lose cases in one direction only (3/73 and 0/46): a term whose removal is near-pure loss is
doing work no other term does — the opposite of what a marginal over the sum said about `lat`, and the defect §338.2
records. `podState` is at a plateau (halving an 8.0 bonus moves one case) and the decorative pair is exactly neutral
(6/6, 81 cases moved, net 0), which is the first independent confirmation of a role from §338.1.

The kinetic weight sits **just inside a cliff**: ×2 repairs nothing and breaks 37, ×0.5 repairs 5 and breaks 2 and is
positive in both folds. 0.5 is therefore the better default on robustness grounds as well as accuracy (+3, +2 top-3,
+1 top-5), but seven flips do not mandate a default change that also alters what the arm is asked — the next dispatch
(≈¥21) settles it on the surface that ships.

## 339 The competitor's metric is our metric, and their AC@1 is bounded by it (iteration 339)

**Owner of:** `docs/cutoff-accuracy-339.md` — the reading, its floors, the nine unmeasured census rows and the
reproduction commands. This entry is the register's summary of it, not a substitute for it.

The register carried the closest competitor — DeCoR / RICE-CM, `DOI 10.1186/s13677-026-01009-x`, which **assumes a
known fault-onset time** and is therefore the one external method whose premise matches `detectMADOnset` — behind the
sentence *"its metric is Avg@5, ours is Acc@1, so the numbers are not comparable directly"*. That sentence was wrong.
`Avg@5` is `(1/k) Σ_{j=1..k} AC@j` by its own abbreviations table, every term is an indicator on one integer, and the
census this repository writes after every RCAEval run carries that integer (`truthRank`) and the pool it was ranked in
(`pool`). The gap was a missing **column**, not a missing population, and `benchmarks/src/cutoff-accuracy.ts` supplies
it as a module (`37` tests, `100/100/100/100`) rather than as a paragraph.

**The nine cells** (census of run `45314745837` at `9588dda4`, digests `62dd882e…` / `b126a462…` / `3118005c…`,
byte-identical to the previous full run's):

| cell | n | AC@1 | AC@3 | AC@5 | Avg@5 | floor |
| ---- | -: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ----: | ----: |
| RE1:OnlineBoutique | 125 | 90.4 % | 96.0 % | 100 % | 96.2 % | 56.5 % |
| RE1:SockShop | 123 | 96.7 % | 100 % | 100 % | 99.0 % | 30.3 % |
| RE1:TrainTicket | 125 | 90.4 % | 96.8 % | 99.2 % | 95.7 % | 4.7 % |
| RE2:OnlineBoutique | 87 | 96.6 % | 97.7 % | 100 % | 98.2 % | 39.5 % |
| RE2:SockShop | 89 | 100 % | 100 % | 100 % | 100 % | 25.7 % |
| RE2:TrainTicket | 90 | 84.4 % | 87.8 % | 90.0 % | 88.0 % | 4.4 % |
| RE3:OnlineBoutique | 27 | 96.3 % | 96.3 % | 96.3 % | 96.3 % | 34.6 % |
| RE3:SockShop | 30 | 80.0 % | 93.3 % | 93.3 % | 89.3 % | 23.4 % |
| RE3:TrainTicket | 30 | 73.3 % | 83.3 % | 86.7 % | 81.3 % | 4.4 % |
| **pooled** | 726 | 91.7 % | 95.9 % | 97.7 % | **95.4 %** | 26.5 % |

`abs` is zero on all nine cells: every miss on this corpus is a **depth** miss, which is the shape the 1 422-case
ledger prices as breadth.

**The comparison, and the bound that needs no protocol assumption.** DeCoR reports `0.6000 / 0.7040 / 0.4864` on a
300-case subset of SS1 / SS2 / OB. Our reading on those fleets is `Avg@5 ≥ 0.893` on every Sock Shop suite and
`≥ 0.962` on every Online Boutique suite — invariant under the mapping, because which of `RE1/RE2/RE3` is their "SS1"
is not published and all three exceed their best cell either way. Stronger, and independent of any mapping:
`Avg@k ≥ AC@1` **by definition**, so a method that publishes only a cutoff average publishes an upper bound on its own
first-choice accuracy. Their bound on OB is `0.4864`; our `AC@1` there is `0.904`. The inequality is asserted in
`cutoff-accuracy.test.ts` over every rank and every cutoff rather than reasoned about, because it is the one claim every
external comparison leans on.

**The floor, which is why a cutoff average needs one.** A uniformly random order over a pool of `n` scores
`(1/(n·k)) Σ_{j=1..k} min(j, n)` — `0.70` at `n = 4`, `0.50` at `n = 6`, `0.25` at `n = 12`, `0.047` at `n = 64`.
On `RE1:OnlineBoutique`, whose pool has a median of **6**, a random order therefore scores `56.5 %` `Avg@5`, more than
half of our `96.2 %`. And the sharper reading: `arXiv:2609.27069` measures a ranker that reads **no telemetry at all**
at `Avg@5 0.488` on this benchmark, and DeCoR's Online Boutique row is `0.0016` **below** it. That is not a criticism
of their proof — it is what a twelve-service fleet does to a method that ranks by relational evidence alone, and it is
the reason a floor now travels beside every row.

**Nine rows the metric cannot reach.** Of the 735 census rows, **nine** carry no `truthRank` (RE1 2, RE2 4, RE3 3), so
the answer's `AC@1` is defined on 735 cases and every cutoff on 726 — `90.61 % (666/735)` against `91.73 % (666/726)`.
The module carries `rankMeasured` as a field rather than collapsing an absent column into `null`, and
`censusPopulations` returns both populations, so a reading cannot quote one over the other's denominator. On this
artifact the two columns agree to the case on every cell (`passes 0`), which is a property of the **file** —
`truthRank` is a position in the published order — and the `+83` reordering stays visible only on the 1 422-case
surface, whose dump keeps the sum's order beside the published one.

**Axes this closes.** One, and it is a hedge rather than a hypothesis: *"`Avg@5` competitors cannot be compared with
this system"* is closed — the protocol is now identical and the comparison is a command. **Axes this opens.** Two, both
priced: **RICE-CM as a method** (the protocol is comparable, the four components are not reproduced — a build, not a
reading), and **`AC@3` on TrainTicket** (`4.2 pp` pooled between the first and third cut, `10 pp` on
`RE3:TrainTicket`), which is headroom a scoring change can reach without widening the presentation.

**A competitor update that arrived with the reading.** `DecompRCA` (`arXiv:2609.36686`, code at
`github.com/cruiseresearchgroup/DecompRCA`) decomposes a `top@k` miss into **retrieval** and **reranking** failure and
reports that on microservice benchmarks retrieval is "nearly solved (98–100 %)" — which is this entry's `abs 0` on all
nine cells, measured by a different instrument. Two consequences: the remaining ceiling is a **reranker** question and
no candidate-construction change can move `AC@1`; and their largest published effect (`+7 … +18`) is a **hand-written**
description, not the derived brief arm T already measured at `+1` (`1 166` vs `1 165`). The open item is therefore not
"run the system-description arm" but "settle whether *purpose* is derivable from this corpus", at ¥0.

## 340 The queue's last two 「¥21」 items were never ¥21: a weight is a local run and a join (iteration 340)

**Owner of:** `docs/cost-audit-340.md` — the price structure, the three sentences the correction turns on, the two
instruments it required and the measurement. This entry is the register's summary of it, not a substitute for it.

The queue carried `--self-anomaly-weight 0.5` and `fingerprint_top_k = 22` at **≈ ¥21 each**. That figure is
`¥0.0147 × 1 422` — the price of ONE full-cloud arm dispatch — applied to two changes that never reach a cloud call.
The engine is **¥0.00 per case** (`docs/sota-comparison.md:92`, the cost row's own text), and the module that fires the
first weight is a multiplication on a slope (`packages/tree/src/pruning/pruner.ts:4269`). The second is not an arm at
all: `fingerprintTopK` "sets the width of the PRESENTATION dump and leaves the published ranking at `analyze(graph, 5)`
