… the ranking is computed before the field is read" (`benchmarks/src/fse26-run-config.ts:87-95`), so no rank can move
and the price of a width is zero by construction.

**The one sentence the number came from is contradicted by the arm's own protocol.** `term-marginal-338.md` §6.2
withheld the weight because "the arm's answers were produced from the shipped engine, so the published 1 328 cannot be
verified without a dispatch". The arm does not read the engine's ranking, and three places say so in the same words —
`benchmarks/src/query-agent.ts`'s module doc, this register at §327.2's neighbourhood (the `docs/closed-axes-register`
line quoted in 3067's vicinity), and `docs/free-investigation.md:156`: *"Seeding is a SEPARATE arm and is off here, so
the free arm means free."* Its artifact agrees: five retrieval tools over the case's own telemetry, with `engineRank`
written BESIDE the answer as a comparison rather than read by the loop. A weight cannot move an answer the weight never
entered, so the published surface is a **join** — two artifacts that change with the weight (`per-case`, `terms`) onto
two that do not (`answers`, corpus walk).

**The instrument that correction requires, and the defect building it found.** `benchmarks/src/surface-diff.ts`
(`27` tests, `100/100/100/100`) compares two published surfaces case by case: a net delta is not a finding, a repair
and a break are two populations, two files with different case sets are REFUSED rather than scored on their
intersection, a duplicated id is refused rather than letting the last row win, and the held-out folds are assigned by
the module because a case's fold depends on its position in the corpus order. `run-miss-ledger.ts` gained
`--surface-out` so the shipped surface is written by the runner that defines it. Making the comparison exposed
**`guardCensusOf` / `formatGuardCensus`** (`benchmarks/src/engine-certainty.ts`, `100/100/100/100` over `33` tests):
the certainty guard reads `top1Score − top2Score`, and the stored artifact every earlier surface reading was taken on
carries **neither column**, so the guard was not "idle" — it was never evaluated, and it printed `1 308` (the
first-hop surface) where the register had been quoting `1 328`. The two states are now different lines.

**The measurement, at ¥0.** `--self-anomaly-weight 0.5` on the full corpus in this sandbox (no API key in the
environment, so the semantic layer degrades to TF-IDF and the run is marked `DEGRADED`): **Top@1 81.5 %, Top@3 86.5 %,
Top@5 87.9 %, 1 422 cases, 0 load errors, 0 engine errors** — `0.8150 × 1 422 = 1 158.9` → **1 159**, which is §3's
row of `docs/term-marginal-338.md` to the case. The ablation table is reproducible for the price of the electricity,
which is the whole point: nine weights per iteration is a throughput question, not a budget one.

**The cost model that follows, in five rules.** A change that does not appear in the arm's transcript is never a
dispatch. A join is not a measurement. If an arm genuinely must be re-run, the ceiling arm is 74 cases at ≈ ¥2 and a
stratified 50 at ¥0.74, not 1 422 at ¥21. A cache hit is the same answer at 25 % of the price (W30's ¥41.46 list
against ¥10.53 cache over the same 1 422 cases). And an unmeasured column is a VALUE: any rule that reads one must say
how much of the corpus it could see, or a reading becomes a claim about a population it never saw — which is the
`guardCensus` defect above, generalised.

**And the reading, once the instrument existed, is a REFUSAL.** Both arms were joined onto the same stored answers
and the same corpus walk, with the guard census reporting `evaluated on 1422 / 1422 cases, margin measured on every
one` on both sides:

| surface | shipped | `--self-anomaly-weight 0.5` | delta | repairs / breaks |
| ------- | ------: | --------------------------: | ----: | ---------------: |
| arm answers | 1 287 | 1 287 | +0 | 0 / 0 |
| + first hop | 1 308 | 1 308 | +0 | 0 / 0 |
| **shipped (with the guard)** | **1 328 (93.39 %)** | **1 328 (93.39 %)** | **+0** | **0 / 0** |

The engine moved `+5 / −2 = +3`, and the case-by-case cross-reference names where each movement went: **four of the
five repairs and both breaks are MASKED** — a case the arm already answers correctly cannot be repaired again, because
the published surface does not consult the engine on it — and the one unmasked repair is a case where the engine now
leads with the truth while the surface still publishes the arm's wrong answer, i.e. exactly the case a promotion rule
exists for, and that family is priced at `−52 / −44 / −152 / −70` over the corpus. The weight is therefore refused on
the reading the ¥21 was meant to buy, and the numeral that made it look attractive is the engine's, not the product's.

**The law that follows, which belongs in every future estimate.** An engine delta converts to a published delta only on
cases the arm gets WRONG and no rule already settles: **135 of 1 422 — a 9.5 % aperture**. A weight worth `+3` on the
engine is therefore worth between `0` and `3` on the surface, with an expected conversion under a third. Engine Top@1
is not a proxy for the product number, and the two cannot be inferred from each other; breadth's 28 addressable cases
are 21 % of the aperture and the reasoning residue's 37 are 27 %, so those two are where the next iteration's value
is — not in another weight.

**The field check, and the column it forced.** Four movements this week, in full in `field-survey-340.md`:
DecompRCA reached **v2 as an accepted NeurIPS'26 paper** (`arXiv:2609.36686v2`) whose microservice half reports
retrieval "nearly solved (98–100 %)" and whose graph result is that no learned causal graph "clearly beat[s] the best
statistical baseline" — both of which this register reached first, from a different instrument, which is the strongest
corroboration it has recorded; **RCAEval shipped the decomposition as an official flag** (`--report-decomposition K`,
printing `Retrieval@K` and `Rerank@1`) together with an opt-in chance floor (`--report-chance`), so a reading taken
only on `Avg@5` is no longer comparable with the field's own table and our `abs 0` must be printed in their two
numbers; **Alibaba's BRiSE family** (RCA-100: 103 cases, six modalities, a 3–4-step causal chain with **661 numeric
checkpoints**; AIOps2025: 400 cases) opened a **process-scored** front whose `Reason` pillar grades the transcript —
a thing this corpus cannot score, and whose two published findings ("fault injections ≠ fault cases", and 62.5 % of
cases needing two or more modalities) are this register's `unwidenable 20` and its single-channel refusal under other
names; and **Greptime's Agent RCA Bench** measured the query interface as a variable (105/168 correct against 130/168,
$1.09 against $0.59 per investigation), which is external evidence for the single-surface design `buildTelemetry`
already uses. The first of the four was actionable inside this iteration and is done: `decompositionAt` and
`formatDecomposition` in `benchmarks/src/cutoff-accuracy.ts` print the split under every cutoff table, and the split is
an **identity** — `AC@1 = retrieval × rerank` at every `k`, asserted per cutoff — rather than a second measurement.

## 341 The arm's own reach: 74 of 94 published misses never queried the causal service (iteration 341)

**Owner of:** `docs/arm-reach-341.md` — the two censuses, the field's `Chance@k`/`Lift@k` definitions read from its code,
the floor defect that reconciling them exposed, the re-priced queue and the falsifiers. This entry is the register's
summary of it, not a substitute for it.

The queue that 340 re-priced still described its misses by where the truth sits in the **engine's** ranking. That
description assumes a seeded arm. The shipped arm is not seeded, and its artifact says so on every row —

```
$ jq -r .seeded /tmp/art328/query-agent.ndjson | sort | uniq -c
   1422 false
```

— so `SEED_WIDTH` is a width an *experiment* would set and the class names describe the **pipeline's** reach. Measured
against the arm's own `calls` column instead: **of the 94 shipped misses, 74 (78.72 %) never queried the causal service
at all**; 20 queried it and still missed. On the arm's own answers the same split is 102 / 135 (75.56 %). Against the
corpus the first is **5.20 pp**, the second **1.41 pp** — so the reasoning residue the queue carried as "37 cases,
≈¥21" is 20 cases, and the largest remaining block was not in the queue at all.

Four facts make those 74 a *reach* population rather than a hard one, and each is a file, not an opinion: the culprit is
a key of the case's own `metrics` map **and** an endpoint of its own `traceEdges` in **all 74** (51 of 74 also carry log
lines for it); the arm stops with **4.99** of its **ten** tool calls spent and **1.888** distinct services queried, in a
corpus that carries ~50 services a case; in **40** of the 74 the culprit's id is already somewhere in the recorded
transcript (a lower bound — a row keeps its last 2 000 characters); and the 74 are spread over six fault families, so
this is a policy failure rather than one injector's blind spot.

**What a stated policy already reaches.** "74 reachable" is not a plan; the budget is ten calls, so the question is how
many of the 74 have the culprit inside the first ten a stated ordering would put first. Against the ordering the
pipeline already computes: **40 of the 74 (54.1 %) sit within the engine's top ten** (29 within the top five; 16 at
11–20; 18 beyond 20), and over all 94 misses 58 (61.7 %). So a schedule that spends its ten calls on the engine's own
first ten candidates would have queried the culprit in 40 cases — **2.81 pp** — for no extra token and no widening.
The two forties are not the same forty: the 40 whose culprit is named in the transcript and the 40 inside the engine's
top ten overlap in only **19** cases, so their union is **61 of the 74 (82.4 %)** — the routes are complementary, and a
reader who merged them would conclude the schedule had nothing to add.
This also explains a result this register has carried as a mystery: §318 measured a **seeded PROMPT** as worse than the
free arm, and showing a model an order is not the same as ordering its **calls** — the first invites anchoring on the
engine's first choice, the second spends a finite budget where the evidence is most likely to be. The seed was refused
on measurement; the **schedule** has never been run, and now has a ceiling.

**Instruments.** `reachCensusOf` / `formatReachCensus` in `benchmarks/src/retrieval-block.ts` (34 tests,
`100/100/100/100`) count three disjoint miss buckets — queried, unqueried, and **unrecorded** (no `calls` column), so an
absent column can never read as a measured absence; the share is printed over the classifiable misses and names its
denominator; and the row states which configuration it was read on, because "the arm is free on every row" and "the arm
was seeded on every row" are opposite claims about the same number. `SEED_WIDTH`'s docblock and the module header were
corrected to say what they measure.

**The field's two columns, from its code rather than its changelog.** `RCAEval` prints `Chance@5` and `Lift@5`
(`main.py --report-chance`), and two of the three definitions are not what their names imply: `Chance@5` is
`chance_average(5)`, the mean of `min(k, n)/n` over the cuts — `0.70` on a four-service cell, not `1.00`; it is
therefore **this module's `floor`**, and the identity is asserted per cutoff rather than argued; and `Lift@5` is
`average(k) - chance_average(k)`, an **excess**, so a ratio printed under that label would be a different number
wearing the field's name. `CutoffReading` now carries `lift` beside `avg` and `floor`, `formatCutoffs` prints both
columns, and a test asserts the ratio is not the lift.

**The defect that reconciliation exposed.** `absent` has always been documented as "unreachable at every cutoff, by
construction", and the floor was charged `uniformFloor(k, pool)` for every case including those whose answer the pool
never held — two statements that cannot both hold, since an answer outside the pool cannot be found by any order over
it. `chanceAt(k, pool, inPool)` returns `0` for those, the floor is the mean over cuts of that per case, and the
corpus's three row states are now distinct: measured-in-pool, measured-absent (`0` and `0`), and unmeasured (excluded
from both populations by `censusPopulations`, which is why the answer metric is defined on 735 rows and the order
metric on 726).

**The rewritten law, to sit beside the aperture.** An engine-side change converts only on cases the arm gets wrong and
no rule settles — 135, **9.5 %**. An arm-side change converts on cases the arm never investigated — 74, **5.2 %**, with
the evidence already in the case file. The levers are disjoint and the second is the larger one.

**Field check.** RCAtlas (late Oct 2026, 90 incidents over eight datasets) publishes the ordering this register argued
from the inside — plain harnesses 65–77 % PR@1 against 16–53 % for five published SOP agents and 6–39 % for
statistical/causal methods, with every Pareto-optimal configuration a simple harness — and names the mechanism
("hard-coded investigation paths skip the decisive evidence"), which is this iteration's 74 cases seen from the other
side: ours has no SOP at all and still looks in the wrong place, because a budget without a policy is not a search.
CARE-PO (`arXiv:2611.12125`) finds 82.8 % of agent trajectories carrying a removable call and 68.0 % of calls
removable. **Corrected in 342:** this entry first read that as "the unspent half of our budget is the normal state of
the art", and the arm has no unspent half — six rounds execute five calls and the artifact carries 4.99 of them. What
CARE-PO prices here is not slack but *choice*: if most calls are removable, then which five are spent IS the policy,
and a schedule is the cheapest way to change it. SRE-1
(ResolveAI, 18 Nov 2026) puts a process-scored competitor in production: 38.8 % single / 71 % five-run ensemble pass on
49 live cases at −37 % cost against the strongest frontier model, over 400+ tools and a citation-bearing causal chain —
a column this corpus still cannot score.

**342 — the schedule is not the seed, and the budget the arm spends is five.** Two corrections and one instrument; the
full record is `schedule-not-seed-342.md`, and the withdrawal it supersedes is noted in `arm-reach-341.md`.

*The budget.* `DEFAULT_QUERY_BUDGET` states `maxRounds: 6, maxToolCalls: 10`, and the second number never binds: the
loop's last turn is answer-only, so **five** calls are executable and the shipped artifact carries 4.99 of them
(`jq -r .toolCalls` → `1 416 × 5, 6 × 4`). The 341 entry's "4.99 of ten, half unspent" is wrong and is withdrawn; the
zero-cost width of a schedule is therefore **five**, not ten. `usableCallsOf(budget) = min(maxToolCalls, maxRounds − 1)`
is the one place that arithmetic lives, and a test pins it to the loop's own `forcing` condition.

*The mechanism.* 341's mystery — a seeded prompt losing to a free arm (§318) — is not a mystery once the two objects are
separated: a **seed** prints the order, which invites re-ranking a prior (priced at chance, `z = −9.26` over 5 335
claims), while a **schedule** keeps the order in the harness and serves one service per call. The arm's own artifact
says which the model responds to: the 20 misses that queried the culprit had it at engine **median position 2** and the
74 that did not at **9**, on 1.888 distinct services out of five calls — the model looks where the engine points and
stops after fewer than two services.

*The two prices.* `TOOL next` plus `--schedule none|engine` ship the route; `run-schedule-reading.ts` prices it on
artifacts already paid for. At the authorised five calls the ceiling is **29 of the 74 (2.04 pp)** and the point
estimate, at the 98.33 % conversion measured on the 1 198 investigations that did query the culprit, is **2.01 pp**; at
ten calls (`--max-rounds 11`, 2× model calls, ≈ ¥0.029/case) it is **40 (2.81 pp)** and **2.77 pp**. Two widths, two
prices, one flag apart — the 341 number was the second one quoted as if it were free.

*The second axis.* The same corpus's `Retrieval@5` split by the arm's own record is **99.25 %** on the population it
investigated and **26.79 %** on the population it did not (`reach-decomposition.ts`, `--split-at 5`), so DecompRCA v2's
"retrieval nearly solved (98–100 %)" is one split of two and the pooled 87.83 % averages a solved problem with an
unsolved one. `Retrieval@1` inside the queried split is 88.23 % against 7.14 % outside it, which is the mechanism: the
arm looks where the engine points, so the misses it never investigated are the ones the engine ranked third to fifth —
exactly the slots a five-call schedule adds.

*The instrument.* `benchmarks/src/investigation-schedule.ts`, 36 tests, `100/100/100/100`, plus
`query-agent-schedule.test.ts` over the directive and the loop: three disjoint miss populations (`queriedMisses +
unqueriedMisses + unrecordedMisses = misses`), `null` for a truth the pool never held rather than "infinitely far", and
a test that fails if the ceiling is ever printed as the estimate. `formatConversion`'s `cases === 0` guard was removed
as unreachable and the reason is written where it stood.

**The dispatch refused the arm.** 532 cases (all 266 engine misses + 266 engine hits), `--schedule engine`, ¥7.36:
**agent Top@1 184 against the engine's 266**, 45 repairs against 127 breaks, and **139 of 266** engine-correct cases
retained against the free arm's 1 134 of 1 156. Projected onto the sample that is **77.8 % for the free arm against
34.6 %** — a −43 pp sign error against the +2.01 pp ceiling, and it is an instruction defect, not a coding one: v1 of the
prompt sold the schedule as a replacement for `TOOL fleet` (eight services per call), stated a budget of ten calls the
loop cannot execute, and served a single-service view that carries neither `ERROR` lines nor failed-interface counts.
Full record: `schedule-dispatch-342.md`. **Closed:** a schedule that competes with the fleet read. **Open:** the same
premise implemented as a `fleet` section, which adds engine-ranked services to what the fleet already shows at zero
extra cost.

**Closed here:** "spend more calls" as the reach lever (the wall is rounds, and the ceiling doubles for 2× the price —
priced, not assumed); "the arm wastes its budget" as a diagnosis (it spends all five); and the reading of §318 that a
schedule had already been refuted (it had not — a seed had).

## 343 The shortlist inside the fleet read, and the census that makes an arm readable (iteration 343)

*The correction 342b's own artifact forced.* `TRACE_CHARS = 2 000` is a record of the END of an investigation, and
**532 of 532** rows in both arms of the 342b sample begin `[earlier results elided]`, keeping **4.11** of 5 executed
directives (free arm **4.05** on the same ids). So a per-tool table computed from a `trace` is a table of the tail:
`TOOL fleet` and `TOOL services` are **0.000 in both arms** — they are the calls an investigation makes FIRST, and the
first block is the one elision removes. Two 342b claims are withdrawn with that measurement: "the fleet read was never
common (0.5 %)" (a different denominator; 0.000 on these 532 ids) and "the route was never walked" (`0 of 532 traces name
next` is a statement about the last four calls, since a `next` issued first is invisible by construction). What survives
is the tail's composition — `TOOL logs` **73.7 % → 25.2 %**, `TOOL edges` **60.5 % → 97.4 %**, both arms eliding the same
number of blocks — and every outcome column (184 vs 266, retention 52.26 %).

*The instrument.* `QueryOutcome.tools` / `QueryOutcome.nextServed`, written into the artifact as row fields and printed
by the job log as a `census:` line, count directives **as they run**, so neither a 2 000-character cap nor elision can
reach them; a refused tool is counted because a refused tool is still what the arm reached for. Ten tests in
`query-agent-shortlist.test.ts` were written before the code, plus one wiring test for `query_fleet_order`.

*The arm.* `--fleet-order none|engine` prints the pipeline's own first `PIPELINE_LINES = 5` candidates **inside `TOOL
fleet`**, names only, after the two surprise sections. It is neither a seed nor a schedule: the instruction is
byte-identical to the published one (asserted in a test), no call is spent, no round is added, and no prompt token is
charged. That property is the whole design — 342b's −43 pp came from four appended prompt lines whose advertised tool was
never demonstrably called, so the next intervention changes what an investigation can SEE and not what it is TOLD.

*Pre-registered before the artifact exists, and refused by its own measurement* (run **45437298998**, the same 532 ids
as 342b, ¥7.17): **H1 passes** — `TOOL fleet` is called in **532 / 532** cases, 1.00 per case, so 342b's 0.5 % fleet
figure was elision and nothing else; **H2 fails** — agent Top@1 **209** against the free arm's **414** (−205 cases,
**−38.53 pp**) and against the bar of 425; **H3 fails, and is the veto** — **160 / 266 = 60.15 %** of the engine's
correct answers retained; **H4 passes and sizes the 342b defect** — the tail agrees with the census exactly for the
tools called LAST (`logs` 44.2 % both, `services` 0 % both) and understates the ones called FIRST (`fleet` 0.0 % →
**100 %**, `failed` 69.9 % → 95.1 %, `metric` 79.3 % → 100 %).

*The mechanism is substitution, measured on the answers.* On the 266 cases the engine has right, the arm answers its
rank 1 in **158** cases against the free arm's **261**, and answers a **sibling of the printed five** in **44**
instead of 1 — 140 siblings over the whole sample against 64. The section does not make the model follow the engine; it
makes it **choose from** the engine, and its choice is worse than either ranker: fewer distinct services investigated
(1.615 against 1.895), less agreement (37.2 % of answers are the engine's rank 1, against 67.5 %), and 39.29 % against
77.82 %. Two rankings in one context, and the model reconciles them into a third that is the worst of the three.

*Three presentations, three losses.* Seed (§318, printed in the prompt) **81.08 %** against the free arm's 93.39 %;
schedule (342b, one name per call) **52.26 %** retention; shortlist (this, a five-name section in `TOOL fleet`)
**60.15 %**. Full record: `fleet-shortlist-343.md`. **Closed:** "show the arm the engine's order" in all three known
forms — the text-free form, which should have been the strongest, is refused hardest on retention. **Open:** raising
`maxRounds` with **no** order shown (341 prices it at 40 of 74 for 2× the model calls), which no iteration since 318 has
run because every dispatch went to a presentation.

## 344 Early convergence priced: 40 % of the shortlist's loss, and a conversion rate read on the wrong stratum (iteration 344)

*The question 343 left asserted.* 343 named **substitution** as the mechanism of its −38.53 pp and did not price it.
The same 532 paired ids, at ¥0, split by (is the engine right) × (did the investigation query the culprit) × (is the
answer correct): **414 − 209 = 205** decomposes into **−107** (engine hits, queried: the free arm queries the culprit in
246 of 266, the shortlist arm in 161 — **85 fewer per-service queries**, which is the whole of `distinct` 1.895 → 1.615),
**+6** (engine hits, did not query), **−3** (engine misses, queried) and **−101** (engine misses, did not query).

*Convergence is the smaller half, and the shape of the other half rules out every budget knob.* The `−107` block is worth
at most **83 cases (40 %)** at the free arm's 98.0 % conversion — 74 (36 %) under an independent reweighting, so the two
estimates bracket it at **36–40 %**. The `−101` block is not convergence at all: on the engine's MISSES neither arm
queries the culprit (48 vs 43 of 266), and with **no** query the free arm still answers **115 / 218 = 52.8 %** while the
shortlist arm answers **14 / 223 = 6.3 %**. A 46.5-point collapse in a block where both arms did the same thing. The
residual **24 cases (12 %)** are the same queries converting at 83.2 % instead of 98.0 %. **No tool weighting can reach
this block, because the block is where the arm did NOT act** — so the "log evidence first" lever was rebuilt on a
different premise rather than on a weight: iteration 345 appends the service's first `ERROR`/`FATAL` offset and count to
each `TOOL metric` line (`docs/onset-channel-345.md`), which is the one thing the block can plausibly be short of.

*341's reach ceiling was overstated by a fifth.* The published **98.33 %** conversion is the **hits** stratum's number:
on a hit the culprit IS the engine's rank 1, so "queried the culprit" and "agreed with the engine" are one event, and the
hits supply 246 of the 294 culprits the rate is computed over (83.7 %). Reach cases are **misses** by definition, and the
misses stratum converts at **79.2 %**. Restated where the ceiling applies: **1.61 pp** at width 5 and **2.23 pp** at width
10, not 2.01 and 2.77. Second time this programme used a blended rate on a stratified question, and the first time the
blend was caught before a dispatch rather than after one.

*What ships.* Two guards, written before the code they fence. `benchmarks/__tests__/engine-order-surface.test.ts` —
`ENGINE_ORDER_SURFACES` names the **two** surfaces through which the engine's order may enter a model's context
(`schedule`, `shortlist`), each call site carries an `ENGINE-ORDER SURFACE:` fence, the count of `scheduleNames(` uses
must equal the list's length, and an arm carrying neither prints nothing from the order. A fourth presentation now fails
in the suite on the day it is written. `benchmarks/__tests__/budget-surface.test.ts` — `DEFAULT_QUERY_BUDGET` is
**6 / 10**, `usableCallsOf` is **5**, `--max-rounds` is parsed in exactly one file, the dispatch input defaults to the
empty string, and **no `packages/*/src` file knows the vocabulary** (`maxToolCalls`, `transcriptChars`, `usableCallsOf`,
`QUERY_BUDGET`). The round ceiling is a measurement knob and this is what "evaluation side only" means to the build.

*Withdrawn.* 342b's v2 prompt (the one that no longer claims ten calls) is **not** dispatched. It repairs wording, and
the presentation it repairs retains 52.26 % of the engine's correct answers — a 47-point deficit that no sentence about
how many calls exist can close. Keeping it as a pending arm would re-open a closed axis on a cosmetic pretext. Full
record: `early-convergence-344.md`. **Open:** a wider investigation with **no** order shown (`--max-rounds 11`, ¥14,
re-priced here from 2.77 pp to 2.23 pp) — the only arm on this axis never run.

## 346 A 236-case drift between two days, and three published signs that flip (iteration 346)

*The mistake that found it.* 345 dispatched an arm whose flag never reached the loop — `runQueryAgent` had gained an
eleventh parameter and its call site still passed ten — so the run that came back was a **plain free arm**. Its artifact
says so: `err=` appears in **0 of 532** transcripts.

*What that arm measured.* On the same 532 ids as every arm since 342b: free **414** (11-23 09:21), schedule **184**
(11-24 14:27), shortlist **209** (11-24 16:27), free **178** (11-24 23:36). The first and last are the same arm, and
McNemar on the paired cases gives **245 discordant one way and 9 the other (Δ −236, p < 0.001)**. Same prompt (fenced by
a test), same corpus (same `converterDigest`), same 532 ids. Nothing in a row recorded which day it was from.

*The signs, re-read against the same day's control.* shortlist **209 vs 178 = +31 (+5.8 pp, 16 vs 47, p < 0.001)**;
schedule **184 vs 178 = +6 (15 vs 21, p = 0.405)**; shortlist vs schedule **+25 (11 vs 36, p < 0.001)**. So "three
presentations, three losses" is **withdrawn**: against a control of the same day, the section inside `TOOL fleet` is the
only arm in this line with a measured **positive** effect, and the schedule is indistinguishable from free. **Open
again:** the presentation axis, with its strongest form now the one 343 published as the worst.

*The standing is not comparable.* 1 328 / 1 422 = **93.39 %** is an 11-23 measurement by the arm that scores **33.46 %**
on the 532-case sample today. Unless §5.2 of `model-drift-346.md` fires, no current dispatch can reproduce it, and every
number in `sota-comparison.md` is a comparison between a measurement and a memory. **Cause: unverified** — the supplier's
model behind the name, supplier-side routing, or an unfenced change here; the first is the only one invisible to every
run in this repository, because every run records the model's **name**.

*What ships.* `<artifact>.meta.json` (`startedAt`/`endedAt`/`durationSeconds`/`model`/`budget`/`arms` as one string);
`agent-runner-wiring.test.ts`, which asserts the call site and the signature agree on the **count** of arguments and
reports the missing **name**; and the rule this session earned — **an arm's control is the free arm dispatched in the
same batch, never the free arm in the file**.

*The repeat, and the level it establishes.* A free arm dispatched at 00:35 on 11-25 returned **170 / 532** against
345's **178** the night before: **Δ −8, McNemar 22 vs 14, p = 0.243** — no difference. Against 11-23's 414 the same arm
is **Δ −244, 252 vs 8, p < 0.001**. So the drift is a **level around 174 ± 6 today**, not a stable 414 with a bad night,
and §5.1 of `model-drift-346.md` fires while §5.2 does not.

*The axis, re-read against that level.* shortlist **+39 cases (+7.33 pp, 11 vs 50, p < 0.001)** against the 11-25 control
and **+31 (+5.83 pp, 16 vs 47, p < 0.001)** against the 11-24 one; schedule **+14 (p = 0.054)** and **+6 (p = 0.405)**.
**The section inside `TOOL fleet` is the only intervention in this programme with a measured gain, under both controls.**
The schedule is positive in sign and significant under neither, which on 532 cases is what a null with a small real
effect looks like. **Reopened:** the presentation axis, with its strongest form the one 343 published as its worst.
**Withdrawn with it:** 344's 205-case decomposition — its gap is a day boundary, not two arms (`early-convergence-344.md`
carries the retraction; the arithmetic is right and the object is wrong). **Unchanged:** 344's within-run findings, the
98.33 %-was-a-hits-stratum correction, the 1.61 / 2.23 pp ceilings, both guards, and the rule that a control is the free
arm dispatched in the same batch.

### 347 The two files were never the same arm — a 244-case gap that is 186 configurations and 58 instructions

**The reading that ends the drift.** 346 compared two artifacts it called *the free arm*. They ran different harnesses.
The 2026-11-22 artifact (run `45085062340`, arm 00:26–00:58Z) ran `gate contrast, fallback engine, resolve edge-novel`
and its own rows say **287 of its 532 sampled cases were answered by something other than the model** — 155 by the
prior, 71 by the entry-prior rule, 61 by the interface witness. The 2026-11-25 artifact (run `45519251447`) ran all
three at `none` and answered **532 of 532** from the model. Neither record named `fallback` or `resolve`: both read
`free`-plus-`gate=contrast`, and the two fields that decide the comparison were absent from the file written to make
comparisons safe.

**The decomposition, on the same 532 ids.** `model` 245 cases: 180 → 122. `prior` 155: 105 → 40. `entry` 71: 68 → 2.
`interface` 61: 61 → 6. So **186 of the 244 cases were never a model answer in either run** (the 287 non-model rows:
234 right then, 48 right now), and the model's own 245 lose 58. Among those 245, the 139 whose answer string is
identical are **correct in 139 of 139** in both runs — zero disagreements — and the 106 that changed are the cases where
the final turn differs: 589 of the old run's 1 422 investigations ended on the round cap (`stop: rounds`) because a
fallback existed and nothing forced an answer, while today's loop tells the model on its last turn that an unanswered
case scores zero.

**Reversed.** The drift, its "level 174 ± 6", the claim that 414 may not be compared with anything current, and the
retraction of the standing — `1 328 / 1 422 = 93.39 %` is a **pipeline** reading and a bare arm cannot speak to it.
**Still invalid, for the corrected reason:** 342b's −43 pp and 343's −38.53 pp compared a bare arm to a pipeline
control. **Still standing:** 346's same-day **+31 shortlist** (bare against bare, 16 vs 47, p < 0.001); 344's
within-run findings; 341's 98.33 %-was-a-hits-stratum correction and the 1.61 / 2.23 pp ceilings. **Restated standing:**
the 11-22 pipeline artifact is **1 287 / 1 422 = 90.51 %** (repairs 153, breaks 22, precision 0.874, ¥20.87), and the
published 93.39 % adds two deterministic guards over it (+50 first hop, +20 engine certainty). The model's marginal
contribution to the pipeline is **+131 cases over the engine alone**.

**And re-measured, because the retraction above could not stand on arithmetic alone.** A full-corpus dispatch with the
same flags (run `45531140696`, ¥20.81) returned **1 328 / 1 422 = 93.39 %** with **180 repairs and 8 breaks** (precision
**0.957**), retention 0.993, and the two guards applied inside the artifact (`door` 28, `certainty` 20). Paired against
the 11-22 artifact on the same 1 422 ids: **42 gained, 1 lost, Δ +41, p < 0.001** — the guards' own worth as a paired
delta for the first time. The number 346 called unreproducible at any price reproduces at ¥21, and higher. **What is
left is 94 cases:** 8 breaks (5 model, 3 `entry-prior`), 86 un-repaired engine misses — of which **37 sit inside the
engine's top five and 12 more inside the top ten**, and 20 at rank 21 or deeper.

**Shipped.** `run-metadata.ts` now **requires** `fallback` and `resolve` and records `revision` (`GITHUB_SHA`);
`arm-comparison.ts` refuses a pairing whose two records differ outside the declared axis (model, budget, revision, and
any `arms` key — an absent flag is a difference, not a default) and prints both McNemar forms, the exact conditional
binomial and the continuity-corrected chi-square the published 0.243 comes from; `run-arm-comparison.ts` exits 1 rather
than printing a table beside a warning; `benchmark-agentic.yml` gains `query_control=free`, which runs the control in
the **same job** with the harness flags forwarded and the three presentation flags omitted, and derives the comparison
axis from the dispatch. The `.meta.json` files were also written and **never uploaded** until now. Full record:
`arm-configuration-347.md`.

### 348 The bill was never a rate: 98 % of it is the question, and 55 % of it bought discarded answers

**The decomposition, from the artifact's own columns.** Run `45531140696` cost **20.81 CNY** for 1 422 cases:
**10 221 261 prompt tokens against 46 085 completion — 222 to 1**, which at the endpoint's two prices is 20.44 of
input and 0.37 of output. **98.23 % of the money is the question.** Every arm of the previous six iterations was
discussed as though the two columns were interchangeable, and none of them moved the one that carries the bill.

**Where it went.** Grouped by the resolver that settled the case: `model` 636 cases ¥9.40, `prior` 516 ¥7.51,
`interface` 148 ¥2.15, `entry` 74 ¥1.07, `door` 28 ¥0.40, `certainty` 20 ¥0.29. **786 of the 1 422 cases were settled
by something other than the model, after each had paid for six turns: 11.41 CNY, 54.82 % of the run, spent on answers
then discarded.** The `interface` row is the sharpest — 148 cases, **148 correct**, not one of which needed a call. The
per-case cost is 0.0143–0.0148 across all six strata, which is the tell: the loop spends its budget whether or not the
result is used.

**The one signal available at the door.** The engine's margin separates the populations almost perfectly (hits at a
median 0.872, misses at 0.081). Simulated on the artifact, skipped cases answering with the engine's winner:
floor 0.30 → 964 skipped, ¥14.18, **−23 cases**; 0.50 → 771, ¥11.32, −12; 0.80 → 603, ¥8.85, −2;
**0.87 → 582 skipped, ¥8.55, ±0 cases, accuracy unchanged at 93.39 %**; 1.00 → 520, ¥7.64, +0. The loss-free region
is bounded on both sides, which is what makes the figure a measurement rather than a knob.

**Not a bug in the resolver.** Discarding those answers is correct — the interface witness is 148/148 because it reads
the failing interface and the model does not. The defect is **placement**: whether a model will fail is not knowable
before it fails, so the decision that could have been taken at the door is taken at the exit.

**Shipped.** `cost-model.ts` (`costOf`, `auditCost`, `skipAt`, `lossFreeFloor`) at 100 % statements / branches /
functions / lines over 26 cases, refusing an artifact with no `engineMargin` column and treating a `null` margin as
unknown rather than high; `token-rates.ts`, the two prices behind an interface, **the input rate being the cache-MISS
rate because the invoice is the miss arithmetic**; `run-cost-audit.ts`, which prices any artifact offline so the
question is a command rather than a paragraph; and `--certainty-floor`, wired through **both** hops and pinned by two
assertions in `agent-runner-wiring.test.ts`, because iteration 345's `onset` is what a price knob dropped at a hop
looks like — parsed, logged, present in 0 of 532 transcripts. A skipped case is the same arm at a lower price: the
fallback's name, `rounds: 0`, zero tokens, empty transcript, attributed to `prior`, no new vocabulary in the artifact.

**Open, with a measurement attached.** 10.2 M prompt tokens were charged at the miss rate across 8 530 calls to one
endpoint with a byte-identical 750-character system prompt, so **no prefix was reused**. Recovering the cache would cut
the input price by up to 75 % — more than every other row above combined — but it is an endpoint-side property this
repository cannot assert by reading its own code. Stated as an open question rather than a saving.

**Also dropped, with no dispatch:** the acceptance rule. Every arm of the last six iterations was accepted or rejected
on a full-corpus run at ¥20.81 when the question each asked was a paired delta on the engine's 266 misses. A 466-case
stratified sample (`--sample-misses` / `--sample-correct`, both already shipped) costs ¥6.8 and resolves 5 points at
p < 0.01; the full corpus added resolution below 1.5 points, which no decision here has ever turned on.

**Every CNY figure above is an upper bound by 1.87×**, and the cache saving is withdrawn: a four-request probe of the
endpoint (349) found that the served model's published rate is $0.15 / $0.60 per million — 1.07 / 4.28 — rather than
the 2 / 8 these numbers are priced at, and that two byte-identical calls read `prompt_cache_hit_tokens: 0`. The
structure is a token ratio and survives the correction; the money column does not. Full record:
`cost-structure-348.md`.

### 349 The model in every artifact is retired, the cache serves nothing, and the price was an estimate

**Four requests of eight tokens, ¥0.001, and three answers.** `GET /v1/models` returns **two** models — `deepseek-flash`
and `deepseek-v4-pro`. `deepseek-chat` is **not among them**: the alias was retired, and a request for it is *served
anyway*, by `deepseek-flash`, which the response's own `model` field reports. Every artifact this programme wrote
carries the name that was ASKED FOR, so **every one of them names a model that no longer exists**, including the
93.39 % standing. What that changes is comparability across the retirement date and not the readings: the arm that ran
ran, and the response named it.

**The cache, closed with a no.** The same body, twice, on both models:

```
deepseek-chat  #1 {"prompt_tokens":191,"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":0,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":191}
deepseek-chat  #2 {"prompt_tokens":191,"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":0,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":191}
deepseek-flash #1 {"prompt_tokens":216,"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":0,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":216}
deepseek-flash #2 {"prompt_tokens":216,"prompt_cache_hit_tokens":0,"prompt_cache_miss_tokens":216}
```

**Zero on the second identical call.** 348 listed "recovering the cache would cut the input price by up to 75 % — more
than every other row combined" as the largest open item; it is closed, and the 75 % was never available. What replaces
the inference is the endpoint's own field, recorded per call from now on: a run that claims a cache saving has to
**show** one.

**The price was an estimate, by 1.87×.** This repository prices a run at 2 CNY per million in and 8 out; every "CNY"
figure it has published is that arithmetic, applied to the endpoint's own token counts. The served model's published
off-peak rate is **$0.15 / $0.60 per million** — **1.07 / 4.28** at 7.13. So **run `45531140696` cost 11.13 CNY and not
20.81**, which is **0.0078 per case** and **1/820th** of the only competitor that publishes a per-case price. The
structure is untouched: 98.23 % input, 222 tokens of question per token of answer, 786 cases settled without the model
at 54.82 % of the bill, and the 0.87 floor's 41.1 % — every one of those is a token ratio, and a price table cancels
out of it. The ratio stays bounded on both sides, which is why the floor is still the one saving on the table.

**A risk the probe found on the way past, and did not walk into.** The `deepseek-flash` responses carry
`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens: 8` — the model spent its whole eight-token budget thinking, because
**thinking is on by default on that name**. The shipped arms spend 5.4 completion tokens per call, which is impossible
with thinking on, so the retired alias was serving it with thinking **off**. Migrating the requested name without also
disabling thinking would multiply the output bill tenfold and look like a price change rather than a configuration one;
the migration is therefore one change — `deepseek-flash` with thinking disabled, served name and reasoning tokens both
recorded — and it is not made here.

**Shipped.** `ChatCompletion` carries `cacheHitTokens` / `cacheMissTokens` parsed from the endpoint's own `usage`, with
absence reading as zero (an endpoint that reports no cache served nothing from one); `QueryOutcome.servedModel` and
`QueryArmRow.servedModel` record what the endpoint SAID it served, empty when it says nothing and **never the requested
name**; `QueryArmRow.cacheHitTokens` sums the split across turns; `DEEPSEEK_FLASH_RATES` sits beside
`DEEPSEEK_CHAT_RATES` with the 1.87 asserted by a test; the banner reads `asked for deepseek-chat`; and
`probe-endpoint.yml` is dispatch-only, four requests, no artifact — the next time a supplier moves, the answer costs a
hundredth of a corpus case instead of a day spent reading two files that disagree. Full record:
`endpoint-probe-349.md`.

### 351 The floor priced one rule and shipped another, and the correction is a per-case identity (iteration 351)

**One rule priced, another shipped.** `--certainty-floor` was added as the first saving taken *before* the call, and it
settled a skipped case on `priorTop ?? engine.top1`. The certainty guard — the rule the floor is a pre-call form of —
settles on `engine.top1`, and `cost-model.skipAt`, the function that decided whether the floor was worth buying,
credited a skipped case with `engineRight`, the **guard's** answer. So for one iteration this tree priced one rule and
ran another: the defect `applyResolver`'s own comment records from iteration 322, reproduced by the iteration that
quoted it.

**Three disagreements, and the third hid the first.** (1) the answer: `priorTop ?? engine.top1` against `engine.top1`;
(2) the boundary: `margin >= floor` against `engineCertainty`'s `margin > bar`; (3) the stratum: `answeredBy: 'prior'`
against `'certainty'`. The third is what made it invisible — the stratified bill in `cost-structure-348.md` showed a
`certainty` stratum of 20 cases (the guard's, applied *after* the call) and a `prior` stratum of 516 that silently
contained every floored case, so a floored case and a refused one were merged into one row of one table.

**It was latent, and that is stated rather than excused.** The run both rules were read on ships `--fallback engine`,
so `priorTop` *is* `engineWinner`: **1 422 of 1 422 cases agree** on the acceptance artifact. Both rules shipped the
same name there; only the stratum and the boundary differed. A `--fallback seed` arm would have shipped a different
answer, and no artifact in this tree was taken on one — so the fix is required by the rules and by the arithmetic, not
merely by a reading.

**The correction buys an identity, not a delta.** `SkipReading` now carries `gains` and `losses` separately, because a
net delta cannot distinguish a rule that changes nothing from a rule that changes sixty and sums to zero. Above the
corpus's fitted frontier both are **zero on every one of the 1 422 cases**. `ruleEdges` names why in two numbers: the
highest margin at which shipping the engine's answer would have **destroyed** a correct case is **0.8630**, and the
highest at which it would have **repaired** one is **0.5707**. Between them the rule is a straight loss with nothing to
offset it; above both it is inert — so 0.87 was never a frontier, only the first probe above the cliff.

**1.5 is inherited, and the proof does not mention a corpus.** The default is `ENGINE_CERTAINTY_MARGIN`, for a reason
that holds on any artifact: `applyResolver` applies the guard *last*, over `door ?? settled`, so for any case whose
engine margin exceeds that bar the shipped pipeline overwrites whatever the model said. A pre-call floor at the same
bar therefore cannot change an answer; it can only stop paying for a turn that was going to be discarded. Two
preconditions, both checkable in the artifact: the resolver is armed, and the arm settles on some name (a refusal
settles on the prior and the guard then renames it). The one shape outside the argument is a case with no prior and no
model answer, where the arm ships silence and the floor ships the engine's name — a case already scoring zero.

**Six predictions, one dispatch, six hits.** Run `45595943761` (`--seed none --gate contrast --fallback engine
--resolve edge-novel --certainty-floor 1.5`, 1 422 cases, dispatched two days after a run that measured nothing because
`query_agent_sample` was left empty): **360** cases at `rounds: 0` with zero tokens and an empty trace, all 360 on
`engineWinner` attributed `certainty`, **0 gained / 0 lost**, corpus **93.32 %** (1 327/1 422, the one-case gap inside
the 1 062 that still called), **1.69 CNY**, and **no** `servedModel` on the 360 against 1 062 `deepseek-flash`. The
`certainty` stratum now reads `360 cases · 0.00 CNY · 360 correct` — the only row in the table that bought nothing, for
nothing. Full record: `certainty-floor-351.md`.

### 352 The cache serves 81 % of the tokens at 1/50 the price, and a probe cannot see it (iteration 352)

> **Superseded by §354.** The decomposition below is wrong in one part: the repeated text is a **543.8-token
> opening**, not a 5 800-token system prompt, and the uncached column is the **one block that is new on each call**.
> The per-token argument survives — a miss token costs 50 times a hit token — and the lever it points at is the block.

**A probe cannot price a workload.** 349 sent the same 191-token body twice and read `prompt_cache_hit_tokens: 0` on
both models, and on that evidence this register closed the 75 % saving as never available at any price. The workload
says otherwise: run `45595943761` recorded **6 204 649 of 7 636 769 prompt tokens as cache hits, 81.25 %** — **5 842
hit against 1 349 miss a call** across 1 062 calls — because an agent repeats a ~5 800-token system prompt and not a
~1 350-token telemetry block. What 349 established is narrower than it was published as: **a short prompt does not
cache**. It has no stable prefix to hit.

**The card has two columns and the old table was the dearer one.** Off-peak **1 / 4 / 0.02**, peak **2 / 8 / 0.04**,
peak exactly double, weekdays 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC. So the 2 / 8 every artifact in this tree was priced with
is a real tariff — the *peak* one — and 349's "1.87x over-statement" was the USD card converted at 7.13 rather than the
CNY card read. The acceptance run cost **1.69 CNY, 0.00119 a case**, against 7.77 with no cache and 15.55 at peak.

**The lever flips.** Cache-miss input is now **84.6 %** of the bill, output 8.1 %, the cached system prompt 7.3 % — so
shortening the **transcript** (1 349 uncached tokens a call) is worth fifty times per token what shortening the system
prompt is, and that reverses every prompt-length recommendation in this register. Full record: `cache-hit-352.md`.

**A negative result worth its own line.** Because the shipped arm runs `--fallback engine`, `priorTop` equals
`engineWinner` on all 1 422 cases, so a floor that settles on `priorTop ?? engine.top1` collapses to the engine arm's
**81.29 %**. A two-signal floor is not measurable on an arm where the prior IS the engine's ranking; it needs a
`--fallback seed` arm that no artifact here holds.

### 353 The bill the runner printed was not the bill (iteration 353)

**One sentence, two arithmetics.** Every run of the free-investigation arm ends with `tokens P+C · est. ¥X at the
declared prices`, and `X` was `P x 2 + C x 8` — the peak column, with every prompt token billed as a cache **miss**.
Run `45595943761` cost **1.69** and its own last line said **15.55**: a **9.2x** overstatement in the line most readers
see before any table, three lines above an audit block that had the right number. `costOf` had priced the cache
correctly since 352; the constant and the function never met.

**Fixed by deleting the constant.** `billLine` composes the sentence from `costOf` — the function `auditCost` prices
its strata and its total with — so the printed figure and the table can only disagree if the line stops being called.
`billNote` prints the counterfactual (*with every prompt at the miss price the same run would read ¥7.77*) because
that is what every earlier report carried, and a silent correction is what makes a series untrustworthy.
`QueryArmSummary.cacheHitTokens` carries the column, clamped per row and `null` — not zero — when no row declared it,
because the runner could not price a cache whose count it never received.

**The tier is a clock, not a default.** `tariffAt` / `servedRatesAt` read `[01:00, 04:00)` and `[06:00, 10:00)` UTC on
weekdays — half-open, so no instant is billed at both — and apply them to the artifact's own `startedAt`. A repricing
months later lands on the column the run was billed under, not on the clock of whoever reads it; a constant is exactly
what produced 15.55 for a 1.69 run. `PRICES` is gone from `run-query-agent.ts`, and so is the phrase that named it.

**And one floor stops printing twice.** `distinctFloors` dedupes at the printed resolution (`5e-4`), so the cliff
`0.8629602…` and a requested `0.863` are one row: a table that lists one floor as two readings invites the conclusion
that the curve steps there. What this does not fix is stated in the same place: the windows are transcribed from the
card rather than queried, the line prices an artifact rather than a case, and the transcript lever — 84.6 % of the
bill — is still unpriced. Full record: `bill-line-353.md`.

### 354 The knob that priced the transcript reached nothing, and the cheap tokens were the ones it removed (iteration 354)

**The flag was inert on every run this tree ever dispatched.** `--transcript-chars` travelled from the workflow through
the runner into `trace`, and two lines later `TRACE_CHARS = 2 000` overwrote it; `buildUserPrompt` called
`renderTranscript(exchanges)` with **no budget at all**, so every prompt was rendered at the default 9 000 characters.
The wall was never reached — the corpus's own final trace is ~1 700 characters — so no artifact could have caught it.
This is the third iteration running of one defect class: 351 priced one rule and executed another, 353 printed one
arithmetic and computed another, 354 moved a lever that was not connected. Fixed by passing the budget through, and by
a red test that asks a 120-character cap to say `elided` **inside the prompt**.

**Three arms on the full corpus, differing only in the cap.** At 1 200 and 600 characters against the anchor
`45595943761`: accuracy **−9**, **−19** and (alone, on `b9ba1df`) **−13** cases — −0.63 / −1.34 / −0.91 pp — with paired
discordants **+6/−15**, **+5/−24** and **+6/−19**. The acceptance test is the trajectory, because accuracy is a sum over
1 422 cases and a cap that repairs one and breaks another is indistinguishable from a cap that changed nothing
(`CoACT`, `arXiv:2607.02911`): **54.50 %, 46.13 % and 46.34 %** of cases made the same directives in the same order. The
tool census says what changed: `TOOL logs` **794 → 40 → 34** (−95 / −96 %), `TOOL failed` 1 078 → 1 653 → 1 651,
`TOOL edges` 1 160 → 1 569 → 1 509. An arm that cannot re-read what it found stops asking for long lists and starts
asking for verdicts.

**The cap removed 38.3 % of the tokens and 11.8 % of the money, and two thirds of the money came from somewhere it did
not act.** Run alone the 600-character arm costs **1.493 against 1.693**. It fell because the arm **changed tools**: a
list of verdicts is a shorter observation than a dump of log lines, so the full-price column fell 9.4 % (225.0 → 203.5
tokens a call) and that term is **67 %** of the saving — against **28 %** from the cache and 5 % from shorter answers.
The cache column is the one that costs: **hits per call halve, 974.7 → 535.8**, and both caps land on the same figure
although they differ by 44 tokens a call, so elision removes one stable block rather than a slope — the region the
endpoint had been serving at 1/50th the miss price. Destroying 45 % of the cache-served tokens bought 0.056 CNY.

**The first reading of that money was wrong, and the third dispatch is why.** The two capped arms ran concurrently on
one key while the anchor ran alone, and the concurrent 600 arm read **1.70** — "no money". Alone it reads 1.49. The
decomposition is exact: the **window** removes 438.9 cache-served tokens a call that vanish (2.79 M, costing nothing to
lose); the **contention** moves 34.8 a call from the hit column into the miss column (0.22 M, **+0.22 CNY**); and the
two nearly cancelled inside the concurrent artifact. The dichotomy this iteration first wrote down — "contention, or
the window" — was false, because it assumed the bill follows the cache.

**The bill, to the token.** The capped artifact's per-call curve puts the **opening at 543.8 tokens**: the first call
carries no transcript, so that point is the standing instruction plus the head and nothing a cap can reach, and
543.8 × 6 372 calls is **3.47 M** of the 4.70 M the arm spent. The rest is the **newest observation on each call** —
225 tokens at full price × 6 366 calls = **¥1.432, 84.6 %** of the anchor's bill, against ¥0.124 for the 6.2 M tokens of
accumulated history (7.3 %) and ¥0.137 of output (8.1 %). The history is not what the run pays for, which is what
reverses 352's "shorten the transcript" recommendation rather than confirming it.

**What this closes and what it opens.** The front-eliding family is closed as a lever over the history — 45 % of the
cache-served tokens for 0.056 CNY is a bad trade — and not closed as evidence about cost, because the saving it did
produce came through the one channel it did not intend: the size of the observation. That channel now has an
instrument, `--result-chars`, which truncates a result as it **enters** the transcript, keeps every byte already read
and leaves the prefix alone: at 100 tokens a block instead of ~200 the bill reads **¥1.06, −37 %** against the anchor's
other two columns, judged by the same free test (trajectories preserved per case). Two columns were added to make that
dispatch readable rather than inferred: `turnTokens` (one prompt count per call, which located the 543.8-token
opening) and `turnHitTokens` (the cached share of each call, so the next arm states which call lost its cache instead
of deriving it from a case total).

**What this does not establish.** Contention is measured (0.22 M tokens, **¥0.22**) but not paired: the alone arm ran
23 minutes later and on a different revision (`b9ba1df`, the bill-line fix rather than an arm change), so the sign of
the decomposition is not in doubt and its standard error is. And **501–536 cache-served tokens a call is 92–99 % of the
543.8-token opening**, which a strict byte-prefix cache could not serve — the budget line changes every turn and sits in
the third line of the head — so the endpoint caches more generously than a prefix match, or counts hits differently
than its documentation implies. Every figure above prices the reported counts, which is what an invoice charges, and
none assumes the mechanism. Full record: `docs/transcript-lever-354.md`.

### 355 The entry gate is refused, and the refusal is what the iteration found

The `entry-prior` rule renames 75 answers and is **70 right and 5 wrong**. This iteration tried to gate the five out,
on one artifact, at zero cost, and every gate failed for a different and instructive reason.

**The margin gate cannot work, and the reason is two thousandths.** The highest-margin REPAIR sits at **0.569** and the
highest-margin BREAK at **0.571** — two cases on opposite sides of the outcome, separated by a quantity smaller than
any rounding of the corpus. A `<= 0.5` bar keeps 66 repairs and 4 breaks, a net **+62** against the ungated **+65**;
`priorSurprise <= 100` reads **+35**. No threshold separates a population from itself, and the phrase "the
distributions overlap" now has its witness: the overlap is two cases deep at the very top of the range.

**The `engineRank` gate works and is ILLEGAL.** `engineRank != 1` keeps 69 repairs and 2 breaks, a net **+67**, and it
is a rule about the LABEL: `engineRank` is `truthRank`, the truth's own position in the engine's order. A resolver
reading it scores itself with the answer key. Recorded because it is the most tempting gate in the artifact — it is a
single comparison, it reads like "respect the engine's confidence", and it is worth +2.

**The `faultType` gate works, reproduces on four arms, survives cross-validation, and is still refused.** A bandwidth or
delay fault raises no error, so the entry rule's premise ("no failure crossed the door", read from the error channel)
is vacuously true exactly where the rule is wrong. Excluding `NetworkBandwidth` and `NetworkDelay` is worth **+3 cases
on all four artifacts** (1 327 → 1 330, 1 318 → 1 321, 1 308 → 1 311, 1 314 → 1 317), and 5-fold cross-validation by
`(hash(family) + index-in-family) mod 2` returns **+3 on held-out folds** — identical to in-sample, which is the
signature of a real constraint rather than a fitted one. **It is refused anyway, on protocol grounds:** `faultType`
lives in `case.json` beside `groundTruthServices`, the harness gives the arm telemetry and nothing else, no prompt
carries it, and `buildTelemetry` never reads it. The +3 would be bought with a field the benchmark reserves, and the
comparison would not survive review. **This is the first measured positive in this programme rejected for a reason
that is not about the measurement**, and it is written here so the next iteration does not rediscover it and ship it.

**The legal version already exists and already ships disabled.** A departure-channel gate (`conduitUnder`,
`ENTRY_PRIOR_TRAFFIC_KAPPA = null`) asks the observable form of the same question, and its pricing read a peak at one
grid point on one corpus — the shape this programme has refused twice. The axis stays closed on its own record, not on
this one.

**What is left of the five breaks: nothing reachable.** They are one `HTTPRequestDelay` at margin 0.355 and four
network faults, their common signature is an error channel that stayed flat, and the only legal way to read that
signature is the channel gate that is already refused. **The rule ships as it is, at 93.3 % precision on the population
it addresses, and the 5 breaks are its price.**

### 356 The trace channel is worth 15.5 points and none of it is topology (iteration 356)

`arXiv:2603.02057` says **"trace-based methods largely fail"** on a GPU-driven LLM inference deployment, and this
engine's largest single FSE'26 gain is `failedTraceEdges`, so the sentence has stood in the record since 355 as a
warning about a channel. Read at source this iteration, both halves of the premise changed.

**The paper is a finding over two implementations.** Its abstract says *"Across 24 methods (20 metric-based, two
trace-based, and two multi-source)"*. So the failure is 2 of 2 trace METHODS, not a property of trace DATA, and it
cannot separate "traces do not carry root cause on an inference stack" from "these two trace methods were built for a
request-path topology". The paper motivated the census; it could not supply the number.

**The number, measured on 1 422 cases at zero model calls, control asserted at the published 1 186 (83.40 %):**

| arm | hits | Δ | lost | gained |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `baseline` | 1 186 | — | 0 | 0 |
| `call-graph-edges` (`traceEdges: []`) | **1 186** | **+0.0 pp** | **0** | **0** |
| `failed-edges` (`failedTraceEdges: []`) | 1 031 | **−10.9 pp** | 155 | 0 |
| `edge-latency` (`traceEdgeLatency: []`) | 1 114 | −5.1 pp | 74 | 2 |
| `all-trace` | 966 | **−15.5 pp** | 222 | 2 |

**The zero is the finding, and it is a claim about what kind of method this is.** Removing every observed
`[caller, callee]` pair the bridge recorded changes **not one case in 1 422**, on any fault type. The call graph is
`buildFSE26StaticEdges` — the **static topology** — and the trace-derived edges are pure redundancy on top of it.
**This engine does not discover topology from traces; it asserts it, and uses traces to measure per-edge failure and
per-edge latency.** So the paper's finding cannot reach this engine through a topology channel, because there is no
topology channel to fail; it can only reach it through the two measurement channels, and those cost 10.9 pp and
5.1 pp.

**The two measurement channels own disjoint fault families, which the loader's docblock asserted and nothing had
measured.** `failed-edges` loses 74 of its 155 on the four network fault types (233 cases: `NetworkPartition` 29,
`NetworkBandwidth` 18, `NetworkLoss` 14, `NetworkCorrupt` 13): a network fault makes a call fail or never complete,
and the per-edge failure record is the only input that says *which* edge stopped carrying traffic — the containment
order reads the same channel, so it loses both at once. `edge-latency` is the continuous counterpart and loses where
nothing fails and everything slows: `NetworkDelay` 9 of 20, `JVMLatency` 3 of 6, both **42.9 %**. 155 + 74 = 229
against a composite loss of 222, so the two overlap on only **seven cases**.

**And 294 cases never needed a trace at all**: `JVMMemoryStress` 171/171, `ContainerKill` 89/89, `PodFailure` 24/24,
`PodKill` 10/10 — every one at **100 %** and **zero loss** under full ablation. Crash and saturation faults are solved
from metrics alone, and they are the fault families closest to a GPU inference stack's own failure modes.

**What the axis does not close.** The zero is conditional on the static topology being correct, and this corpus cannot
create the alternative: with a right prior, observed edges add nothing, and on an unknown topology there is no prior
to be redundant with. **So the defensible claim is narrower than "this engine does not need traces" — it is that this
engine's topology is a PRIOR rather than a MEASUREMENT, which is exactly the assumption an inference stack would
break, and what that would cost is the one quantity here that remains unpriced.**

Fenced as the ablation it is: the channel → field mapping is a `Record` over the union so a fourth channel cannot be
silently unablatable; the control is asserted against the published cell and the run REFUSES on disagreement rather
than printing a table about another configuration; and the label — accepted set, fault type, metrics, logs, injection
time — is copied through every strip, because a gain bought by narrowing the answer set is the `engineRank` defect.

### 357 `--result-chars 600` keeps every answer and costs 89 % more (iteration 357)

The axis this iteration's plan called P0 was the entry-side cut: shorten the tool result, project ¥1.06 (−37 %),
keep the trajectories. It ran — `45695839124`, 1 422 cases, 23 min 41 s of model time, success — and it is
**refused, because it is not cheaper.**

| | anchor `45595943761` | arm `45695839124` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| agent Top@1 | **1 327** | **1 327** |
| prompt tokens | 7 636 769 | 6 232 574 (−18.4 %) |
| cache hits | 6 204 875 (81.25 %) | 3 238 016 (51.95 %) |
| **uncached prompt** | **1 431 894** | **2 994 558 (+109.1 %)** |
| **bill, off-peak `1 / 4 / hit 0.02`** | **¥1.69** | **¥3.20 (+88.8 %)** |
| per case | ¥0.00119 | ¥0.00225 |

**The accuracy test passed and the ledger failed.** Not one case moved, so the cut really did delete observation
text and nothing else. But a cache hit is **50×** cheaper than a miss on this card, and the cut removed 1.40 M
prompt tokens while destroying 2.97 M tokens of cache hits:

```
cache hits lost   2.9669 M × ¥0.02 = +¥0.0593
misses added      1.5627 M × ¥1.00 = +¥1.5627      net +¥1.5034  →  ¥1.69 → ¥3.20
```

**The projection was wrong about the mechanism, not only the magnitude.** `result_chars` was modelled as an
entry-side cut that leaves the cached prefix alone. It is not: each turn's RESULT becomes part of the NEXT turn's
prefix, so shortening results shortens the cacheable region for every subsequent round. The plan's own kill
criterion said `cacheHitTokens` per call must stay near 975; measured, it **halved to 508** from ~1 170.

**This is the fourth lever in five iterations that priced the token it saved and not the structure it broke** (§351
a rule the arm did not run, §353 a bill nobody computed, §354 a knob that reached nothing, §355 a table describing a
standing it no longer had). The new part is that the bill was read on the real card instead of projected from a
token count.

The shipped cost row is unchanged at **¥0.00119 a case** — the anchor's, on the off-peak card with 81.25 % cache —
and `result_chars` keeps its shipped value. What the refusal leaves behind is a named quantity: the cache share has
two observed states, **81 % uncut and 52 % cut**, and any future entry-side cut must predict its effect on
`turnHitTokens` before it is dispatched rather than after.

| the note block under the table | "superseded by **`1156/1422 = 81.29%`** … (§0p-ix, register §314)" | stops at `1073/1422 = 75.46%` | code |

either way**, 4 118 lines. The two files now differ in exactly one cell, a cross-repo path that is local here and

**And the fence broke first, on its own subject's whitespace.** `standing-anchor.test.ts` located the five tables it
reads by padded header literals — `'| evaluation                              | metric'` — which is one formatter's output

The repair is header-**cell** identity, with a regression test that shows the predicate is invariant under padding

### 363 The neighbour channel is refused in BOTH signs, and a graph defect that cost exactly nothing (iteration 363)

§362 ended on a characterisation it could not act on: **50.0 % of the 76 misses lead with a graph neighbour of the
truth**, in-degree does not separate them, and "aggregators lose" is therefore not the mechanism. This iteration
prices that sentence as an arm, and the answer is a refusal at both ends of the sign — plus a defect in the runner
that had been scoring the corpus on the wrong graph.

**The operator, with its three load-bearing choices stated.** For a case whose engine ranking is `r₁ … rₙ` with
scores `sᵢ`, let `xᵢ` be the within-case min–max image of `sᵢ` in `[0, 1]` and `N(i)` the case's call-graph
neighbours:

> `xᵢ′ = (1 − α)·xᵢ + α·mean_{j ∈ N(i)} xⱼ`

- **`mean`, not `sum`.** The kinetic collision term is a sum over partners, and the transliteration is wrong here:
  a sum pays a node for its DEGREE, and §362 already measured that in-degree does not separate the misses
  (`≥ 3`: 0.571, `< 3`: 0.504). `mean` is the expected value over partners — one collision, not degree many.
- **Undirected.** §362's 50.0 % was measured on undirected adjacency, so the arm has to test THAT sentence.
- **A partner the ranking does not contain contributes nothing.** Zero is a measurement; absence is not, and a mean
  of one measurement and two absences is not a third of a measurement.

`α = 0` is the engine bit for bit and `α = 1` is the **neighbour-only baseline**, so both ends of the axis are arms
rather than annotations. The runner asserts the identity before printing a table: every case's `α = 0` ordering
equals the engine's, its record equals the runner's `correct`/`truthRank` field for field, and the `α = 0` row
equals the published cells. A probe that disagreed there could not report a gain anywhere else.

**The share is above the null — which makes the refusal sharper, not weaker.** A neighbour-led miss is a
Poisson-binomial variate, not a binomial one, because each miss carries its own probability: the truth's share of its
own graph. On the 76 misses:

| reading | count | rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| observed neighbour-led misses | **38** | 0.5000 |
| null: a uniformly random wrong winner over the same graphs | **22.21** | 0.2923 |
| exact two-sided Poisson-binomial p | | **0.0001** |

So the engine's errors are shifted toward the truth's adjacency by 1.7× the graph's own base rate. **The signal is
real and it is still not exploitable by this operator**, and the reason is the next table.

**The misses are symmetric in direction, so no single sign can serve them.** Of the 76: **19 downstream** (top-1 is
a callee of the truth — the engine blamed a symptom), **19 upstream** (top-1 calls the truth — it blamed a consumer),
**0 reciprocal**, **38 unrelated**. The two directional populations have opposite repairs and are the same size, so
a signed rule has to be right per case; a global sign is guaranteed to be wrong on half of them.

**The pre-registered sweep, on the same 156 cases at CNY 0.00:**

| `α` | `boutique/codedefect` | `boutique/performance` | `trainticket/performance` | all | gained | lost | p |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **0** | **0.3636** | **0.8095** | **0.6596** | **0.5128** | — | — | — |
| 0.05 | 0.3636 | 0.8095 | 0.5319 | 0.4744 | 0 | 6 | 0.0313 |
| 0.10 | 0.3636 | 0.7619 | 0.4255 | 0.4359 | 0 | 12 | 0.0005 |
| 0.20 | 0.3636 | 0.7619 | 0.3830 | 0.4231 | 0 | 14 | 0.0001 |
| 0.30 | 0.3864 | 0.8095 | 0.3404 | 0.4295 | 4 | 17 | 0.0072 |
| 0.50 | 0.1932 | 0.7143 | 0.1915 | 0.2628 | 3 | 42 | 0.0000 |
| 1.00 | 0.0455 | 0.1905 | 0.0213 | **0.0577** | 5 | 76 | 0.0000 |

The neighbour-only baseline is **0.0577**, i.e. a hair above the 5.5 % a random order would score on these pools
(§362's 15–51 candidates). So the strongest possible reading of "the ordering is propagation" is worth less than the
